jobs.title: Field Application Engineer- Aerospace & Defense
jobs.description:
About Us
At Emerson Test & Measurement Business Group (Formerly known as National Instruments), we empower engineers and innovators to solve the world’s toughest engineering challenges through automated test and measurement solutions. Our platforms are widely used across Aerospace & Defense, Semiconductor, Automotive, Communications, and Industrial markets to accelerate innovation and improve engineering productivity.
We are looking for a highly motivated and technically strong Field Applications Engineer (FAE) to support and grow our Aerospace & Defense business in India.
Role Overview
The Field Applications Engineer (FAE) will play a critical role in driving technical engagement with Aerospace & Defense customers by understanding customer challenges, architecting solutions, supporting evaluations, and enabling successful deployment of automated test and validation systems.
This role requires strong technical depth, customer-facing capability, and the ability to work closely with sales teams, system integrators, partners, and customer engineering organizations. The ideal candidate is passionate about solving complex engineering problems and translating technology into measurable customer outcomes.
In This Role, Your Responsibilities Will Be:
Engage with Aerospace & Defense customers to understand technical requirements and system-level challenges
Architect and demonstrate solutions for applications involving RF & microwave, radar, electronic warfare, avionics, communications, embedded systems, HIL, and automated validation
Support pre-sales technical activities including customer presentations, solution demonstrations, workshops, benchmarking, and proof-of-concepts
Work closely with Account Managers to drive technical wins and accelerate business growth
Collaborate with System Integrators and ecosystem partners to support scalable deployment models
Design and recommend architectures using modular instrumentation, PXI platforms, automated test software, and validation frameworks
Provide technical consultation on system integration, automation strategies, and test methodologies
Support customer onboarding, implementation guidance, and technical issue resolution
Work cross-functionally with R&D, product teams, services, and global application engineering teams
Track emerging Aerospace & Defense technology trends and customer requirements to influence future solution strategies
Who You Are:
You are a proactive, strategic problem solver who establishes last relationships and delivers exceptional results. You’re comfortable managing complex accounts and driving account growth at both tactical and strategic levels.
For This Role, You Will Need:
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering is mandatory (Electronics, Electrical, ECE, Instrumentation, Aerospace, or related disciplines preferred)
6–10 years of experience in application engineering, systems engineering, validation, or technical consulting within Aerospace & Defense or related industries
Strong technical understanding of automated test and validation systems
Experience with RF test, radar systems, avionics, embedded systems, communications, or HIL environments
Ability to understand and architect complex system-level solutions
Strong customer-facing communication and presentation skills
Ability to work collaboratively with sales teams, customers, and partners
Willingness to travel based on project and customer requirements
Strong problem-solving mindset with technical curiosity
Ability to engage deeply with customer engineering teams
Passion for solving real-world engineering challenges
Strong ownership and execution orientation

jobs.description:
Our Purpose

Title and Summary
AI Principal Architect
Mastercard's Business & Market Insights (B&MI) group empowers organizations to achieve growth and innovation goals by delivering unparalleled data-driven intelligence and cutting-edge AI solutions. By harnessing proprietary data, frontier generative AI, and global expertise, B&MI helps businesses make smarter, faster, and more impactful decisions. We transform complex, multi-modal data into agentic systems and generative applications that drive measurable business outcomes and sustained competitive advantage.
We're looking for a Principal Architect, Generative AI & ML Engineering, for the Operational Intelligence Program within B&MI. As a principal-level technical leader, you'll define the architecture vision and technical strategy for our agentic AI platform. On this platform, agents make extensive tool calls into enterprise services and APIs and must run securely, reliably, and at scale. You'll set the standards teams build on across tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, self-correcting agents, memory, retrieval, and LLMOps. You'll also make the key decisions on models, platforms, and trade-offs. Working closely with engineering, product, security, and business leaders, you'll shape the long-term direction of Gen AI across B&MI and mentor architects and senior engineers. You'll also stay hands-on with prototypes that de-risk big bets. The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale. If you've solved them as a backend or distributed systems architect and have started applying that experience to LLM systems, we'd love to hear from you.
Roles & Responsibilities
• Own the architecture and technical roadmap for the Operational Intelligence Gen AI platform, defining reference architectures and standards that teams across the program can reuse and scale.
• Architect the enterprise tool-calling layer, setting standards for how internal services, data platforms, and external APIs are exposed to agents as tools. This covers schemas, contracts, versioning, access control, and resilient execution (parallel and chained calls, retries, timeouts, idempotency, circuit breakers, and fallbacks).
• Set the architecture for multi-agent and skills-based agent systems (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen), including when to use agents versus deterministic workflows and how agents coordinate, delegate, and share context.
• Design self-correcting agent patterns: tool critics and verifiers that check tool selection, arguments, and results, plus reflection and plan-and-execute loops that catch errors before agents act or respond.
• Architect agent memory and state for long-running, multi-step sessions, including short- and long-term memory (e.g., Mem0, Zep, LangGraph memory), session persistence, and memory scoping and retention.
• Define retrieval architecture for grounded reasoning, including Self-RAG, Corrective RAG (CRAG), adaptive retrieval, and Graph-RAG, built on vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, pgvector, OpenSearch) and knowledge graphs (e.g., Neo4j, AWS Neptune).
• Design the inference and orchestration layer for high throughput, covering async processing, streaming, caching, rate limiting, and model routing across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and open-source models.
• Establish the LLMOps architecture on Databricks (AWS), including MLflow, CI/CD for prompts and agents, and model lineage. Set platform-wide evaluation and observability standards: end-to-end tracing of tool calls, tool-selection accuracy, task success rates, cost, and latency.
• Build security and Responsible AI into the architecture, including guardrails, prompt-injection defenses, hallucination mitigation, data privacy, and audit trails that meet Mastercard's data ethics and regulatory standards.
• Own key architecture decisions and trade-offs, such as build versus buy, model and vendor selection, and cost versus latency versus accuracy, documented through architecture decision records. Assess emerging models, frameworks, and standards such as MCP for production readiness.
• Lead design reviews and partner with engineering, product, security, and data teams to align on architecture and raise the engineering bar across the program.
• Stay hands-on, building prototypes and reference implementations that de-risk decisions and give teams a working starting point.
All About You
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, AI/ML, or Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
• Significant experience architecting large-scale distributed systems in production, including microservices, event-driven systems, data platforms, and cloud-native infrastructure.
• Deep expertise in API design and systems integration, including contracts, security models, and reliability patterns for services consumed by many teams. You understand what changes when the consumer is an LLM.
• Hands-on experience designing and shipping LLM-powered systems in production, especially agents that use tool/function calling, memory, and retrieval, and a clear view of how they fail.
• Strong Python skills for hands-on prototyping (async programming, FastAPI or similar), plus SQL proficiency.
• Deep experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS preferred; Azure or GCP welcome), including its AI services such as Bedrock, SageMaker, Azure OpenAI, or Vertex AI.
• A solid grounding in security, privacy, and compliance for enterprise systems, ideally in financial services or another regulated industry.
• The ability to influence without authority, aligning engineering, product, and leadership around a technical direction and explaining trade-offs in business terms.
• Nice to have: hands-on experience with tool critics, Self-RAG, CRAG, reflection loops, memory frameworks such as Mem0 or Zep, MCP tool servers, or agent evaluation frameworks.
• Nice to have: exposure to fine-tuning (LoRA, PEFT, RLHF), multimodal models, or knowledge graphs.
• Coming from backend or distributed systems architecture? The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale, and you've solved them before. If you've started applying that experience to LLM systems, we want to hear from you, even if you haven't used every tool listed here.
Corporate Security Responsibility
All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

jobs.title: IP RTL Senior Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
The Role and Impact:
As an IP Logic Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in developing high-quality intellectual property (IP) for Unified Intel Chassis designs. This position is at the forefront of Intel's innovation, ensuring that our products consistently deliver world-class performance, power efficiency, and reliability. Work closely with architects to define and design complex protocol bridges. Define and implement range-based access control for secured memory and register paths across HBW and LBW. Own privilege qualification and policy propagation across AXI-Lite, APB, IOSF-SB, and HBW request paths. Design and validate parity/ECC generation and checking for request, response, and data channels. Define fault behavior for unauthorized accesses and corrupt transactions, including silent block semantics, RAZWI-style handling, poison propagation, and timeout cleanup. Build or integrate logging, interrupt, and firmware-visible error harvesting flows for local and global RAS handling. Support error injection, diagnostics, and post-silicon debug hooks for both security and reliability validation. Define and implement telemetry capture for fabric load, latency, congestion, error context, and other operational health indicators. Own debug and trace data paths for wrapper-level and fabric-level observability, including data capture, transport, formatting, and handoff to downstream debug infrastructure. Design counters, sticky status, snapshots, and firmware-visible CSRs that make performance and failure analysis practical. Integrate trigger, monitor, and logging hooks needed for bring-up, stress triage, and post-silicon correlation. Work with architecture, validation, firmware, and post-silicon teams to ensure telemetry and debug signals are useful, stable, and diagnosable. Balance observability depth against area, timing, bandwidth, and survivability constraints. Support root-cause analysis of bandwidth loss, latency outliers, protocol stalls, and intermittent field or lab issues using hardware observability features.
Key Responsibilities:
Develop logic designs, register transfer level (RTL) coding, and simulations required for IP blocks, functional units, and subsystems.
Define architecture and microarchitecture features for the IP block being designed.
Apply strategies, tools, and methods to optimize RTL design for power, performance, area, and timing targets.
Strong knowledge of AXI, AXI-Lite, APB, parity/ECC schemes, and transaction error handling.
Experience with secure MMIO, access-control/firewall logic, or privilege-based filtering.
Experience with RAS concepts such as fault containment, poison, interrupt generation, logging, and recovery-oriented design.
Support SoC customers with seamless integration and verification of IP blocks.
Telemetry and debug are both observability functions rather than primary Datapath functions.
Drive compliance with quality assurance standards to enable smooth IP handoff within the SoC development process.

Knowledge of IP block integration workflows within SoC designs.

Job Description:
Performs physical design implementation of CPU designs from RTL to GDS to create a design database that is ready for manufacturing. Conducts all aspects of the CPU physical design flow including synthesis, place and route, clock tree synthesis, floor planning, static timing analysis, power/clock distribution, reliability, and power and noise analysis. Conducts verification and signoff including formal equivalence verification, static timing analysis, reliability verification, static and dynamic power integrity, layout verification, electrical rule checking, and structural design checking. Analyzes results and makes recommendations to improve current and future CPU microarchitectures closely collaborating with logic, circuit, architecture, and design automation teams. Possesses CPUspecific expertise in various aspects of structural and physical design, including physical clock design, timing closure, coverage analysis, multiple power domain analysis, structured placement, routing, synthesis, and DFT. Works intimately with industry EDA vendors to build and enhance tool capabilities to design a highspeed, lowpower synthesizable CPU. Optimizes CPU design to improve product level parameters such as power, frequency, and area. Participates in the development and improvement of physical design methodologies and flow automation.
Qualifications:
As a CPU Physical Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in implementing high-performance, low-power CPU designs from RTL to GDSII. You will focus on detailed processes such as synthesis, placement, routing, timing analysis, and power optimization, enabling designs that meet stringent performance and efficiency targets. Your work will directly influence the success of Intel's next-generation CPUs and their manufacturing readiness, contributing to innovative advancements in computing technology.
You will join a dynamic team dedicated to designing Intel's latest high-performance CPUs using cutting-edge technologies. As CPU Circuit Design Lead, you will lead the development of advanced digital circuits for custom blocks such as SRAM, register files, memory compilers, Custom Data path, and caches. Oracle is seeking an engineering director to build and lead a new Systems Firmware team in Bengaluru. You will hire the founding engineers, establish the team’s technical direction and culture, and take responsibility for outcomes that directly affect the reliability and serviceability of our server fleet.
The team’s initial mission is to resolve BMC and BIOS firmware issues in production. Working closely with US engineering teams, infrastructure operations, hardware teams, and external partners, you will lead complex investigations, drive lasting fixes, and improve the diagnostics, testing, and release practices that prevent problems from recurring. The team will participate in on-call rotations during India daytime hours, complementing US coverage through coordinated response and clear technical handoffs.
You will start with four senior engineers and provide close technical leadership while building the practices and partnerships needed for the team to succeed. You will set priorities, develop your engineers, and balance immediate fleet needs with longer-term improvements in firmware quality, security, and operational efficiency.
You will also shape the team’s roadmap and future capability. This includes working with original design manufacturers and joint design manufacturers (ODM/JDMs), particularly Taiwan-based partners, on platform requirements, firmware integration, bring-up, validation, and production readiness.
This role calls for a leader with deep systems firmware expertise, sound operational judgment, and a record of building strong engineering teams. You should be comfortable guiding difficult technical investigations, holding partners accountable for delivery, and translating lessons from production into better engineering decisions.
Key Responsibilities
Build and lead the Bangalore Systems Firmware team. Recruit, develop, and retain exceptional engineers working on BMC firmware and BIOS. Establish clear ownership, coach technical leaders, and create an inclusive culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Own firmware operational support during India daytime hours. Establish sustainable on-call rotations and effective handoffs with US teams to provide continuity of support for Oracle’s server and GPU fleet.
Lead resolution of complex firmware issues. Guide incident triage, troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions across firmware, hardware, and software boundaries. Prioritize work by customer impact and ensure timely resolution and clear stakeholder communication.

Establish engineering and operational standards. Define and evolve runbooks, escalation processes, maintenance procedures, and firmware validation and deployment practices that improve fleet availability, health, security, and reliability.

jobs.title: Principal Systems Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Firmware connects hardware capability to cloud reliability. At OCI, you will work where those layers meet—investigating challenging failures, developing lasting fixes, and improving how firmware is tested, deployed, and operated across our infrastructure.
As a Principal Systems Firmware Engineer, you will design, develop, and improve BMC firmware or BIOS/UEFI and the tools that support its deployment across OCI’s server and GPU infrastructure. You will own complex engineering problems across firmware, hardware, and operating systems, delivering changes that improve platform reliability, diagnosability, security, and recovery.
Your initial focus will be engineering improvements for platforms already operating in our fleet. You will use production findings to identify design weaknesses, develop and validate firmware fixes, extend automated testing, and eliminate recurring failure modes. Success means delivering durable improvements that reduce failures and the need for manual intervention.
You will also participate in an India daytime on-call rotation, complementing US engineering teams. This responsibility connects your engineering work directly to how platforms behave in production and includes incident investigation, mitigation, and coordinated handoffs.
As the team grows, its scope is expected to expand into new server and GPU platform development, with opportunities to work alongside silicon suppliers and ODM/JDM partners on firmware integration, platform bring-up, and validation.
This role offers the opportunity to help shape a new team’s engineering practices while remaining deeply involved in design, code, and complex technical investigations.
Key Responsibilities
Own firmware development and integration. Design, develop, debug, and maintain BMC or BIOS/UEFI components and supporting systems software. Define clear interfaces across firmware, hardware, operating systems, and fleet management services.
Resolve complex fleet issues. Lead investigations into boot failures, management controller faults, firmware update problems, hardware initialization failures, and other platform reliability issues. Develop mitigations, establish root cause, and deliver durable fixes.
Provide operational support. Participate in the India daytime on-call rotation, coordinate investigations and handoffs with US teams, and communicate impact, progress, and resolution clearly.
Build automation and preventive controls. Develop tools for firmware provisioning, updates, diagnostics, recovery, and validation. Improve telemetry, logging, and failure analysis to reduce recurring incidents and manual intervention.
Drive software quality and security. Write maintainable code, lead design and code reviews, and develop functional, regression, negative, and recovery tests. Apply secure development practices and support firmware vulnerability remediation.
Contribute to platform bring-up. Diagnose interactions across firmware, hardware, bootloaders, and operating systems. Use platform logs and appropriate hardware debugging tools to isolate faults and validate end-to-end behavior.
Collaborate with engineering and vendor partners. Work with hardware, silicon, operating system, validation, and fleet operations teams. As product development scope grows, work with ODM/JDM partners on requirements, defect resolution, firmware releases, and platform readiness.
Provide technical leadership. Own delivery of complex engineering work, identify dependencies and risks, document designs and debugging methods, mentor engineers, and contribute to hiring and continuous improvement.
Required qualifications
Meet one of the following education and software development experience combinations:
11 years of software development experience; or
A bachelor’s degree/B.Tech in a relevant engineering, computing, information technology, mathematics, physics, or related field, with 7 years of software development experience; or
A master’s degree/M.Tech in one of these fields, with 5 years of software development experience; or
A doctorate in one of these fields, with 3 years of software development experience.
At least 6 years of experience using programming and scripting languages, with strong C/C++ skills and the ability to build diagnostic and automation tools.
Substantial hands-on development and debugging experience in BMC firmware or BIOS/UEFI, with the ability to investigate interactions across the broader server platform.
Strong understanding of server architecture, embedded systems, hardware/software interfaces, and Linux fundamentals.
Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex issues across firmware, hardware, and operating systems, using evidence to distinguish symptoms from root causes.
Experience owning software components through design, implementation, code review, testing, release, and ongoing support.
Experience developing automated tests, diagnostics, or operational tooling and improving reliability, observability, or performance.
Ability to lead technical investigations, mentor colleagues, and communicate effectively across engineering teams and external partners.
Willingness to participate in the India daytime on-call rotation.
Preferred qualifications
Experience with OpenBMC or other server BMC stacks, or with server BIOS/UEFI implementations such as EDK II or commercial firmware platforms.
Familiarity with relevant platform interfaces and protocols, such as Redfish, IPMI, PLDM/MCTP, SMBus/I²C, SPI, PCIe, or ACPI.
Experience with server or GPU platform bring-up, hardware initialization, power and thermal management, or reliability, availability, and serviceability (RAS) features.
Experience using JTAG, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers, or emulators, and interpreting schematics and board documentation.
Experience with secure boot, firmware signing, update and recovery mechanisms, or firmware security remediation.
Experience supporting production infrastructure at cloud or hyperscale environments, including controlled firmware rollouts and incident response.
Experience collaborating with silicon suppliers, BIOS/BMC vendors, or ODM/JDM engineering teams.

jobs.title: Principal Data Systems Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Build the next generation of Oracle Zero Data Loss Recovery Appliance (ZDLRA) software, helping fortune 500 enterprises protect and recover their business-critical Oracle databases. Work on software where data integrity, recoverability, cyber resilience, and performance at scale directly affect customers' most important operations.
Join our growing engineering team in Bengaluru and collaborate with experienced ZDLRA engineers in India and the US. You will contribute to shared product priorities, deliver new features and projects, and help evolve an enterprise data protection platform. This role offers the opportunity to help shape a new team while building deep product expertise within an established global engineering organization.
The work spans Oracle database kernel development and systems programming, primarily in C and PL/SQL on Linux. You will tackle engineering problems involving buffers and caches, memory management, storage, file systems, I/O, networking, concurrency, and distributed systems. Strong algorithms, thoughtful design, and an understanding of how these components interact will be central to delivering correct, efficient, and maintainable software.
You will participate throughout the development lifecycle: understanding problems, exploring the codebase, identifying root causes, designing solutions, implementing changes, writing tests, and validating results. The work combines new development and enhancements with complex defect resolution, including issues encountered in customer environments. As your product knowledge grows, you will take increasing technical ownership of assigned features and components, contributing to design decisions, code reviews, ongoing maintenance, and knowledge sharing.
We value engineers who investigate problems systematically, use documentation and diagnostic tools resourcefully, communicate clearly, and help colleagues succeed. You will use modern engineering tools, including LLMs and AI coding agents, to accelerate code exploration, development, and testing while applying independent judgment and rigorous validation to the resulting designs and code.
We welcome experienced developers with strong C, Linux, system programming skills and practical knowledge of database internals, storage, distributed systems, or other demanding enterprise software. Prior Oracle Database, RMAN, PL/SQL, or backup and recovery product experience is an advantage. Strong systems fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to translate complex requirements into reliable production software are essential.
This position is based in Bengaluru, India.
Product development and technical ownership
Design, implement, and maintain ZDLRA features and enhancements in C and PL/SQL on Linux, contributing to Oracle database kernel and systems software development.
Translate requirements and technical problems into clear designs, manageable tasks, and deliverable milestones. Evaluate alternatives and document trade-offs involving correctness, performance, scalability, compatibility, and maintainability.
Apply appropriate algorithms and data structures to build efficient, reliable software. Reason about memory use, concurrency, synchronization, and behavior under demanding workloads.
Develop and improve assigned components involving buffers, caches, storage, file systems, I/O, networking, and distributed processing, with careful attention to data integrity and recovery behavior.
Build product expertise through code exploration, technical documentation, collaboration, and delivery of fixes and enhancements. Progress toward ownership of assigned features and projects, including subsequent development, maintenance, and defect resolution.
Investigation, performance, and quality
Investigate complex defects, including issues reported from customer deployments. Reproduce failures, trace relevant code paths, establish root causes, and implement durable fixes.
Use GDB, core dumps, logs, traces, profiling tools, and Linux utilities to gather evidence and understand software behavior across interacting components.
Diagnose performance and scalability bottlenecks involving CPU, memory, storage, I/O, and networking. Establish useful measurements and validate the impact of changes against representative workloads.
Design and implement tests alongside production code. Cover functional behavior, boundary conditions, regressions, concurrency, and relevant failure and recovery scenarios using the team's engineering and test frameworks.
Use shell scripting and automation to improve diagnostic data collection, issue reproduction, testing, and other repeatable development tasks.
Follow secure coding practices and engineering standards. Evaluate error handling, resource management, backward compatibility, and versioning implications when modifying existing code or interfaces.
Engineering execution and collaboration
Take assigned work through the software development lifecycle, from analysis and design through implementation, review, testing, integration, and maintenance.
Plan work realistically, identify dependencies, and communicate progress, design decisions, risks, and blockers. Coordinate with the engineering team to deliver agreed project milestones.
Collaborate closely with ZDLRA engineers in India and the US and with relevant database engineering teams to resolve cross-component issues and deliver shared product objectives.
Participate in design and code reviews, providing constructive feedback on correctness, clarity, performance, security, test coverage, and long-term maintainability.
Write and maintain useful design notes, implementation documentation, and troubleshooting guidance. Share findings so that investigations and engineering decisions benefit the wider team.
Use internal documentation, specifications, and existing code resourcefully to understand unfamiliar areas. Ask focused questions, seek timely feedback, and help colleagues solve technical problems.
As product expertise grows, provide technical guidance, mentor colleagues, and contribute to improvements in the team's development practices and engineering quality.
AI-assisted engineering
Use LLMs and AI coding agents to accelerate code exploration, problem analysis, implementation, test development, and documentation where they are useful.
Critically review AI-generated suggestions and verify them against the actual codebase, requirements, and observed behavior. Validate changes through appropriate reviews and tests, and remain accountable for the correctness, security, performance, and maintainability of delivered software.

Adapt facilitation methods to suit different learner profiles, experience levels, and capability gaps.
Reinforce the application of soft skills during customer interactions, rather than focusing solely on theoretical concepts.
2. Agent Coaching & Performance Improvement
Conduct individual and group coaching based on call observations, Quality feedback, assessment results, and identified skill gaps.
Review customer interaction examples to identify behavioural opportunities and recommend targeted interventions.
Provide actionable feedback on communication, empathy, listening, ownership, and resolution behaviours.
Conduct mock calls, practice conversations, and behavioural assessments to evaluate agent readiness.
Track coaching actions and conduct follow-up validations to ensure feedback is translated into improved performance.
Support agents who require additional intervention through structured improvement plans and targeted practice.
3. CRT Program Execution
Support the implementation and ongoing delivery of CRT learning interventions across relevant agent groups.
Partner with the CRT program team to understand learning objectives, customer pain points, performance trends, and priority capability gaps.
Prepare session plans, facilitator guides, participant activities, practice scenarios, and assessment materials.
Maintain training attendance, assessment results, coaching records, and program progress reports.
Ensure consistent delivery of approved content and alignment with CRT standards.
Incorporate feedback and emerging customer interaction trends into future training interventions.
4. Quality & Business Collaboration
Partner with Quality and Operations teams to identify recurring communication and customer experience gaps.
Participate in call calibrations and feedback discussions to understand performance expectations and align coaching approaches.
Analyse available quality insights, customer feedback, repeat contacts, and escalation trends to identify relevant learning needs.
Support pre- and post-training assessments to evaluate skill development and learning transfer.
Recommend targeted refreshers or coaching interventions based on observed performance gaps.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives aimed at improving customer experience and resolution effectiveness.
5. Learning Effectiveness & Reporting
Measure learning effectiveness through assessments, mock-call evaluations, facilitator observations, and post-training feedback.
Maintain accurate records of training delivery, learner progress, and follow-up coaching.
Prepare regular updates on training completion, learner performance, key behavioural gaps, and improvement opportunities.
Share insights and recommendations with the CRT program, Quality, and Operations stakeholders.
Demonstrate the impact of training through observable improvements in agent communication and customer interaction quality.
Qualifications & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in any discipline; relevant training certifications are an advantage.
Typically 3–6 years of experience in soft skills training, customer service training, communication coaching, or learning and development.
Experience in a customer support, BPO, contact centre, or customer experience environment is preferred.
Demonstrated ability to facilitate soft skills sessions and coach customer-facing employees.
Experience with call listening, mock-call assessments, Quality feedback, or behavioural coaching is desirable.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage diverse audiences.
Proficiency in PowerPoint, Excel, and standard virtual training tools.
Ability to manage multiple training activities, maintain documentation, and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
Core Competencies
Facilitation excellence: Creates engaging, interactive, learner-centred sessions.
Customer empathy: Demonstrates a strong understanding of customer emotions, expectations, and service recovery.
Coaching effectiveness: Provides specific, constructive, behaviour-based feedback.
Communication: Communicates with clarity, confidence, and professionalism.
Adaptability: Adjusts delivery based on learner needs and performance gaps.
Analytical thinking: Uses call observations and Quality insights to identify capability needs.
Collaboration: Works effectively with Training, Quality, and Operations teams.
Execution discipline: Manages schedules, records, assessments, and follow-up actions consistently.
Success Measures
Training delivery completion and adherence to the CRT learning plan.
Improvement in soft skills assessment and mock-call scores.
Observable improvement in empathy, active listening, probing, ownership, and expectation setting.
Reduction in recurring behavioural gaps identified through call monitoring, where applicable.
Completion and effectiveness of targeted coaching and refresher interventions.
Positive stakeholder feedback and demonstrated application of learning on the job.
What We Are Looking For
We are looking for a practical, energetic, and learner-focused trainer who can connect with frontline agents, simplify behavioural concepts, and translate them into effective customer conversations.
The right candidate will combine strong facilitation and coaching skills with an understanding of contact centre realities. They should be comfortable working closely with Quality and Operations, using real customer scenarios to address capability gaps, and contributing to measurable improvements in the CRT program.
This is an intermediate-level opportunity for a trainer who is ready to take ownership of soft skills learning delivery and grow their impact through structured coaching, stakeholder collaboration, and continuous improvement.

jobs.description:
Workplace Experience & Real Estate Portfolio Lead
Description -
Workplace Experience & Real Estate Portfolio Lead
Bengaluru, India
About the Role
India is one of HP Inc.’s strategically important and operationally complex markets. The Principal, CREWS India is the accountable workplace experience and real estate leader for India, shaping environments that enable business performance, strengthen employee engagement, and help teams, peers, and partners thrive across multiple sites.
Based in Bengaluru and reporting to the Director, CREWS — APJ, the Principal, CREWS India will serve as a trusted country leader and partner to India business and site leaders, Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement, Security, EHS, and global CREWS stakeholders. The role requires executive presence, sound judgment, and the ability to align diverse stakeholders, lead enterprise-scale change, and translate business, workforce, and employee needs into an integrated India workplace strategy.
This is a strategic leadership and accountability role. The successful candidate will lead through others, influence without authority, and connect workplace decisions to HP’s business priorities. Success will be measured through business continuity, productivity and collaboration, employee experience, cost and capital discipline, risk and compliance, partner performance, and delivery of complex transformation priorities.
Key Responsibilities
Own workplace experience, facilities, and site services across India, creating safe, compliant, reliable environments that enable employees and teams to perform at their best.
Bring a hospitality-led mindset to workplace delivery, creating responsive, thoughtful, high-quality experiences for employees, leaders, visitors, and partners.
Set India’s real estate and workplace strategy, translating business and workforce priorities into portfolio plans, space optimization, investment choices, and executive-ready recommendations.
Partner with senior business and site leaders to anticipate growth, workforce, cultural, operational, and regulatory needs and convert them into workplace solutions that improve productivity, collaboration, talent experience, and resilience.
Establish strong governance through clear KPIs, SLAs, reporting rhythms, accountability, and recovery plans for service providers and internal delivery teams.
Own India operating and capital budgets, optimize total workplace cost, and build compelling business cases that balance financial return, employee experience, risk, and long-term value.
Provide strategic oversight of construction, fit-out, renovation, consolidation, expansion and facilities related issues
Build, coach, and develop India CREWS team and partner ecosystem, fostering an inclusive, positive environment where people take ownership, collaborate, and thrive.
Represent HP Inc. with landlords, developers, service partners, consultants, and senior governmental or regulatory representatives where required.
Drive EHS, security, procurement, financial, sustainability, and statutory compliance across the India portfolio.
Ensure disciplined follow-through on issues, escalations, and service gaps, with clear ownership, urgency, transparency, and closure.
Foster collaboration, ownership, continuous improvement, and One HP problem-solving across regional, global, and local teams.
Lead India’s employee transportation program, ensuring compliance, service reliability, and adoption of innovative, industry-standard technologies.
Education & Experience
Bachelor’s degree required in Business Administration, Engineering, Architecture, Real Estate, Facilities Management, or a related discipline; equivalent demonstrated experience will be considered.
Graduate degree, MBA, or postgraduate qualification preferred.
Typically 12+ years of progressive experience in facilities services, corporate real estate, workplace operations, portfolio management, or related fields.
Experience leading large, complex, multi-site operations in India, preferably within a multinational, technology, engineering, R&D, or shared-services environment.
Demonstrated track record of influencing senior executives, leading enterprise-scale change, and delivering measurable outcomes across workplace experience, cost, risk, and business performance.
Preferred certifications include Certified Facility Manager, PMP, RICS, MCR/CORENET, LEED, GRIHA, or equivalent credentials.
Required Knowledge & Skills
Facilities management, workplace services, preventive maintenance, EHS, sustainability, security coordination, and business continuity.
Construction, fit-out, renovation, HVAC, plumbing, property management, supplier management, and project governance.
Finance, procurement, financial analysis, budget ownership, forecasting, invoicing, and executive reporting.
KPIs, service provider governance, root-cause analysis, continuous improvement, and recovery planning.
Ability to navigate statutory requirements, government interfaces, landlord/developer relationships, and India market dynamics.
Leadership Competencies
Strategic thinking, results orientation, and the ability to convert ambiguity into clear priorities, decisions, and execution plans.
Executive presence and effective communication with senior leaders, employee councils, government representatives, landlords, developers, vendors, and internal teams.
Customer centricity, digital fluency, learning agility, and data-driven decision-making, with the ability to translate business, workforce, and employee needs into strategies that improve productivity, collaboration, engagement, and organizational performance.
Collaborative leadership across matrixed global, regional, and local teams, creating trust, shared accountability, and a positive environment where colleagues and partners can thrive.
Ability to influence outcomes without direct authority by building trust, aligning stakeholders, creating shared ownership, and following through on commitments.
Constructive, resilient leadership under pressure, maintaining clarity, inclusion, accountability, and momentum through ambiguity and escalation.
People leadership capability, including coaching, performance management, talent development, team building, and succession readiness.
Enterprise leadership potential to lead large cross-functional programs, influence long-term direction, and represent the function at senior forums.
Impact, Scope & Complexity
Shapes outcomes for large functions and leads complex, cross-division initiatives across India, with visibility and influence at country, regional, and global leadership levels.
Delivers innovative, practical solutions to complex real estate and workplace challenges, using data and stakeholder insight to improve employee experience, productivity, resilience, cost, and risk outcomes.
Balances day-to-day service reliability with long-term transformation, portfolio optimization, sustainability goals, and workforce experience outcomes.
Requires sound judgment, resilience, collaboration, and the ability to make trade-offs across cost, risk, service quality, compliance, employee experience, and business growth.
Preferred Leadership Differentiators
Experience with smart building technologies, workplace analytics, and sustainability frameworks such as LEED, GRIHA, or equivalent.
Track record leading workplace transformations or portfolio expansions in complex, high-growth organizations.
Natural ability to influence, align, and collaborate across global, regional, and local teams without relying on formal authority.
Passion for operational excellence and belief that the workplace can drive culture, performance, collaboration, and talent experience.
Travel
Travel within India and occasional regional travel may be required based on business, site, project, and stakeholder needs.
Why HP Inc. India
At HP Inc., CREWS creates workplace experiences that enable business outcomes, support our people, and advance the well-being of our communities and planet. This role offers the opportunity to shape one of HP’s most important country portfolios, lead through meaningful complexity, and strengthen India CREWS capability. The right candidate will help make HP’s workplace a competitive advantage while developing the breadth, judgment, and enterprise leadership capability to take on expanded scope as opportunities arise.
HP Inc. is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace.

jobs.title: Communications & People Engagement Lead
jobs.description:
Communications & People Engagement Lead
Description -
The Communications & People Engagement Lead is a strategic partner responsible for shaping organizational culture, driving employee engagement, strengthening leadership communications, and enabling successful change adoption across the Global Customer Care Centers (CCC) organization.
This role serves as the connective tissue between leadership, employees, and business priorities assuring that communication is not merely informational, but transformational. The individual will design and execute integrated communication, engagement, culture, recognition, and change management strategies that foster connection, transparency, inclusion, and organizational effectiveness across a globally distributed workforce.
The role requires a highly creative, customer-centric, and influential communications professional capable of translating business priorities into meaningful employee experiences that build trust, drive alignment, accelerate adoption of change, and strengthen employee commitment to organizational goals.
Working closely with Customer Care Center leadership, Operations, Quality, Training, HR, Communications, and other business stakeholders, the Communications & People Engagement Lead will help build a connected, resilient, engaged, and future-ready workforce while elevating employee experience across all care center locations.
Key Responsibilities
1. Strategic Communications
Organizational Communications Strategy
Develop and execute integrated communications strategies aligned to CCC business priorities, transformation initiatives, and organizational objectives.
Serve as the primary communications advisor to CCC leadership, shaping messaging that drives clarity, engagement, and alignment.
Build annual communication roadmaps and engagement calendars supporting strategic priorities.
Ensure consistent, timely, and effective communication across global teams, sites, and functions.
Establish communication standards, governance, and best practices across the organization.
Executive & Leadership Communications
Develop executive-level messaging, presentations, speeches, town halls, leadership updates, and employee communications.
Support leadership engagement sessions, all-employee meetings, fireside chats, podcasts, and interactive forums.
Partner with leaders to strengthen visibility, accessibility, and connection with employees.
Coach leaders on communication effectiveness, storytelling, and employee engagement approaches.
Communication Content Management
Own and manage end-to-end communication channels and content strategies.
Create and distribute:
Newsletters
Leadership updates
Internal campaigns
Employee stories
Organizational announcements
Transformation communications
Recognition communications
Ensuring content reflects organizational values, culture, and customer-focused priorities.
2. Storytelling, Branding & Employee Advocacy
Strategic Storytelling
Develop compelling narratives that connect employees to purpose, customers, business outcomes, and organizational strategy.
Translate complex business concepts into engaging, relatable, and actionable content.
Create storytelling frameworks that highlight innovation, customer impact, quality, transformation, and employee success.
Employee & Customer Impact Stories
Identify and amplify stories showcasing employee contributions, customer outcomes, operational excellence, and business impact.
Partner with leaders and teams to celebrate achievements and successes across geographies.
Build internal advocacy programs that increase employee pride and organizational connection.
Creative Content Development
Lead innovative communication approaches leveraging:
Visual storytelling
Infographics
Video communications
Digital campaigns
Podcasts
Interactive experiences
Executive narratives
Employee spotlights
Social and collaboration platforms
3. Employee Engagement & Culture
Employee Experience Strategy
Design and implement programs that strengthen employee engagement, belonging, motivation, and connection.
Partner with HR and leadership teams to improve employee experience across the employee lifecycle.
Develop initiatives that align employee sentiment with organizational goals and values.
Recognition & Appreciation Programs
Lead enterprise recognition strategies that celebrate performance, innovation, customer obsession, teamwork, and cultural excellence.
Establish scalable global recognition programs and engagement events.
Drive employee appreciation initiatives that reinforce desired organizational behaviors.
Inclusion, Belonging & Community
Champion an inclusive culture where all employees feel valued, respected, and empowered.
Build engagement initiatives that foster collaboration across countries, cultures, functions, and teams.
Partner with employee resource groups and community networks to create meaningful employee experiences.
Employee Listening Programs
Design and manage employee listening strategies including:
Pulse surveys
Focus groups
Listening sessions
Engagement assessments
Sentiment analysis
Translate employee feedback into actionable recommendations.
Ensure leadership accountability through continuous feedback loops and action planning.
4. Change Management & Organizational Adoption
Management of Change (MoC)
Lead communication and engagement workstreams supporting organizational transformation programs.
Develop comprehensive change communication strategies and adoption plans.
Ensure employees understand the rationale, benefits, risks, and impacts of transformation initiatives.
Change Communications
Create and implement communication plans covering:
Business rationale for change
Strategic objectives
Employee impacts
New ways of working
Adoption expectations
Success outcomes
Ongoing progress updates
Change Champion Network
Build and manage global networks of change champions.
Enable champions with training, messaging, communication assets, and engagement tools.
Drive local advocacy and adoption across regions and teams.
Adoption & Readiness Management
Measure awareness, readiness, engagement, and adoption of key initiatives.
Identify resistance points and engagement risks.
Develop mitigation strategies and targeted interventions.
Track organizational readiness and communication effectiveness.
5. Leadership Engagement & Organizational Effectiveness
Leadership Partnership
Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders on employee engagement, communications, culture, and change initiatives.
Provide insights and recommendations that improve organizational effectiveness and employee connection.
Employee Engagement Events
Lead planning and execution of:
Global All Employee Meetings
Leadership forums
Town halls
Engagement weeks
Recognition ceremonies
Cultural celebrations
Volunteer and community activities
Learning and development events
Global Collaboration
Foster collaboration across sites, partners, suppliers, and functional organizations.
Encourage sharing of best practices, knowledge, and organizational success stories.
6. Employee Relations & Interpersonal Effectiveness
Employee Advocacy
Champion employee concerns, perspectives, and ideas.
Promote transparent communication and trust across the organization.
Active Listening & Empathy
Create environments where employees feel heard, respected, and supported.
Strengthen leadership understanding of employee needs and experiences.
Conflict Resolution & Engagement Support
Facilitate constructive dialogue and partnership across teams.
Support resolution of communication, engagement, and adoption challenges.
Promote collaboration and positive working relationships.
Success Measures
Performance will be measured through:
Communication Excellence
Employee awareness and understanding of organizational priorities.
Communication reach, engagement, and effectiveness.
Leadership communication satisfaction metrics.
Quality and timeliness of communication delivery.
Employee Engagement
Improvements in engagement and sentiment indicators.
Participation in engagement programs and activities.
Recognition program adoption and impact.
Employee advocacy and connection measures.
Change Adoption
Change readiness and adoption of metrics.
Effectiveness of change communication programs.
Champion network participation and influence.
Achievement of transformation communication objectives.
Culture & Leadership Impact
Improved employee trust and leadership connectivity.
Stronger culture of transparency, inclusion, and recognition.
Increased alignment to organizational vision and goals.
Enhanced employee experience outcomes.
Qualifications & Experience
Education
Bachelor’s degree in communications, Public Relations, Marketing, Human Resources, Organizational Development, Business Administration, Journalism, or related discipline.
Master's degree preferred.
Experience
8–12+ years of experience in Communications, Employee Engagement, Internal Communications, Organizational Development, Change Management, Human Resources, or related fields.
Experience supporting global and matrixed organizations.
Proven track record managing enterprise communication and engagement programs.
Experience supporting organizational transformation and change adoption initiatives.
Critical Skills & Competencies

Executive and organizational communications
Internal communications strategy
Employee engagement and experience
Change management
Strategic storytelling
Event management
Stakeholder management
Program and project management
Communication analytics and insights
Content creation and digital communications
Leadership Competencies
Influencing without authority
Strategic thinking
Business acumen
Customer obsession
Relationship building
Emotional intelligence
Collaboration and partnership
Creativity and innovation
Resilience and adaptability
Inclusive leadership

The Communications & People Engagement Lead transforms communication into a strategic business capability—connecting people to purpose, enabling organizational change, strengthening culture, elevating employee experience, and building a highly engaged, resilient, customer-obsessed workforce across the Global Customer Care Centers organization.

jobs.description:
About Analog Devices
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. Job Description:
We are seeking a skilled and experienced DFT Engineer to join our VLSI design team. The ideal candidate should have a strong background in Design for Testability (DFT) techniques, including LBIST (Logic Built-In Self-Test), ATPG (Automatic Test Pattern Generation), DFT DRC (Design Rule Checking), MBIST (Memory Built-in Sefl-Test), Boundary Scan, JTAG and Analog/Phy DFT.
Responsibilities:
Collaborate with the Design/Arch/PTE/PD team to ensure efficient and effective testability of complex integrated circuits.
Design and implement DFT features such as scan chains, compression, and built-in self-test structures to enhance testability.
Conduct DFT DRC checks in RTL/Netlist database to ensure compliance with DFT guidelines and rules.
Utilize Siemen’s DFT tool to perform DFT analysis and optimize testability metrics.
Generating high quality manufacturing ATPG test patterns for stuck-at (SAF), transition fault (TDF) models using on-chip test compression techniques.
MBIST Design (including repair) and Verification using Siemen’s EDA tool.
Validation of DFT structures/patterns in RTL, Netlist with and without SDF.
Work closely with the verification team to define and implement DFT verification plans.
Work closely with physical design team for DFT implementation/constraints strategy for synthesis/STA.
Analyze and debug test failures and collaborate with the test engineering team to resolve issues.
Provide guidance and mentorship to junior DFT engineers.
Qualifications:
Bachelor's/Master's degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering, or a related field.
7-10 years of hands-on experience in DFT methodologies and techniques.
Strong knowledge of LBIST, ATPG, DFT DRC, Scan compression, Low power DFT Techniques, MBIST, Boundary Scan, Analog DFT, JTAG Architecture, DFT STA Constraint development.
Hand-on experience/expertise in Cadence/Siemen’s DFT EDA tools for Scan stitching, DRC, ATPG, Coverage improvement, MBIST, Boundary Scan.
Proficiency in scripting languages such as Perl, Tcl, and/or Python for automation.
Solid understanding of digital design fundamentals, RTL coding, Lint/CDC, Low Power Checks and ASIC design flow.
Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

Key Responsibilities
Verification Environment Development: Develop and maintain SystemVerilog/UVM verification environments, including agents, sequences, monitors, scoreboards, reference models, assertions, and functional coverage.
SoC Verification: Verify SoC functionality involving embedded processors, memories, interconnects, interrupts, DMA controllers, peripherals, communication interfaces, and mixed-signal subsystems.
Verification Planning: Contribute to verification plans by translating design and product requirements into test scenarios, coverage items, and verification objectives.
Test Development: Develop directed and constrained-random tests for block-level, subsystem-level, and SoC-level verification.
Processor-Based Verification: Develop and execute verification scenarios for microprocessor-based SoCs, including processor initialization, register accesses, interrupts, exceptions, boot sequences, and basic firmware interactions.
C DPI Integration: Develop and maintain C/SystemVerilog DPI interfaces and integrate C-based models or reference functions into simulation environments.
E2B Functionality: Verify E2B communication functionality, including configuration, control, data transfer, timing behavior, error handling, diagnostics, and recovery scenarios.
Coverage and Metrics: Analyze functional, code, and assertion coverage; identify verification gaps; and develop additional tests to support verification closure.
Regression Execution: Execute and monitor verification regressions, analyze failures, classify issues, and communicate results to the project team.
Debugging: Analyze and resolve verification failures across testbenches, RTL, embedded C code, reference models, and system-level scenarios.
Functional Safety Support: Contribute to verification of automotive safety mechanisms, fault injection tests, requirements traceability, and verification evidence for ISO 26262-related activities.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with design, architecture, firmware, functional safety, validation, and applications teams to resolve technical issues and support project milestones.
Documentation: Create and maintain clear documentation covering verification plans, testcases, coverage results, known issues, and verification status.
Automation: Develop scripts to automate regression execution, results analysis, coverage reporting, and other verification workflows.
Technical Reviews: Participate in design, architecture, verification plan, and code reviews, providing verification-focused feedback.
Must-Have Skills
SystemVerilog and UVM: Proficiency in developing and maintaining verification environments using SystemVerilog and the Universal Verification Methodology.
Testbench Development: Experience developing coverage-driven verification components and testcases for complex digital designs.
Digital and SoC Verification: Understanding of digital verification concepts and experience verifying blocks, subsystems, or SoCs containing processors, memories, buses, interrupts, peripherals, or communication interfaces.
C and C DPI: Experience with C programming and familiarity with integrating C models or functions into SystemVerilog environments through DPI.
Verification Techniques: Experience with directed testing, constrained-random verification, functional coverage, code coverage, and assertion-based verification.
Verilog RTL: Strong understanding of RTL design concepts and the ability to read and debug Verilog or SystemVerilog RTL.
Debugging: Ability to analyze and resolve moderately complex verification problems with limited supervision.
Scripting and Automation: Ability to develop scripts using Python, Perl, TCL, shell, or similar languages to improve verification workflows.
EDA Tools: Experience using simulation, waveform-debug, regression, and coverage-analysis tools.
Communication Interfaces: Working knowledge of communication interfaces such as SPI, I2C, or UART and their verification requirements.
Collaboration: Effective communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate with design, firmware, validation, and other engineering groups.
Preferred Skills
Experience verifying SoCs incorporating RISC-V processors. Experience with ARM or other embedded processor architectures is also valuable.
Familiarity with processor concepts such as privilege modes, exceptions, interrupts, memory protection, debug infrastructure, and firmware boot sequences.
Experience with firmware-driven verification or hardware-software co-verification.
Experience developing C/SystemVerilog DPI components and integrating C-based reference models.
Familiarity with automotive connectivity technologies, in-vehicle networking, or E2B technology.
Experience verifying packet-based communication protocols, control channels, error handling, diagnostics, or recovery mechanisms.
Understanding of automotive functional safety and ISO 26262 development processes.
Familiarity with fault injection, safety-mechanism verification, or requirements traceability.
Experience with emulation, FPGA prototyping, virtual platforms, or pre-silicon firmware development.
Familiarity with mixed-signal verification or analog behavioral models.
Knowledge of formal verification, clock-domain crossing, reset-domain crossing, low-power verification, or gate-level simulation.
Familiarity with continuous integration and automated regression infrastructure.
Preferred Education and Experience
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics and Communications Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
2–4 years of relevant experience in digital design verification.
Experience developing SystemVerilog/UVM testbenches and coverage-driven verification environments.

Senior Verification Manager – Automotive Connectivity SoCs (E2B)
About the Role
As a Senior Verification Manager at Analog Devices, you will lead a team of verification engineers responsible for the development and verification of next-generation automotive connectivity SoCs based on E2B technology. The role combines strong people leadership with deep technical expertise in complex SoC verification, enabling the successful delivery of safety-critical automotive products.
You will define verification strategies and execution plans for highly integrated SoCs incorporating embedded processors, communication subsystems, firmware, security functions, and mixed-signal components. Working closely with architecture, design, firmware, functional safety, and program management teams, you will ensure robust verification coverage, successful tapeouts, and compliance with automotive quality standards.
This position requires a hands-on technical leader who can guide teams through complex verification challenges while driving organizational excellence in verification methodologies, automation, and execution.
Key Responsibilities
Technical and Organizational Leadership
Lead, mentor, and grow a team of verification engineers across multiple automotive SoC programs.
Establish verification methodologies, best practices, and reusable infrastructure across projects.
Drive hiring, career development, performance management, and technical growth within the verification organization.
Manage project execution, resource planning, risk assessment, and verification schedules.
SoC Verification Strategy
Define and oversee verification strategies for complex automotive SoCs containing embedded processors, firmware, security features, communication controllers, DMA engines, memory subsystems, and mixed-signal IP.
Establish verification plans, coverage goals, and sign-off criteria aligned with product and safety requirements.
Drive verification closure through coverage-driven methodologies, assertions, formal verification, and software-driven verification techniques.
Automotive Connectivity and E2B Verification
Lead verification activities for E2B communication technology and associated protocol implementations.
Ensure robust validation of protocol compliance, interoperability, error handling, diagnostics, timing behavior, and system-level performance.
Collaborate with architecture and firmware teams to ensure seamless hardware-software integration and protocol deployment.
Functional Safety and Quality
Ensure verification activities satisfy automotive development requirements, including ISO 26262 processes and safety mechanisms verification.
Support safety analysis activities, fault injection campaigns, safety collateral generation, and traceability requirements.
Establish metrics and quality indicators to measure verification effectiveness and product readiness.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner with architecture, RTL design, firmware, validation, applications, and product teams throughout the product lifecycle.
Participate in technical reviews and project milestones from architecture definition through silicon validation.
Drive resolution of complex cross-functional issues impacting schedules, quality, or technical execution.
Must-Have Skills
SoC Verification Expertise
Extensive experience verifying complex SoCs containing embedded processors, memory hierarchies, interconnects, DMA engines, interrupts, security modules, and communication subsystems.
Proven experience delivering successful SoC tapeouts in advanced semiconductor development environments.
Processor-Based Verification
Strong experience verifying microprocessor-based SoCs.
Experience with RISC-V processor architectures strongly preferred.
Understanding of privilege modes, exception handling, memory protection, caches, debug infrastructure, and firmware interactions.
SystemVerilog and UVM
Expert-level knowledge of SystemVerilog and UVM.
Proven experience architecting large-scale reusable verification environments and verification IP.
Experience defining organization-wide verification methodologies and verification frameworks.
DPI and Hardware-Software Co-Verification

Verification Strategy: Develop and implement comprehensive verification strategies and test plans for automotive connectivity SoCs and E2B-related functionality.

Debug and Issue Resolution: Analyze and resolve complex issues across RTL, UVM environments, embedded software, C models, and system-level use cases.
Functional Safety Verification: Support verification of safety mechanisms, fault injection campaigns, requirements traceability, and verification activities associated with ISO 26262-compliant automotive products.

Hardware-Software Integration: Experience developing firmware-driven tests and debugging interactions between embedded software and RTL.
Debugging Expertise: Strong analytical and debugging skills across SystemVerilog/UVM testbenches, RTL, embedded C code, and system-level environments.
Scripting and Automation: Proficiency in Python, TCL, Perl, shell scripting, or similar languages for regression management, result analysis, and workflow automation.

Oversee the full RFx lifecycle for complex construction, engineering, cleanroom, and fit‑out packages.
Set negotiation strategy, support contract‑structure development, and ensure commercial alignment across multiple projects and markets.
Ensure commercial rigor on change‑order management, claims mitigation, cost reconciliation, and risk allocation.
Partner with Commercial Managers/GWI to ensure category execution directly supports project schedule, budget, and risk requirements.
3. Supplier Strategy, Governance & Performance Management
Lead supplier capability assessments, long‑term performance tracking, and supplier‑development programs across APAC construction categories.
Provide forward‑looking visibility into resource constraints, market disruptions, contractor risks, and capacity challenges.
Influence supplier segmentation strategy together with GSP Category Leadership.

Lead development of high‑fidelity cost models, inflation indexes, market‑trend dashboards, and commercial risk heatmaps.
Provide decision‑grade insights to Singapore Category Leadership, onsite commercial teams, and project executives.
Support regional capital planning with analytical inputs, cost forecasts, and scenario modeling.
Drive data governance discipline to ensure audit‑ready processes, document control, and compliance.

Enable rapid scaling of sourcing support across India, Korea, Taiwan, and China during project surges.
Establish standardized processes, templates, playbooks, and commercial governance frameworks for APAC.
Partner closely with onsite focal resources to resolve commercial issues, negotiate escalations, and drive supplier accountability.
Lead continuous‑improvement initiatives to optimize cycle time, sourcing quality, and process maturity.

10–15 years of experience in capital construction procurement, category management, or large‑program commercial operations.

Deep expertise in commercial negotiation, contract terms, risk allocation, claims strategy, and cost governance.
Strong leadership capability — able to build, mentor, and scale high‑performing teams.
Advanced analytical capability: cost modeling, market intelligence, benchmarking, and financial analysis.
Experience influencing senior stakeholders across functions and geographies.
High agility, strong judgment, and ability to operate in fast‑moving and high‑ambiguity project environments.

India is being established as the central execution hub for APAC capital construction sourcing.

High‑quality commercial packages delivered on schedule, aligned to project and category strategies.

This is a hands-on product management role with a strong emphasis on execution, cross-functional coordination, and operationalizing AI/ML capabilities within content localization workflows. This role will be based in Hyderabad and will be responsible for leading a large controllership team, ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant financial reporting, strong balance sheet governance, effective internal controls, and successful delivery of close, reporting, audit support, and compliance requirements.
This is a critical leadership role within the Accounting COE and will play a key part in building, transitioning, stabilizing, and scaling controllership activities including transition from other regions. The Director will partner closely with WBD Controllership, FP&A, Tax, Treasury, Global Business Services (GBS), and other global and regional stakeholders to deliver high-quality financial outcomes at scale.
The role requires a strong controllership mindset, deep technical accounting knowledge, proven people leadership, and the ability to operate effectively in a complex, matrixed, global environment. The successful candidate will be expected to lead transition of accounting work to WBD’s Hyderabad center, drive operational discipline, process standardization, automation, continuous improvement, and a culture of accountability, quality, and compliance.
This role will manage ~ 5 Senior Manager level accounting positions in Hyderabad and will oversee a broader team of ~50 accounting positions, supporting the controllership function. Your normal hours of work are 3:00 p.m IST. to 11:00 p.m IST. Monday to Friday. However, due to business needs, you may be required to work outside these hours and on holidays for the proper performance of your role without any additional pay. Your Role Accountabilities…
Controllership, Close and Reporting Leadership
• Lead and oversee RTR accounting and controllership activities
• Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close processes, ensuring accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and compliance with applicable accounting and reporting requirements.
• Supervise intercompany reconciliations and resolve out-of-balance items with WBD counterparts.
• Ensure strong balance sheet governance, account reconciliation quality, variance analysis, management reporting, and timely issue resolution.
• Review and analyze financial results against expectations and provide meaningful insights to controllership and business stakeholders.
• Review and sign-off monthly and quarterly Balance Sheets, Income Statements, and Cash Flow Statements, including footnotes disclosures and supplemental schedules, ensuring completeness and accuracy.
• Ensure accounting implications of business transactions are assessed timely, including coordination with Technical Accounting teams where required.
• Responsible for system/manual reconciliations between the Business Unit boundary systems and SAP, ensuring data consistency and accuracy
• Continuously identify, design, and implement process improvements and standardizations across areas of responsibility to enhance efficiency and effectiveness. This includes special projects and serving as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) as needed.
Governance, Controls and Audit Readiness
• Maintain a strong internal control environment and ensure compliance with SOX requirements.
• Partner with internal and external auditors to support audit planning, walkthroughs, testing, information requests, and timely closure of audit matters.
• Drive discipline around documentation, evidence retention, review controls, issue tracking, and remediation.
• Proactively identify financial reporting, compliance, and control risks and ensure appropriate escalation and resolution.
Transition and Operating Model Buildout
• Lead the transition, stabilization, and scaling of accounting activities being insourced from other regions into the Hyderabad Accounting COE.
• Establish clear ownership, process documentation, KPIs, service levels, governance routines, and escalation mechanisms.
• Partner with global and regional stakeholders to ensure business continuity, knowledge transfer, and successful transition outcomes.
• Build sustainable team capacity and capability to support the future-state controllership operating model.
