jobs.title: LLM & Agentic AI Performance Engineer
jobs.description: Job Details: Job Description: The Role and Impact: Join Intel's Data Center AI organization and help shape how LLM and Agentic AI workloads perform on Intel platforms. Our team operates at a unique intersection of core performance optimization, AI frameworks, and customer-facing AI solutions. We bridge the gap between teams that deeply understand silicon and benchmarking and teams building real-world AI solutions, turning performance insights into software optimizations that developers and customers can use. In this role, you will own end-to-end performance characterization and optimization of LLM and Agentic AI workloads, from Python-level frameworks and inference runtimes down to Linux, system architecture, and hardware performance counters. This is not simply a benchmarking role. Benchmarking tells us what the number is. Your job is to understand why the number is what it is, identify the hardware or software bottleneck, and determine what needs to change to remove it. Your work will translate into code contributions, framework optimizations, best-known configurations (BKCs), customer-ready solutions, and insights that help influence future Intel hardware and software. If you enjoy working across the complete AI stack, from agent frameworks and LLM serving engines to NUMA, memory bandwidth, cache behavior, and silicon counters, this role provides an opportunity to work at that intersection. About the Team: The AI Solutions and Toolkit Engineering team is part of Intel's Data Center organization, focused on enabling modern AI workloads and solutions on Intel platforms. We work across the AI ecosystem, collaborating with AI framework and runtime developers, performance and optimization teams, hardware architects, open-source communities, and solution engineering teams. Our goal is to take deep platform capabilities and performance insights and translate them into practical, optimized AI solutions that developers and customers can deploy. The team works across areas including LLM inference, Agentic AI, AI frameworks and runtimes, workload optimization, open-source software, and datacenter AI systems. Key Responsibilities: Characterize and optimize LLM and Agentic AI workloads across the complete software and hardware stack. Identify performance bottlenecks across AI frameworks, inference runtimes, operating systems, memory, compute, and platform architecture. Design and develop hardware-aware and hardware-agnostic optimizations for AI frameworks and runtimes. Optimize LLM inference techniques including KV-cache management, attention, continuous batching, and quantization. Work hands-on with serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, or equivalent technologies. Analyze host and accelerator performance using tools such as VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, and roofline modeling. Debug complex performance issues spanning Python frameworks, native code, Linux, runtime libraries, and hardware. Convert performance findings into software changes, upstream contributions, BKCs, and reusable optimization guidance. Collaborate with open-source communities to upstream and integrate performance improvements. Translate silicon-level findings into actionable recommendations for framework developers, while bringing application and framework insights back to Intel platform and silicon teams. Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: BE +10 years / M.Tech +8 years in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline. Significant hands-on experience in performance engineering, systems optimization, or workload characterization on server-class platforms. Demonstrated ability to identify complex performance bottlenecks and deliver measurable performance improvements. Strong programming skills in Python and C++, or equivalent systems programming experience in C/Rust. Strong understanding of server architecture including cache hierarchy, memory bandwidth, NUMA, interconnects, and system-level performance behavior. Hands-on experience with Linux performance and system technologies such as affinity, huge pages, cgroups, eBPF, ftrace, perf, or equivalent tools. Preferred Qualifications: Deep understanding of LLM inference, including KV-cache, paged attention, continuous batching and quantization such as INT8, INT4, or FP8. Hands-on experience modifying or optimizing AI serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, OpenVINO, or equivalent. Experience building, profiling, or optimizing Agentic AI systems using technologies such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, MCP-based frameworks, or similar platforms. Experience with hardware counter-level performance analysis using VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, or roofline modeling. Contributions to significant open-source projects, including upstream code contributions. Ability to communicate across abstraction layers, translating silicon-level findings for software developers and application-level requirements for hardware architects. Why Join This Team? This role gives you the opportunity to work across boundaries that few engineering positions span: Agentic AI & LLMs AI frameworks inference runtimes Linux server architecture silicon You won't be limited to measuring performance or optimizing an isolated component. You'll help connect the entire stack, identify where the real bottlenecks are, implement improvements, and make those optimizations available to developers and customers. The result is tangible: better AI performance today, stronger software solutions for customers, and insights that can influence tomorrow's Intel platforms. Key Responsibilities Lead the architecture, design, implementation, and optimization of 3D reconstruction algorithms from concept through production deployment. Develop and improve tomographic reconstruction techniques for CT, XCT, and cone-beam CT, including analytical, iterative, model-based, and AI-assisted methods. Build algorithms for projection preprocessing, calibration, denoising, artifact correction, reconstruction, registration, segmentation, and volumetric analysis. Combine physics-based modeling, inverse-problem optimization, computer vision, and deep learning to improve reconstruction quality and system performance. Optimize large-scale 3D reconstruction pipelines for GPU, multithreaded, and high-performance computing environments. Define validation methodology and quality metrics using simulation, laboratory, and production datasets. Collaborate with systems, hardware, software, applications, and product teams to translate customer needs into scalable algorithmic solutions. Mentor algorithm engineers, conduct technical reviews, establish engineering best practices, and contribute to the technology roadmap. Key Requirements Master's or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Biomedical Engineering, or a related discipline; a bachelor's degree with substantial relevant industry experience may also be considered. 8+ years of experience in algorithm development, computational imaging, image processing, computer vision, or a related technical field. At least 5 years of hands-on experience developing 3D image reconstruction or tomographic imaging algorithms. Proven experience delivering production-quality reconstruction algorithms for X-ray CT/XCT, cone-beam CT, microscopy, medical imaging, industrial inspection, or semiconductor metrology systems. Hands-on expertise with analytical and iterative reconstruction techniques such as filtered back projection, Feldkamp-Davis-Kress, ART, SART/SIRT, and model-based iterative reconstruction. Experience solving inverse imaging problems using numerical optimization, regularization, statistical estimation, compressed sensing, or Bayesian methods. Experience with projection-domain and image-domain corrections including detector calibration, denoising, ring and streak artifact reduction, beam-hardening correction, and motion or alignment compensation. Experience with large volumetric datasets, 3D registration, segmentation, feature extraction, defect analysis, and quantitative metrology. Strong programming skills in C++ and Python; MATLAB or equivalent scientific prototyping tools are beneficial. Experience with CUDA/GPU computing, parallel processing, multithreading, or high-performance computing. Strong foundation in linear algebra, numerical methods, optimization, probability, statistics, signal processing, imaging physics, and 3D geometry. Experience with NumPy, SciPy, OpenCV, ITK, VTK, CUDA, or equivalent scientific and imaging libraries. Preferred Qualifications Experience with semiconductor inspection, metrology, defect review, or advanced manufacturing systems. Knowledge of X-ray imaging physics, detector behavior, acquisition geometry, system calibration, and numerical simulation. Experience applying deep learning to reconstruction, denoising, super-resolution, segmentation, or artifact reduction using PyTorch or TensorFlow. Experience with point-cloud processing, surface extraction, mesh generation, multi-modal registration, or 3D visualization. Experience leading technical teams, mentoring engineers, owning architecture decisions, and coordinating cross-functional delivery. Patent filings, peer-reviewed publications, or recognized innovation in reconstruction, imaging, or computational methods. . This role exists at the boundary between customer and product - /ou embed with clients before a single line of production code is written, validate whether an AI solution actually solves the business problem, and hand a scoped, evidence-backed brief to the product and engineering teams that build it. You are a builder first, but your deliverable is clarity, not code. Roles and Responsibilities: Embed directly with issuer and acquirer clients to understand their operational workflows, surface pain points, and identify where AI-driven automation or intelligence creates measurable business value. - Design and build rapid proof-of-concept prototypes - agentic pipelines, conversational interfaces, analytical tools - scoped deliberately to test a specific business hypothesis, not to be production-ready. Translate ambiguous client requirements into concrete, testable problem statements; push back on requirements that are too broad to validate or too narrow to generalize. Run structured validation sessions with customers using working prototypes, gather qualitative and quantitative signal on whether the PoC addresses the stated need, and document what it does not. Synthesize field observations into product briefs: scoped requirements, edge cases discovered in the wild, constraints the platform team would not have known from a desk, and a clear go/no-go recommendation. - Partner with product managers to ensure PoC findings directly inform roadmap decisions - requirements that survive validation become backlog items; those that do not get killed before investment is made. Maintain a working knowledge of the AI capability landscape (LLMs, agentic frameworks, retrieval-augmented generation, structured data reasoning) broad enough to know what is feasible in a six-week PoC versus what requires a platform build. - Identify patterns across client engagements that suggest platform-level investment - repeatable needs that should become product features rather than one-off prototypes. Represent technical feasibility in pre-sales and discovery conversations; give customers and internal stakeholders an honest read on what AI can and cannot do for their specific workflow today. - Mentor engineers and analysts on the team on customer discovery craft - how to ask questions that reveal unstated requirements, how to scope a PoC to answer one question well, and how to present findings without overselling. All About You: Master's or bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, with significant experience delivering AI or data solutions to enterprise clients. - Proven track record building working AI prototypes that directly influenced product or investment decisions - you can point to cases where your PoC changed what got built. Strong engineering foundation: you can write clean, working code quickly without over-engineering for production concerns that are irrelevant at the PoC stage. Fluent in Python and comfortable with SQL; experience with large-scale structured data and cloud data platforms is a strong plus. - Hands-on experience with LLM APIs and agentic patterns - you understand the tradeoffs between what you can prompt, what you need to engineer, and what requires fine-tuning. Exceptional customer-facing communication: you can run a discovery session with a non-technical reconciliation analyst in the morning and write a technical scoping document in the afternoon. Strong product instinct: you can distinguish a business requirement from a solution assumption, and you know when a client is describing a symptom rather than a root cause. - Comfort operating in ambiguity - you thrive when the problem statement is unclear and see scoping it as part of the job, not a blocker. Experience working in regulated industries (financial services, payments, healthcare) where data sensitivity, compliance constraints, and customer trust shape what can and cannot be prototyped. Track record of handing off well-scoped, evidence-backed briefs to product and engineering teams; you measure success by what gets built from your findings, not by the prototype itself. Description and Requirements Lenovo Solutions & Services Group is running a company-wide AI transformation programme, embedding engineering talent directly inside business functions. Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) are the builders at the center of that model. As an FDE, you will be assigned to a specific business function and work alongside its leaders and teams to identify where AI creates real leverage, then build and deploy practical solutions that fit how work actually gets done. This is not a research or advisory role — you move from discovery to working prototype to deployed solution within sprint cycles, in close partnership with a Domain Leader who provides business direction and context. The right candidate is energized by driving meaningful change in a business — not just shipping code, but making sure what gets built is genuinely adopted and used. You are comfortable working with typical tech stacks such as Microsoft and ServiceNow as well as building custom AI agents/ solutions on other internal platforms. What You Will Do Discover and Define Embed in a business function and work with the Domain Leader and subject matter experts to map workflows, surface pain points, and identify high-value AI opportunities. Translate business problems into scoped, deliverable use cases — balancing ambition with what is practical to build and adopt. Build and Deploy Design and build AI solutions using the right tools for the problem: Microsoft AI and productivity platforms (Copilot Studio, Azure OpenAI, M365), RAG pipelines, agent workflows, automation tooling, and custom development where needed. Prototype quickly, test with real users, and iterate within short sprint cycles. Deliver solutions that integrate into existing workflows — not standalone demos. Drive Adoption and Impact Own adoption as well as technical delivery — work alongside change resources to help teams actually use what gets built. Gather feedback post-deployment to improve performance and increase business value over time. Contribute to patterns and practices that can scale across squads and functions. Communicate and Collaborate Bridge business stakeholders, data teams, and platform partners — translating clearly in both directions. Provide concise, honest updates on progress, risks, and tradeoffs to technical and senior non-technical audiences alike. What We’re Looking For Required 5+ years in software engineering, solutions engineering, applied AI, or a closely related technical role. Hands-on experience building and deploying AI, automation, or intelligent workflow solutions in real business settings. Strong working knowledge of LLMs, prompt design, retrieval-based architectures, orchestration, and agent-based systems. Comfortable integrating with enterprise APIs, data sources, and workflow platforms. A genuine drive to see change land — you understand that building the solution is only half the job. Clear communicator; able to explain technical decisions in plain language to business and leadership audiences. Preferred Experience with Microsoft AI platforms: Copilot Studio, Azure OpenAI, M365, Power Platform. Custom development skills (Python, JavaScript, or similar) for problems that off-the-shelf tooling cannot solve. Background in technical consulting, solutions architecture, or customer-facing engineering. Experience with change enablement, user adoption, or process redesign alongside technical delivery. What Success Looks Like Working solutions in users’ hands at the end of each sprint — not decks or proofs of concept. Measurable business outcomes: time saved, processes improved, decisions made faster. A team that has adopted the tools and can articulate the impact. A function that can operate and evolve its AI solutions after the engagement ends. jobs.title: Scaled AI & Solution Architect
jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY The Scaled AI & Solution Architect is the senior technical design authority for the Digital Quality (DQ) organisation, which delivers the solutions that transform Quality, Safety and Environmental Operations (QSEO) across Pfizer. The role is a global individual contributor position accountable for setting and driving the AI and solution architecture direction across the entire DQ product portfolio, rather than for the delivery of any single product. The incumbent defines the target architecture, reference patterns, reusable components and engineering standards that every DQ solution is built against, so that capability is built once and reused many times rather than rebuilt product by product. The role leads the scaled adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and agentic AI across the portfolio, translating enterprise AI platforms and emerging technology into GxP-compliant, validated, production-grade capability that measurably improves quality, safety and environmental outcomes at site level. Recognised as an expert within and beyond Digital Quality, the incumbent influences the strategic technology direction of the QSEO business, and partners with Solution Leads, the Platform and Solution Engineering team, Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security to ensure architectural coherence, compliance and pace across a complex global portfolio. ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES Cross-Product Solution Architecture Own the target-state solution architecture for the Digital Quality portfolio, spanning quality management, laboratory, manufacturing quality, and safety, environment and occupational health solutions. Define how products, platforms, data and integrations fit together, and drive convergence of point solutions onto common architecture, avoiding duplicated capability and unmanaged technical debt across the portfolio. Architecture Standards, Patterns and Reusable Components Establish, publish and maintain the architecture standards, reference patterns, reusable components and engineering guardrails that DQ solutions are designed and built against, covering integration, data, identity, AI, validation and cyber security. Make reuse the path of least resistance for delivery teams, and measure adoption, reuse and the resulting delivery efficiency. Scaled AI Enablement Define and drive the AI and agentic AI architecture for the DQ portfolio, including use case patterns such as deviation and incident triage, leading-indicator prediction, automated document and content generation, and conversational access to standards and procedures. Determine where AI capability should be built once as a shared service versus configured per product, and ensure AI is delivered on enterprise platforms with appropriate human oversight, evaluation, model monitoring and lifecycle management. Design Authority and Technical Governance Act as design authority for significant DQ investments, reviewing and approving solution designs at key lifecycle gates and providing architectural assurance on build-versus-buy, platform selection and vendor technical fit. Identify multiple viable options for highly complex problems, set out the trade-offs in cost, risk, compliance and time to value, and make clear recommendations to Digital and business leadership and relevant governance forums. Technical Leadership and Capability Building Provide hands-on architectural leadership to Solution Leads, Product Managers, engineers and vendor teams across the portfolio without direct reporting authority, influencing through expertise, credibility and evidence. Mentor and raise the technical capability of architects and engineers across Digital Quality, and lead architecture and AI Communities of Practice that spread good practice across DQ and the wider Digital organisation. Compliance, Data Integrity and Security by Design Ensure architectural decisions embed GxP computerised system compliance, data integrity, data privacy and cyber security requirements from the outset, in partnership with Quality, Legal, Privacy, Compliance and Cyber Security. Define validation-efficient architecture patterns that allow AI and cloud capability to be deployed at pace while remaining inspection-ready. Innovation and Emerging Technology Exercise foresight in evaluating emerging AI, data and platform technologies, and act independently on self-initiated proofs of concept and technical experiments that challenge the status quo and shape the multi-year DQ technology roadmap. Take appropriate, well-governed technical risk, and translate proven experiments into scaled, supportable production capability with a defined adoption path. QUALIFICATIONS Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree required in Information Technology, Engineering, Environmental or Occupational Health Sciences, Life Sciences or a related discipline. 10+ years of relevant experience in in solution architecture, technical leadership or enterprise software delivery (9+ years with an MS/MBA; 7+ years with a PhD), including demonstrable accountability for architecture across a portfolio of products rather than a single application. Demonstrated experience designing and delivering AI or machine learning capability into production, including an understanding of large language model and agentic architecture patterns, retrieval, evaluation and model lifecycle management. Strong experience with cloud, integration and data architecture, and with modern software engineering and Agile ways of working; SAFe preferred. Experience setting and driving adoption of technical standards across teams that do not report to the incumbent, influencing senior stakeholders through technical credibility. Experience across all stages of the system and application lifecycle, from value analysis and business case through deployment to value realisation and technical debt management. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical trade-offs to non-technical senior leaders. Preferred Qualifications Experience in the pharmaceutical industry or another highly regulated manufacturing environment, including GxP computerised system validation and data integrity expectations (e.g. GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11, Annex 11). Working knowledge of quality, or EHS business processes and the platforms that support them (for example Veeva, LIMS, Cority). Experience deploying AI in a regulated context, including responsible AI governance, model risk assessment and human-in-the-loop design. Recognised architecture certification (e.g. TOGAF) or equivalent cloud architecture certification. Track record of external technical contribution — industry forums, working groups, publications or conference speaking. PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS Typical desk job; no specific physical or mental requirements beyond standard office work. NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS Occasional travel up to 20% Ability to work with colleagues virtually across different regions and time zones, including occasional out-of-hours working to support deployment go-lives and hypercare. ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIONSHIPS Reports into Pfizer Digital, PGS, Enabling Functions & Enterprise Platforms – Digital Quality Lead. Key internal relationships include Enterprise Architecture, the enterprise AI and Data organization, Cyber Security, Digital Compliance and Computerized System Validation, Legal and Privacy, and senior business stakeholders across Quality and EHS in Pfizer Global Supply. External: strategic software and AI vendors, cloud and platform providers, implementation and managed service partners, and relevant industry and regulatory technical forums. RESOURCES MANAGED Financial Accountability No direct budget ownership. Influences the architecture and technology decisions underpinning the Digital Quality portfolio representing approximately $10M of annual software, services and transformation investment, and is accountable for identifying reuse and rationalization opportunities that improve return on that investment Supervision Individual contributor with no direct reports. Provides technical direction and design authority to matrixed teams of product, engineering, data, validation and vendor resources across the Digital Quality portfolio, and mentors architects and senior engineers across the organization. Work Location Assignment: Hybrid Pfizer is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable equal employment opportunity legislation in each jurisdiction in which it operates. jobs.title: Platform & Solution Engineering Lead
jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY The Platform and Solution Engineering Lead owns the technical foundation on which the entire Digital Quality (DQ) portfolio is built, delivered and operated. Digital Quality delivers the solutions that transform Quality, Safety and Environmental Operations (QSEO) across Pfizer, and this role is accountable for the platforms, engineering capability and delivery pipelines that allow that portfolio to move at pace while remaining compliant, secure and supportable. The incumbent leads a global engineering organisation covering platform engineering, solution architecture and design, integration and data engineering, DevSecOps, environment and release management, and vendor delivery oversight. Accountability spans the full technology mix — Software as a Service (SaaS), commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and in-house developed solutions — ensuring each is engineered, integrated, validated and operated to a consistent standard rather than as isolated stacks. The role is the engineering counterpart to the DQ Solution Leads, who own product strategy and business outcomes, and to the Scaled AI and Solution Architect, who sets cross-portfolio architecture direction and standards; this role is accountable for making those standards real in code, configuration, pipelines and operations. It is also the principal point of alignment between Digital Quality and the wider enterprise technology landscape, including Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security, the enterprise AI and Data organisation, and central platform and infrastructure teams. The role is global in scope, spanning the PGS network, R&D, commercial markets and corporate locations. ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES Platform Engineering and Technical Foundation Own the strategy, engineering and lifecycle of the shared technical foundation for Digital Quality, including cloud footprint, runtime platforms, shared services, reusable components, developer tooling and non-production environments. Build the foundation as a product used by delivery teams across the portfolio, with defined service levels, roadmaps, adoption measures and a managed path for retiring legacy and duplicated technology. Solution Engineering Across SaaS, COTS and Custom Build Provide engineering leadership and design accountability across the full technology mix, establishing how SaaS platforms are configured and extended, how COTS products are deployed and integrated, and how in-house applications are designed, built and maintained. Ensure engineering rigour, supportability and consistent quality regardless of delivery model, and prevent unmanaged customisation that undermines upgradability and cost of ownership. Integration and Data Engineering Own the integration and data engineering layer connecting Digital Quality solutions to each other and to the wider Pfizer landscape, including manufacturing, laboratory, enterprise resource planning and enterprise data platforms. Establish reusable integration patterns, interfaces and data contracts, and ensure integrations are resilient, monitored, documented and compliant with data integrity requirements. DevSecOps, Release and Environment Management Define and run the engineering operating model for Digital Quality, covering source control, continuous integration and delivery pipelines, automated testing, security scanning, infrastructure as code, and environment and release management. Drive automation of validation and compliance evidence so that release frequency, deployment reliability and lead time improve without weakening GxP control. Own the release calendar and change governance across the portfolio, including coordination of platform vendor release cycles. Vendor and Managed Service Delivery Hold strategic technology vendors, systems integrators and managed service partners to account for engineering quality, delivery commitments, security posture and service performance. Shape sourcing strategy and the internal-versus-partner capability mix, define technical standards and acceptance criteria in statements of work, and manage capacity and demand across internal and external engineering teams. Enterprise Technology Alignment Act as the principal interface between Digital Quality and enterprise technology functions, ensuring DQ solutions adopt enterprise platforms, standards and services rather than building parallel capability. Influence enterprise roadmaps, standards and investment decisions on behalf of the QSEO domain, and represent Digital Quality in enterprise architecture, cyber security and technology governance forums. Organisational Leadership Lead, develop and grow a global engineering team of approximately 8–10 direct reports, spanning platform engineers, solution architects, integration and data engineers, DevSecOps and release specialists, alongside matrixed and contract resources. Build engineering capability, talent pipelines and succession plans; set technical performance expectations and career pathways; and foster a culture of engineering excellence, automation, innovation, accountability and continuous improvement across Digital Quality. Compliance, Risk and Governance Ensure the technical foundation and all solutions built on it are maintained in a validated and compliant state in accordance with GRC (Governance, Risk and Compliance) guidelines, computerised system validation expectations, data integrity, data privacy and cyber security requirements. Maintain audit and inspection readiness for engineering processes and evidence, support internal audits and regulatory inspections, and balance pace of innovation with regulatory compliance through effective governance and risk management. Demonstrated experience leading, hiring and developing engineering teams at scale, including matrix leadership of vendor and contract resources across multiple geographies. Deep hands-on grounding in cloud platform engineering, integration architecture and modern software engineering practice, with practical experience of CI/CD, infrastructure as code, automated testing and security-in-the-pipeline. Experience delivering and operating across SaaS, COTS and custom-developed solutions, including vendor platform configuration, extension and upgrade management. Strong experience with Agile ways of working; SAFe preferred. Knowledge of financial management and procurement activities, with the ability to manage complex budgets, vendor contracts and internal-versus-partner capacity decisions. Strong understanding of Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), Agentic AI architectures, and AI application development. Hands-on experience with LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI APIs, LangFuse, RAG frameworks, and prompt engineering. Experience building intelligent agent workflows, tool integrations, retrieval systems, and evaluation frameworks. Knowledge of semantic search, vector databases, embeddings, and enterprise AI architectures. Experience working with cloud platforms, preferably AWS, and modern data platforms. Hands-on experience building AI Skills, Agent Frameworks, and workflow orchestration platforms. Experience developing and integrating MCP servers and AI interoperability frameworks. jobs.title: Sr Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description: At Adobe, you will be immersed in an exceptional work environment that is recognized around the world. Adobe is listed as Fortune’s “100 Best Companies to Work For” for 20 consecutive years. You will also be surrounded by colleagues who are committed to helping each other grow. If you’re looking to make an impact, Adobe's the place for you. Discover what our employees are saying about their career experiences on the Adobe Life blog and explore the meaningful benefits we offer. Changing the world through digital experiences is what Adobe’s all about. We give global brands everything they need to design and deliver exceptional digital experiences. We’re passionate about transforming how companies interact with customers across every screen. The Opportunity Adobe Experience Platform and Apps powers real-time customer experiences for the world’s largest enterprises — unifying data, resolving identity at scale, orchestrating journeys, and activating audiences across channels. The Forward Deployed Engineer sits at the intersection of solution architecture, technical consulting, and hands-on engineering. You’ll work directly with Adobe’s strategic customers to solve complex platform challenges, design scalable architectures, and build solutions that accelerate adoption. You’ll operate in a multi-functional Customer Pod with end-to-end ownership, partnering with customers, product teams, and engineers to turn complex problems into working solutions. What You’ll Do Partner with strategic customers to understand their architecture, workflows, security requirements, and business objectives. Translate complex customer problems into scalable solution designs, reference architectures, and working prototypes. Investigate and resolve production-level platform issues across data ingestion, identity resolution, journey orchestration, and audience activation. Design and validate enterprise solutions spanning AEP, AJO, Marketo, and adjacent Adobe systems. Lead architecture workshops, health checks, and technical deep-dives that build customer trust. Prototype, experiment, and iterate rapidly, using AI-assisted tools as part of your everyday workflow. Connect customer needs with product and engineering teams, bringing field insights back into the product roadmap. Own the technical relationship with assigned accounts from discovery through implementation, launch, and expansion. What Success Looks Like We hire for demonstrated impact and experience. You’ll bring a combination of technical depth, customer empathy, and collaborative problem solving. Hands-on engineering: You write code, build prototypes, and ship working software. Your architecture decisions are grounded in implementation experience. Customer empathy: You understand customers’ goals, constraints, and definitions of success and build trusted relationships through empathy and technical expertise. Collaboration and communication: You work effectively with engineers, architects, product managers, and leaders and communicate complex concepts clearly to technical and non-technical audiences. Enterprise architecture: You design end-to-end solutions across products and systems, considering integration, scale, security, and production requirements. Data expertise: You understand how data is structured, modeled, and moved and can evaluate trade-offs in schema design, identity resolution, and data pipelines. AI fluency and continuous learning: You embrace AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent to design, prototype, and deliver solutions. Proactive problem solving: You identify emerging challenges and take initiative to move them toward resolution. What You Need to Succeed 10+ years of experience across solution architecture, software engineering, technical consulting, or customer-facing engineering. Bachelor’s or advanced degree in computer science or a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience. Experience with CDP, MDM, martech, or data platforms. Experience with data governance, privacy-preserving computation, or secure data collaboration. Familiarity with identity resolution or customer data unification. Experience with workflow orchestration technologies such as Temporal, Step Functions, or similar. Experience contributing to architecture decisions or technical strategy at the team or organizational level. Experience with Adobe Experience Cloud products such as AEP, AJO, Marketo, CJA, or Target is helpful. Experience working in regulated industries such as Financial Services, Healthcare, or Government is also helpful. Why This Team You’ll solve complex enterprise problems with direct customer impact and see your solutions reach production. You’ll combine architecture, engineering, strategy, and customer engagement while working with experienced engineers across Adobe’s global platform teams. You’ll also help shape an engineering engagement model centered on rapid experimentation, customer feedback, and AI-assisted execution. Come build the next generation of enterprise customer experiences with us! Adobe is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and encourage diversity in the workplace regardless of race, gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or veteran status. About Adobe Adobe empowers everyone to create through innovative platforms and tools that unleash creativity, productivity and personalized customer experiences. Adobe’s industry-leading offerings including Adobe Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Creative Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Experience Manager, and GenStudio enable people and businesses to turn ideas into impact, powered by AI and driven by human ingenuity. Our 30,000+ employees worldwide are creating the future and raising the bar as we drive the next decade of growth. We’re on a mission to hire the very best and believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. At Adobe, we believe that great ideas can come from anywhere in the organization. The next big idea could be yours. Let’s Adobe together At Adobe, we believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. Learn more about Adobe life, including our values and culture , focus on people, purpose and community , Adobe for All , comprehensive benefits programs , the stories we tell , the customers we serve, and how you can help us advance our mission of empowering everyone to create. Adobe is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on gender, race or color, ethnicity or national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Learn more. Adobe aims to make our Careers website and recruiting process accessible to any and all users. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation to navigate our website or complete the application process, email accommodations@adobe.com . AI Use Guidelines for Interviews: Our interviews are designed to reflect your own skills and thinking. The use of AI or recording tools during live interviews is not permitted unless explicitly invited by the interviewer or approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation. If these tools are used inappropriately or in a way that misrepresents your work, your application may not move forward in the process. At Adobe, we empower employees to innovate with AI — and we look for candidates eager to do the same. As part of the hiring experience, we provide clear guidance on where AI is encouraged during the process and where it’s restricted during live interviews. See how we think about AI in the hiring experience .

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Full Stack
jobs.description: In most instances, this position requires in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. 1 year of experience with software development in one or more programming languages (e.g., Python, C, C++, Java, JavaScript). 1 year of experience with full stack development, across the back-end such as Java, Python, Go, or C++ codebases, and front-end experience including JavaScript or TypeScript, HTML, CSS or equivalent. 1 year of experience with data structures and algorithms. Preferred qualifications: Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science or a related technical field. Experience developing accessible technologies. About the job Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward. With your technical expertise you will manage project priorities, deadlines, and deliverables. You will design, develop, test, deploy, maintain, and enhance software solutions.Google Play offers music, movies, books, apps and games for devices, powered by the cloud. It syncs across devices and on the web. As part of the Android and Mobile team, Googlers working on Google Play do everything from engineering our backend systems, to shaping product strategy, to forming great content partnerships. They make it possible for people to do things like buy an ebook or song on their Android phone, then have it instantly available on their laptop. The Google Play team enhances the Android ecosystem by giving developers and partners a premium store where they can reach millions of users. Responsibilities Write product or system development code. Review code developed by other developers and provide feedback to ensure best practices (e.g., style guidelines, checking code in, accuracy, testability, and efficiency). Contribute to existing documentation or educational content and adapt content based on product/program updates and user feedback. Triage product or system issues and debug/track/resolve by analyzing the sources of issues and the impact on hardware, network, or service operations and quality. jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Do you want to build machine learning and agentic-AI systems that analyze billions of dollars in transactions every day, and measure your impact in millions of dollars saved? In Amazon's Finance Technology group, we build the detection systems (machine learning, and increasingly agentic AI) that defend Amazon against theft, fraud, abuse, and waste across the supply chain, retail catalog, and corporate procurement. We turn terabytes of transaction, vendor, and operational data into real-time risk decisions: scoring payments as they happen, surfacing anomalous behavior, and uncovering collusion networks that span thousands of entities. We're now building the next generation of that platform around generative and agentic AI: multi-agent systems that discover fraud patterns directly from the raw data flowing through Amazon's businesses, working alongside domain experts to turn what they find into production detection logic. The result is a platform where new detection coverage comes not only from engineers, but from agents and the experts who know the fraud best, shipping in days instead of sprints. You'll build the agent tools, ML pipelines, services, and data infrastructure behind all of this, working with generative AI, large language models, and agent frameworks alongside the anomaly-detection, classification, and graph-modeling techniques they build on. You'll partner directly with applied scientists, fellow engineers, and finance operations teams, and you'll see your ideas reach production in weeks. If you want to apply advanced ML and agentic AI at Amazon scale, on systems with a direct, measurable financial impact, we'd love to talk. Key job responsibilities You will participate in the full software development lifecycle, from collaborating with customers and scientists on design, to building scalable, extensible systems that run in production. You will: Design and build ML pipelines that process terabytes of data and score billions of dollars in transactions. Build agentic AI applications: LLM-powered agents that discover risk patterns and generate detection logic, operating through well-defined tool interfaces with human-in-the-loop review. Build the knowledge and memory systems agents depend on: vector stores, knowledge graphs, the entity-risk layer for cross-entity collusion detection, and in-session and shared memory. Develop how we evaluate agent effectiveness in fraud detection, and turn analysts' ad-hoc investigation patterns into repeatable, templated workflows. Build the platform and tooling (governed data access, model deployment, and self-service rule authoring) that lets agents and non-engineers ship detection logic safely and fast. Take models and agents from prototype to reliable, real-time production systems, and work directly with internal customers to turn feedback into shipped improvements. A day in the life You'll partner with applied scientists, software engineers, and finance operations teams across Amazon. You'll harden an agent pipeline for production, extend the entity graph that powers a new detector, or design a tool interface that lets an agent query data safely, then review it with the customer who'll use it. Because our team and our customers are comfortable trying new ideas, you'll get your work in front of real data quickly and iterate on what you learn. About the team We own the machine learning and agentic-AI systems that prevent, recover, and avoid internal and external theft, fraud, abuse, and waste across Amazon Finance Operations. Our platform makes real-time risk decisions on transactions from many of Amazon's largest businesses. We're actively building toward entity-level risk profiles updated in real time, and agentic systems that compress fraud discovery and investigation from weeks to days, with engineers building the leverage layer that multiplies what every analyst and agent can do. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience Experience programming with at least one software programming language PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Experience in machine learning, data mining, information retrieval, statistics or natural language processing Experience in processing data with a massively parallel technology (such as Redshift, Teradata, Netezza, Spark or Hadoop based big data solution) Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer II, UTR Tech, UTR Tech
jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Amazon’s global fulfilment network enables any merchant in any of the geography ship items that you order on Amazon, to any place on earth. Amazon Logistics’ (AMZL) delivery stations (DS) receive packages from Fulfilment Centers (FCs) and Sort Centers (SCs) and sort them to route level. Drivers come into the DS and pick up the packages for their route and deliver them to Amazon’s customers. This operation is also called the “Last Mile”. An integral component in the Last Mile ecosystem are Amazon's WW delivery hubs where packages are received, sorted and prepared for on-road delivery. Station Tech team, in Last Mile, is responsible for building scalable tools and technology for delivery hubs that scale across multiple programs and businesses including Amazon Logistics (AMZL), Global Specialty Fulfilment (GSF), to increase associate productivity, site throughput, and operational quality and scalability of our delivery network. Our primary customers are delivery station associates (our actual on-ground rockstars who sort millions of packages a day), station managers (who manage Amazon hubs WW to ensure customer promises are met), COs (central operations team who supervise stations across regions) and on-road delivery agents (drivers who sail through all obstacles to get your packages at your doorstep). The team build tools and process which guide our customers to reduce their cognitive load, eliminate decision points to drive standardisation, prioritise work to focus on the highest impact tasks, and take steps for correcting operational defects to reduce the impact of human error and meet our customer SLAs. UTR Tech is an organisation within Last Mile supporting all the delivery stations in the delivery network. A delivery station receives an input set of packages from upstream and performs the required set of operations and processes on the packages to ultimately get them out of the delivery stations for on-road delivery. The associates within the delivery stations use a mobile based application called Dolphin for running the execution operations. As an SDE II on the UTR Tech team, you'll build and scale the systems powering Amazon's fastest delivery promises - Same-Day Delivery (SSD), Grocery, and Rush (1-hr/3-hr) programs across NA, EU, JP, and the Middle East. You'll own services spanning package injection, staging, sortation, and routing that keep millions of time-critical orders on-time, and directly move quality metrics like slot-level DEA and defect BPS. This role blends deep technical ownership with high operational impact: your code runs in a live, sub-hour delivery network where reliability and latency are non-negotiable. jobs.description: About the role and team At Uber, AI agents are increasingly writing, reviewing, testing, and debugging code in production. The AI Context Engineering team builds the context foundation that every software-development AI agent at Uber relies on: AI Context Graph: a unified graph of services, ownership, domain entities, and business flows Code Graph: a graph representation of Uber's monorepos built for agents to consume AI-Generated Documentation: documentation that stays fresh as code changes Agentic Memory: a memory layer that lets agents learn across sessions As a Senior Software Engineer, you will own major parts of this platform end to end. You'll take them from prototype to production at monorepo scale, and work with partner teams to integrate foundational context products with the agents running in production for workflows such as root-cause analysis, code authoring, test planning, and library upgrades, etc What will you do Context Graph and Ontology: Enrich the graph with new entity types, such as data streams, metrics, and observability signals, and link them to code so agents can reason across systems. Code Graph Infrastructure: Build and scale code graphs across multiple monorepos and microrepos, covering symbols, call edges, dependencies, and links between code and tests. Add incremental updates, versioned (historical) graphs, and function-level embeddings, and serve the graphs to agents with low latency through local and remote interfaces. AI-Generated Documentation: Extend automated documentation from backend services to mobile (screens, UI components), libraries, and data pipelines. Use refresh strategies that keep context current as code changes. Agentic Memory: Design the memory layer that lets agents persist and reuse decisions, past fixes, and team preferences across sessions. Standards and Governance: Define and roll out standards for agent instruction files (AGENTS.md), including structure, content, and token budget, and generate them systematically across modules. Context Quality Evaluation: Build continuous evals that measure the accuracy and freshness of every context product, and run A/B experiments that prove the impact on agent outcomes. Tooling and Integration: Build MCP servers, skills, and tools that deliver context to agents. Partner with AI Platform, Developer Experience, and product teams to integrate them into production workflows. Technical Leadership: Drive design reviews, mentor engineers, and turn ambiguous problems into well-scoped, measurable projects What will you need Experience: 8+ years of software engineering experience building production systems, with a degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Programming: Strong in Go, Java, or Python, writing clean, well-tested, maintainable code. LLMs and Agentic Systems: Hands-on experience building with LLMs and agents, including prompt and context design, tool use, and retrieval, and a good sense of what context makes agents succeed or fail. Code Understanding: Experience with static analysis, ASTs, parsers such as tree-sitter, or build and dependency systems in large codebases. Data at Scale: Experience building reliable data pipelines and working with graph or other large-scale data stores. Emerging Protocols: Familiarity with MCP and agent-to-agent protocols and how to apply them. Problem Solving: Strong analytical skills and a habit of measuring outcomes, not just shipping features. Context coverage grows across languages, repos, and entity types, with measurable accuracy and freshness. Bonus Points If you have Graph Databases: Experience with Neo4j or similar graph databases, including query optimization and schema design. Embeddings and RAG: Experience with embedding generation, vector databases, and retrieval pipelines. Evaluation: Experience designing LLM evals, LLM-as-judge methods, or A/B experiments for AI systems. Developer Platforms: Experience in developer tooling, CI, or monorepo infrastructure. Observability: Experience with Prometheus, Grafana, Langfuse, or similar tools for monitoring AI systems. Ready to Ride? What differentiates Tech@Lilly is that we create new possibilities through tech to advance our purpose – creating medicines that make life better for people around the world, like data driven drug discovery and connected clinical trials. We hire the best technology professionals from a variety of backgrounds, so they can bring an assortment of knowledge, skills, and diverse thinking to deliver innovative solutions in every area of the enterprise. About the Business Function: The Tech@Lilly Digital Office (DO) and Global Services (GS) team leads digitalization across organizations spanning the enterprise with Finance, Legal, Ethics & Compliance, Corporate Affairs and Human Resources as well delivers best-in-class ERP Solutions. This team leverages technology and analytics to enable transformations across the enterprise. Job Title: Senior Consultant - Validation As a Senior Consultant - Validation, you will be responsible for driving Computer System Validation (CSV)/Computer Software Assurance (CSA) activities, ensuring compliance, quality, and efficiency across Lilly computer systems following Lilly standards and processes. You also will be responsible to drive innovation by leveraging AI, digital tools, and automation to simplify and automate CSV processes. About the team: Validation - Center of Excellence (CoE) is a specialized team that provides CSV services across all Tech@Lilly business functions. We adopt a modern, enterprise-wide approach that emphasizes automation and simplification, ensuring validation activities are consistent, effective, and aligned with industry best practices and regulations. The DO/GS organization is actively looking for a motivated candidate. In this role, you will be responsible for driving IT quality & compliance, and assurance across Lilly’s mission-critical systems spanning across various business functions. Do you have a passion for shaping the future of validation by embracing modern approaches like use of AI and Automation in validation? If so, please apply. What you’ll be doing: Innovation & Automation: Drive innovation in validation by exploring and leveraging AI, digital tools, and automation technologies to streamline validation documentation, authoring, and review processes. Identify opportunities to simplify CSV/CSA activities through adoption of risk-based approaches, automation frameworks, and smart documentation solutions, reducing effort while maintaining compliance. Continuously evaluate emerging technologies (e.g., AI-assisted authoring, digital validation platforms) and recommend practical use cases for efficiency and quality improvement. Identify and drive continuous improvement, automation, and simplification opportunities in validation processes using digital tools or AI-enabled solutions. Project Validation: Lead and coordinate IT system validation by managing the computer system lifecycle from validation/test planning to reporting and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, Lilly processes and validation standards. Responsible for applying appropriate right sizing method/approach and determining the nature and content of deliverables in scope. Oversee AI/auto generated validation documents by reviewing and updating contents to ensure accuracy, compliance, and alignment with Lilly’s quality management system. Review all the project validation deliverables authored by the project team (developer, SME etc.). Escalate and communicate operational issues, critical compliance findings and risks to the Information System Quality (ISQ) organization and other key stakeholders of the system. Educate project team members on Lilly IT processes and methodologies. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify and mitigate compliance risks, while providing guidance and training on best practices and regulatory requirements. Advise project team on implementation of compliance and security control requirements at the appropriate stages of system development. Contribute to internal and external audits, assessments or inspections. Change Management: Ensures IT system change requests (CR) are executed in compliance with Local/global change control procedures. Review CRs and ensure the accuracy and completeness of all change requests. Review the impacted validation deliverables. Access Roster, Privacy and Periodic Review: Facilitate and support the system custodian/owner and area management to execute access roster and periodic review followed by respective Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) closure. How You Will Succeed: Achieving measurable improvements in validation efficiency (e.g., reduced cycle time, higher CSA adoption, increased compliance). Contributing to continuous improvement for documentation and validation processes for functional areas. Promoting simplification and harmonization across systems and geographies. Mentoring and coaching junior validation staff, foster a quality culture across teams. Driving CSA adoption to simplify and modernize CSV, focusing on risk-based assurance rather than excessive documentation. What You should Bring: In-depth knowledge of regulations, guidelines, and industry standards related to CSV, data integrity, and computerized systems like GxP, GAMP 5, FDA 21 CFR Part 820, 21 CFR 210, 21 CFR 211, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, ALCOA++ Principles, etc. Experience in leading CSV activities across the full system lifecycle (implementation, upgrades, retirement). Expertise in documents creation which includes, but not limited to validation plan, System Configuration, System Overview, Security Plan and validation report, etc. Hands-on expertise in preparing, reviewing, and approving validation deliverables. Strong knowledge of IT system operational compliance processes, including Periodic Reviews and Access Roster Reviews. Proven ability to apply risk-based validation approaches in alignment with CSA principles to balance compliance with efficiency. Hands-on experience with commonly used industry tools (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow, Veeva). Tool-use & integration contracts: design tool/function-calling architectures and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration layers, enforcing clean, decoupled contracts between agents, MCP servers, and downstream APIs. Agent lifecycle governance: define registration, configuration, versioning, deprecation, and runtime governance for agents, applying policy-as-code and identity-as-code across design-time and runtime. Agent security: design defences specific to autonomous systems — prompt-injection mitigation, least-privilege tool-permission scoping, execution sandboxing, and input/output validation across the agent–tool boundary. jobs.title: Senior Network Developer
jobs.description: We are the AI Infrastructure - Network Operations team at OCI (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure). We support and operate the RDMA/RoCE/InfiniBand network fabrics for OCI's largest AI and HPC customers. These fabrics are the foundation underneath OCI's AI, GPU and HPC services, and support major tier-0 vendors in the generative AI industry. If you're running an AI workload at OCI, we're running the RDMA network underneath your workload. A Network Operations Engineer on our team supports the design, deployment, and operations of a large-scale global Oracle cloud computing environment (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure - OCI). Primarily focused on operation and support of RDMA/RoCE/InfiniBand network fabrics and systems, through a combination of a deep network understanding and automation skills to operate a production environment. As OCI is a cloud-based network with a global footprint, this support will include hundreds of thousands of network devices supporting millions of servers, connected over a mix of dedicated backbone infrastructure and the Internet. Key Responsibilities Design, operate, validate, and scale advanced network fabrics for large-scale cloud, AI, and data center environments. Develop automation, scripts, and tooling to streamline network testing, operations, deployment, and troubleshooting. Build and enhance telemetry, dashboards, alerting, and monitoring to improve network health, reliability, and SLO performance. Develop test strategies, lead pre-production validation, and drive root cause analysis (RCA) for network issues and changes. jobs.title: Deputy Director - AI Solution and Platforms
jobs.description: Overview: The AI Solution Engineer is a delivery focused engineer who designs, builds, and operates production agentic AI applications, along with the platform services those applications run on. Working within the technical direction set by AI Solutions and Platforms leadership, the AI Solution Engineer translates solution architecture into production grade agents, retrieval pipelines, tool and system integrations, evaluation harnesses, and the guardrails and observability that keep those systems reliable once live. The AI Solution Engineer is a hands on practitioner who codes, integrates, tests, and iterates, owning feature level delivery across one or more solution or platform tracks while building a working understanding of the wider AI platform. The role works daily with modern AI engineering tooling, including agentic frameworks such as LangChain and LangGraph, the Model Context Protocol, and coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and Codex. This is a technical builder first, with a growing architect mindset Responsibilities: Responsibilities Solution Architecture and Delivery: Architect, build and deploy production agentic AI applications for R&D, taking them from problem definition and prototype through to production use by scientists and engineers. Hands On Engineering: Write production Python and own the difficult parts, including retrieval quality, tool and function design, multi agent orchestration, context management, structured outputs, latency and unit cost. Set the technical bar through design and code review. Agentic Framework Selection: Build with LangChain, LangGraph, MCP and agent to agent patterns. Select the appropriate model across Anthropic Claude, Azure OpenAI and Google model families, and recognise when a deterministic or classical machine learning approach is the correct answer. Evaluation and Quality: Establish evaluation as a delivery gate, covering golden datasets built with R&D subject matter experts, automated evaluations in CI, regression and grounded Ness testing, red teaming, and human review in the loop. Take solutions from prototype into production and remain accountable for them once live. Platform Ownership: Own the shared AI platform for R&D, including retrieval and vector infrastructure, agent runtime, prompt and model registry, MCP server and connector layer, guardrails, tracing and observability, cost attribution and rate management. Define reference architectures and reusable patterns so that downstream teams ship in weeks rather than quarters. MLOps and LLMOps: Embed CI/CD for models, prompts and agents, infrastructure as code, environment promotion, versioning, monitoring, incident response, model deprecation and migration. Enterprise Integration: Integrate AI solutions with the R&D and enterprise estate, including PLM, LIMS, specification and document management systems, SAP, the Azure data platform and the enterprise Lakehouse. Security and Governance: Own security, privacy and governance for these systems in partnership with Cyber, Legal, Privacy and Responsible AI, covering access control, secrets management, handling of confidential formulation and specification data, and auditability. Contribute to AI governance standards for R&D. People Leadership: Lead, coach and grow a team of AI and platform engineers. Develop technical depth in the team and build AI literacy across the wider R&D community. Stakeholder Partnership: Partner with R&D scientists, category and platform leaders to convert ambiguous scientific problems into scoped, valuable products, and to decline those that will not work. Manage delivery partners and vendors. Communicate credibly with a food scientist and a cloud architect in the same conversation, and with senior leadership on portfolio, risk and value. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Engineering, Data Science or a related quantitative field. Masters preferred. 10 to 14 years in software, data or machine learning engineering, including at least 2 to 3 years building and running LLM and generative AI solutions in production. 2 or more years leading engineers, formally or as a senior technical lead, with evidence of having developed people. Strong hands-on Python. Code quality will be assessed during the interview process. Deep practical experience with agentic AI, covering tool calling, planning, memory, multi agent and agent to agent patterns, retrieval augmented generation, structured output, guardrails and evaluation. Production experience with LangChain and LangGraph, or an equivalent framework such as LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, CrewAI, Pydantic AI or custom orchestration, with a clear view of the tradeoffs. Daily working use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex or Cursor, including agent configuration and custom tooling rather than inline completion alone. Solid understanding of LLM fundamentals, including context windows, embeddings, tokenization, fine tuning versus adapters versus prompting, and failure modes such as hallucination and prompt injection. Cloud and platform engineering experience. Azure preferred, covering Azure OpenAI or AI Foundry, AKS and Functions, or the equivalent on AWS or GCP. Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform or Bicep, CI/CD and API design. Data foundations, including SQL, Spark or Databricks, vector stores, and real experience working with messy unstructured technical documents. Overview (Secondary Language): Prior delivery of technology for an R&D, scientific or laboratory function in CPG, food and beverage, pharma, chemicals, flavors and fragrances, agriculture or materials science. Working familiarity with scientific and product data, including formulations and recipes, technical specifications, bills of materials, ingredient masters, sensory panel data, nutrition and claims data, and stability datasets. Experience with R&D systems of record such as PLM, LIMS or ELN, and with specification and technical document management. Track record of taking agentic systems past pilot into sustained production use, with adoption and reliability data to evidence it. Experience building MCP servers and custom tool layers over enterprise APIs and internal systems. Retrieval engineering depth beyond baseline RAG, including hybrid and semantic search, reranking, chunking strategy for technical documents, and table and figure extraction. Databricks at production scale, including Unity Catalog, Delta and Lakehouse patterns. LLM cost engineering, including token accounting, caching, batching, routing across model tiers and chargeback to business units. Experience building internal developer platforms or shared services consumed by other engineering teams. Exposure to Responsible AI frameworks, AI model risk management, or EU AI Act readiness and comparable emerging regulation. Experience handling commercially sensitive or trade secret data, including how intellectual property is protected when third party models sit in the processing path. Experience in a global capability center delivering for global stakeholders across time zones, where the hub owned outcomes rather than executed tickets. Having hired, levelled and grown AI or platform engineers in the Indian market. A postgraduate qualification in Computer Science, Engineering or Data Science, or in a scientific discipline relevant to food, chemistry, materials or nutrition. Candidates who moved from science into engineering are of particular interest. Recognized AI engineering credentials, for example Anthropic's Claude Certified Developer Foundations or Claude Certified Architect exams, GitHub Copilot certification, or Microsoft, AWS or Google AI engineering certifications. Equivalent demonstrated experience is weighted equally. Open-source contributions to agent or LLM tooling, conference talks, published papers or technical writing.

jobs.title: Director
jobs.description: About Rubrik Rubrik is one of the fastest-growing companies in Silicon Valley, revolutionizing data protection, and management in the emerging multi-cloud world. We are the leader in cloud data management, delivering a single platform to manage and protect data in the cloud, at the edge, and on-premises. Enterprises choose Rubrik to simplify backup and recovery, accelerate cloud adoption, enable automation at scale, and secure against cyber threats. We’ve been recognized as a Forbes Cloud 100 Company two years in a row and as a LinkedIn Top 10 startup. Rubrik provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, Rubrik complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. Job Introduction Corporate IT has traditionally been measured by how well it works a queue: tickets raised, tickets closed, SLAs met. That era is ending. Automating a ticket only makes a broken model faster. We want to remove the ticket. We are hiring a Director of Corporate IT to lead Employee Experience globally at Rubrik and rebuild it with AI at the center. The goal is ticketless service: from hire to retirement, an employee’s access, devices, tools, and answers arrive before they have to ask. Our north star is “My Digital Twin”, an agentic layer carrying an employee’s full context alongside the organization’s memory: role, team, entitlements, assets, policy, and history. A system with that context does not need a form. It provisions, anticipates, explains, and repairs. This is a multi-year journey, starting from a real environment that thousands of employees depend on daily. You will own both halves: run the global service organization at a high standard today, and dismantle the parts of it that AI should replace tomorrow. Neither can slip. The team you will lead spans the US, India, and other regions, and the employees you serve are spread across every Rubrik site. The role is based onsite in Bangalore and forms part of the onsite management team there, while the mandate, the standards you set, and the roadmap you own are global. The environment A globally distributed estate: Windows, macOS, and Linux endpoints, virtual desktops, conference rooms across sites in multiple regions, and a broad portfolio of third-party SaaS and open source applications. Collaboration and identity tools: Google Workspace, Okta, Slack, etc. Endpoint and MDM: VMware Workspace ONE, Jamf, Microsoft Intune, etc. VDI and remote desktop environments AV and conferencing: Google Meet, Zoom, room systems, digital signage, event production ITSM: Atlassian (Jira Cloud, Confluence, Opsgenie, Jira Service Management) Public cloud provider environments: GCP, Azure, AWS, etc. Enterprise AI: Claude Code and Claude Cowork, Glean, and other LLM and agent platforms and others What you will be doing Run the business: operational excellence today Own the global end-user service portfolio: Tech Lounge, ticketing, email and Slack support channels, escalations, and reporting, delivered consistently across regions and time zones. Own endpoint device management and client systems engineering across Windows, macOS, and Linux, the VDI estate, and AV and conferencing technology including room reliability and all-hands production. Own administration, governance, and adoption of enterprise AI tooling for employees. Hire, develop, and coach a globally distributed team of support staff and systems engineers across the US, India, and other locations, and grow site and functional leaders under you. Set one global service standard while respecting local needs: follow-the-sun coverage, consistent tooling and policy, shared knowledge, and a single escalation model across sites. Run IT service management to established practice (for example ITIL), own office-wide communications for incidents, outages, and changes, and keep a continual improvement focus across every technology area. Own the procurement forecast and vendor relationships for corporate and end-user IT globally, including India, partner with Information Security on identity, endpoint, and access, and carry IT-managed systems through SOC 2, SOX, and PCI audits. Represent operations in cross-functional programs under the Global IT Strategy & Operations pillar, spanning Global Service Desk, IT Supply Chain, AVOps, and InfraOps. Change the business: build toward ticketless Own the global ticketless roadmap: a multi-year sequence with milestones that can be measured and defended, and a rollout sequence across regions rather than a pilot that never leaves one site. Re-architect hire-to-retire as event-driven rather than request-driven, so joiner, mover, and leaver events trigger provisioning, entitlements, device readiness, and access removal with no human in the loop. Build the organizational memory that “My Digital Twin” depends on: a trustworthy graph of people, roles, entitlements, assets, policies, and history, with data quality good enough for autonomous action. Deploy AI agents against the biggest sources of employee friction and redesign the service catalog around intent instead of forms, holding agents to resolution rather than deflection. Set the guardrails for autonomous IT: identity-aware authorization for agents, least privilege, human approval where it genuinely matters, and audit trails. Move the measurement model from SLAs to experience outcomes, and redeploy your team as automation lands into automation engineering, knowledge ownership, and experience design. What we are looking for Leadership and operating track record Experience leading corporate IT, end-user services, or workplace technology at global scale, including managing managers and senior technical staff in more than one region. A track record of running a demanding environment well while changing it. We will ask for specifics on both. Fluency with AI and automation applied to operations: agents, workflow orchestration, integration across identity and ITSM systems, retrieval over internal knowledge. You need to know what is achievable, what is hype, and where the failure modes are. Hands-on depth in endpoint device management and client systems engineering across Windows, macOS, and Linux, MDM platforms, VDI, and AV and conferencing across multiple sites. Depth in identity and access (Okta or equivalent), SaaS administration, and public cloud environments. Practical experience putting enterprise AI tools in employees’ hands at scale, beyond pilots. Vendor management and procurement, plus IT technical program management with globally distributed teams, and the working habits that make distributed leadership effective across time zones. Executive presence and influence in a matrix organization, with the ability to develop senior leaders and build a culture of integrity, service excellence, accountability, and best practice sharing across sites. Security and compliance are treated as design constraints rather than obstacles, with exposure to SOC 2, SOX, or PCI cycles . AI-native depth, in a CorpIT context Demonstrated hands-on fluency with current generative AI tools, and the judgment to know where they help and where they don’t. Experience with AI-powered digital employee experience management platforms and endpoint telemetry, used to fix problems before employees report them. jobs.title: Senior User Experience Designer II
