Our 135,000+ employees thrive in more than 100 countries. From the simplest of switches to complex operational systems, our technology, software and services improve the way our customers manage and automate their operations. As a Senior User Experience Designer II, you create innovative, user-centric designs that enhance product usability and elevate user satisfaction. You conduct thorough user research, develop wireframes and prototypes, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to refine and optimize designs. You lead usability testing efforts and incorporate user feedback to drive continuous improvement in design quality. Your mission is to enhance the overall user experience by crafting intuitive and enjoyable interfaces that align with user needs and business goals. Your work plays a critical role in driving product success by ensuring that designs are both effective and user-focused. You are a specialized contributor with advanced expertise in user experience design, concentrating on the technical aspects of interface creation and user research. You leverage your skills to tackle complex design challenges and develop innovative solutions. You apply moderate to advanced technical knowledge of UX design, delivering impactful results with direct influence on product outcomes. You independently make decisions about your work and priorities, often navigating ambiguous situations, with decisions guided by past experiences, established practices, and organizational procedures. You set your work priorities autonomously and provide guidance to other professionals when needed. Your work requires minimal supervision, and you actively seek guidance in challenging situations. What do you get to do in this position? As part of the Schneider Electric design organization, every team member is responsible for representing and upholding these core competencies: User-centered design. Apply the tools and methodologies the problem, timing, and context require. Be transparent and mentor colleagues across every stage of the design process. Facilitation and co-design. Prepare and lead workshops to align teams and converge on a common product and service vision. Include others and motivate with curiosity, a constant interest to learn, and a default to doing. Culture and advocacy. Be a representative of design and a user advocate within Schneider Electric. Promote our digital ecosystem, strengthen the brand, and form a unified experience. Systems thinking. Expand and adjust perspectives to understand the problem space. Empathize with users and colleagues and appreciate a diversity of inputs. Find cohesion across areas of the business for our users. Data driven. Know how to use and analyze qualitative and quantitative data in decision making. Design interactions that empower users with information and collect data as a natural part of the experience. As part of specifically being a Senior User Experience Designer II, you will be responsible for these additional competencies: AI-assisted design. Use generative AI tools fluently to explore concepts and scaffold prototypes, then refine AI-generated mockups and HTML/React output — resolving UX issues, aligning to the design system, and bringing them to enterprise-grade quality. Accelerate concept generation without substituting AI for user insight. Requirements translation. Convert ambiguous requirements into low-fidelity wireframes, user flows, and journey maps that surface gaps and misalignments before development starts. Facilitate working sessions that move stakeholders from assumptions to documented, testable requirements. Design execution. Own the full design workflow in Figma from rough concept to pixel-precise, developer-ready specs. Work within and contribute to the Quartz Design System, and maintain design artifacts as a living record across the product lifecycle. Design documentation. Produce annotated documentation a development team can build from independently — interaction states, edge cases, error handling, and component behavior fully specified. Your files should be navigable by a developer who has never met you. Concept testing and risk reduction. Establish a regular cadence of lightweight concept testing with real users to validate direction early and reduce the cost of course corrections downstream. Synthesize findings and communicate them clearly to stakeholders who may be new to incorporating user feedback. Human-centered culture. Model what good design review, critique, and iteration look like. Help the team build user-centered habits pragmatically, without heavy process, and connect to the broader Schneider Electric UX community to bring best practices back to the team. jobs.description: About the Role Adobe is seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join the Adobe Genuine Engineering team. This group protects Adobe's ecosystem from fraud, abuse, and misuse using intelligent systems worldwide. In this position, you will build and develop machine learning models from scratch, including custom transformer-based frameworks, to identify fraudulent actions, stop account sharing, and protect the experience of hundreds of millions of users. You will manage the entire model lifecycle: raw behavioral data and feature engineering, architecture development, large-scale GPU training, deployment, and monitoring. The team is actively building in-house behavioral foundation models that learn identity-preserving representations from long sequences of user activity. This is a role for an engineer who wants to own deep learning systems end-to-end — not consume pre-built ones. Key Responsibilities Build and train deep learning models from scratch, including custom transformer and attention-based architectures for long behavioral event sequences. Own the full training stack: event tokenization, temporal and positional embeddings, self-supervised pretraining (e.g., masked modeling, contrastive learning), and downstream fine-tuning. Train large models efficiently on GPU infrastructure using mixed-precision training, gradient accumulation/checkpointing, efficient attention, and distributed strategies (DDP, FSDP, or equivalent). Build and optimize feature pipelines on Databricks and Spark, transforming raw behavioral events into high-quality model inputs. Translate prototypes into production ML systems — scalable, reliable, and observable — and drive inference performance through architectural and serving-side optimization. Contribute to MLOps practices: experiment tracking, model versioning, CI/CD, automated retraining, and production monitoring. Collaborate cross-functionally with data science, product, and platform teams; mentor junior engineers on experimentation rigor, deployment process, and responsible AI. Stay current with advances in ML/AI and bring relevant innovations into Adobe's products. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, or related field. 5+ years of professional experience building and deploying ML solutions at scale. Strong programming expertise in Python, with hands-on experience in PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar frameworks. Deep understanding of the end-to-end ML lifecycle—from data collection to deployment and monitoring. Strong grasp of model optimization, inference efficiency, and production system integration. Forward Deployed Engineer, Applied AI Genpact • AI Value Studio • Reports into an Applied AI Lead About the Role As a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) on Genpact's Applied AI team, you will embed directly with our most strategic enterprise customers to ship production AI applications that solve real business problems. You will spend most of your week in Claude Code and at the client, turning ambiguous business problems into working software often within days, not months. This is the role at the front line of how the world's largest companies actually adopt AI. You will own a workstream end-to-end: sitting with client teams to understand their workflows, designing the solution, building it, demoing it, and getting it into production. You will collaborate closely with Anthropic, our other AI partners, and Genpact's industry and delivery teams to make sure what you build lasts after you leave. We expect our FDEs to operate autonomously, thrive in ambiguity, and represent Genpact at the highest level inside customer environments. What You Will Do Work inside customer systems to build production applications with Claude and other frontier models, making sure they meet real customer requirements. Deliver technical artifacts: agentic workflows, MCP servers, sub-agents, agent skills, evaluation harnesses, and the integrations that wire them into the client's stack. Own a workstream end-to-end — discovery, architecture, build, demo, handoff. Make trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality in real time. Co-design solutions with client stakeholders at the Director and VP level. Sit in the client's room, take direction, and turn it into shipped code by the end of the day. Provide white-glove deployment support inside enterprise environments. Be the person the client trusts when something has to work. Identify and codify repeatable deployment patterns. Contribute reusable assets — code, prompts, skills, runbooks, reference implementations — back to the Genpact Applied AI practice. Stay current with the latest in LLM capabilities, agent frameworks, and the AI product development stack. Bring field insights back to our product and partner teams. What We Are Looking For 4+ years in a technical, customer-facing role — Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Solutions Architect, or software engineer with consulting experience. Former technical founders are strongly encouraged to apply. Daily, hands-on working fluency with Claude (or a comparable frontier LLM) as a build tool — not as a chatbot. You use it to ship every day. Production experience with LLMs: advanced prompt engineering, agent development, evaluation frameworks, and deployment at scale. Strong programming skills in Python and, ideally, one or more of TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, or SQL. Experience shipping production applications. Track record of shipping something a customer or end-user actually paid for, used, or measured — a product, an internal tool, a notable open-source project, or a demo that closed a deal. Can hold your own in a client conversation with senior stakeholders. You do not need a PM to translate. High agency — comfortable navigating ambiguity in complex organizations and turning vague business problems into concrete technical plans. High cooperation mindset — you can balance competing priorities across customer teams, Genpact delivery, and partners with integrity. Bonus Domain depth in a regulated industry: life sciences, financial services, healthcare, insurance. Hands-on experience with MCP, agent frameworks (Claude Code, Cursor, LangGraph, etc.), evaluation tooling, or LLM observability. Background in a top-tier product, startup, frontier-lab, or consulting environment — or a credible self-built equivalent. Experience operating in hybrid onshore/offshore delivery teams. Familiarity with security, privacy, and compliance considerations for enterprise AI deployment. What We Are Not Requiring A specific degree. No degree requirement, no preference for any particular institution. Specific certifications. The bar is the work, not the credentials. Anthropic, AWS, or other AI certifications are nice to have, not required. A traditional ML or PhD background. We are hiring builders who use LLMs, not researchers who train them. Interview Process Our process is designed to evaluate the work, not the resume: Initial conversation with the hiring manager (45 min). Portfolio walkthrough — bring something you built recently with Claude or a comparable model and walk us through how you built it (45 min). Live build exercise — a 90-minute pair-build or take-home on a realistic client problem using Claude. Highest-signal step in our process. Client simulation — a working session with Genpact senior delivery and a simulated client stakeholder. Final conversations with practice leadership. Location and Travel US-based with hybrid working model. 25–50% travel to client sites and Genpact delivery centers.

jobs.title: GPU Software Development Engineer
jobs.description:
Experience range: 5-10 Yrs
Job Details: Job Description: The Role and Impact: As a GPU Software Development Engineer, you will focus on enabling and optimizing Intel's GPUs by developing, backporting, and validating software solutions that span the stack-from firmware and device drivers to APIs and the application layer. You will play a critical role in designing, debugging, and improving GPU kernel drivers and graphics software on Linux platforms across diverse kernel environments and enterprise distributions, ensuring seamless integration and performance. Your contributions will directly support Intel's innovations in graphics and data center technologies. Business Group: The Data Center Group (DCG) drives Intel's leadership in computing innovation, with a focus on delivering high-performance solutions for data-centric markets. This group develops technologies that power advanced workloads in cloud computing, AI, and graphics acceleration. By joining DCG, you'll collaborate with experts dedicated to enabling cutting-edge GPU solutions that advance Intel's broader mission to shape the future of technology. Key Responsibilities: Develop and validate GPU kernel drivers and graphics software solutions, contributing to the full development lifecycle from design and implementation to testing and release across Linux platforms, including contributions to the open-source graphics software community where applicable. Debug, optimize, and enable Linux DRM/KMD drivers - including root cause analysis of kernel panics, regressions, deadlocks, race conditions, and memory corruption across diverse hardware and software environments. Design and implement new driver features, enhancements, and optimizations within the Linux DRM/KMD subsystem, collaborating closely with hardware and firmware teams to enable new GPU capabilities. Adapt and backport upstream Intel GPU drivers (DRM/KMD) to LTS, enterprise, and customized customer kernel environments, designing and maintaining compatibility layers and out-of-tree packaging solutions such as DKMS. Collaborate with cross-functional teams - spanning firmware, KMD, user-space runtime, and compute/graphics stacks - to ensure robust integration, compatibility, and stability across the full GPU software stack. Partner with validation and DevOps teams to expand multi-kernel test matrices, regression suites, and automated build pipelines that catch compatibility breaks early. Ensure high code quality and adherence to Linux kernel coding standards through active participation in design and code reviews, spanning both upstream driver development and backported driver deliverables. Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electronics/Electrical Engineering. 5+ years of hands-on experience in large-scale software product development with deep focus on Linux kernel and system software engineering. Expert-level C programming with deep understanding of Linux kernel internals, driver architecture, memory management, concurrency, locking primitives, and interrupt handling. Proven experience developing and debugging Linux DRM/KMD drivers and device driver debugging mechanisms. Hands-on experience backporting Linux kernel patches and drivers across kernel versions, with practical understanding of kernel API/ABI drift and compatibility wrapper construction. Proficiency in Linux kernel debugging tools such as ftrace, perf, kdump/crash, kgdb, GDB, dynamic debug, and interpreting stack traces and lockdep reports. Preferred Qualifications: Master's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electronics/Electrical Engineering. Deep experience with Linux DRM/KMS subsystem, GPU memory management (TTM, GEM), DMA-BUF, and modern graphics/compute software stacks. Experience with out-of-tree module frameworks (DKMS, Kbuild backport frameworks) and multi-kernel distribution packaging (RPM, DEB). Experience triaging and resolving kernel regressions caused by upstream changes in core subsystems such as schedulers, memory allocators, power management, and PCIe buses. Experience supporting customer-specific or enterprise Linux distributions such as RHEL, SLES, or Ubuntu LTS, including kernel validation and issue resolution in production environments. Active patch submissions or contributions to the open-source Linux kernel or DRM/graphics community. Join us to work on impactful projects that shape the future of GPU technology and advance Intel's mission of delivering world-changing innovations. Job Type: Experienced Hire Shift: Shift 1 (India) Primary Location: India, Bangalore Additional Locations: Posting Statement: All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, religious creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military and veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, gender, gender expression, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by local law, regulation, or ordinance. Position of Trust N/A Work Model for this Role This role will be eligible for our hybrid work model which allows employees to split their time between working on-site at their assigned Intel site and off-site. * * ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Intel is committed to Responsible Business Alliance (RBA) compliance and ethical hiring practices. We do not charge any fees during our hiring process. Candidates should never be required to pay recruitment fees, medical examination fees, or any other charges as a condition of employment. If you are asked to pay any fees during our hiring process, please report this immediately to your recruiter.

jobs.title: Custom Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Experience range: 5-10 Yrs
Project Role : Custom Software Engineer Project Role Description : Develop custom software solutions to design, code, and enhance components across systems or applications. Use modern frameworks and agile practices to deliver scalable, high-performing solutions tailored to specific business needs. Must have skills : .Net Full Stack Development Good to have skills : NA Minimum 5 year(s) of experience is required Educational Qualification : 15 years full time education Summary :Seeking a forward-thinking professional with an AI-first mindset to design, develop, and deploy enterprise-grade solutions using Generative and Agentic AI frameworks that drive innovation, efficiency, and business transformation.Roles & Responsibilities:Lead AI-driven solution design and delivery by applying GenAI and Agentic AI to address complex business challenges, automate processes, and integrate intelligent insights into enterprise workflows for measurable impact. Professional & Technical Skills: Strong grasp of Generative and Agentic AI, prompt engineering, and AI evaluation frameworks. Ability to align AI capabilities with business objectives while ensuring scalability, responsible use, and tangible value realization. We are seeking a dynamic Mid-Level Application Architects / Senior Developers with a strong focus on hands-on development and practical solution design. The ideal candidate will have robust experience in .NET Core, MVC, and Python, with working knowledge of front-end technologies like React or Angular, and a foundational understanding of AI integration. This role emphasizes active coding, solution implementation, and collaboration across application development, infrastructure, and integration in multi-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) to deliver scalable, secure enterprise applications. Key Responsibilities:•Hands-On Coding:Actively develop, test, and deploy application-heavy solutions, write clean, efficient code in any of the programming languages like .NET Core (C#, ASP.NET), and Python for backend systems, and contributing to front-end development using React or Angular. •Solution Design:Partner with senior architects to design scalable, cloud-native application architectures, focusing on performance, maintainability, and integration in multi-cloud environments. •Integration Development:Build and maintain integrations using APIs, microservices, and event-driven patterns (e.g., REST, GraphQL, Kafka, or message queues). •Multi-Cloud Implementation:Develop and deploy applications across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, ensuring portability and optimization for cost and performance. •AI Integration:Implement practical AI features (e.g., automation, basic analytics) using cloud-based AI services or frameworks like TensorFlow or PyTorch. •Infrastructure Support:Collaborate with DevOps teams to implement containerized solutions (Docker, Kubernetes) and CI/CD pipelines, with hands-on use of IaC tools like Terraform or BiCep. •Performance & Security Optimization:Ensure applications meet performance and security standards through code reviews, testing, and adherence to best practices. •Team Collaboration:Work closely with developers, product managers, and infrastructure teams to translate requirements into technical implementations, providing hands-on support and mentorship. •Continuous Learning:Stay updated on full-stack development trends, cloud technologies, and AI advancements to contribute to innovative solutions. Qualifications & Skills:•Experience:5 to 12 years of hands-on experience in full-stack development, with at least 2 years in a lead developer or junior architect role focusing on application-heavy systems. •Demonstrated experience building and deploying solutions in multi-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud). •Strong proficiency in .NET, and Python for backend development. •Hands-on experience with front-end frameworks like React, Angular, or similar. •Basic exposure to AI/ML integration, such as using cloud AI services (e.g., Azure Open AI, Azure Foundry, AWS SageMaker,) or simple ML frameworks. •Practical experience with integration patterns (e.g., REST APIs, message queues) and microservices architecture. •Familiarity with infrastructure tools like Docker, Kubernetes, and IaC (e.g., Terraform, BiCep).•Experience with cloud-native services (e.g., Azure Functions, LogicApps, ServiceBus etc.). •Working knowledge of DevOps practices, including CI/CD pipelines and monitoring tools. •Understanding of secure coding practices and basic enterprise security standards (e.g., IAM, encryption). Soft Skills:•Strong debugging and problem-solving skills with a hands-on mindset. •Clear communication to collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders. •Ability to juggle hands-on coding with architectural design contributions. •Eagerness to learn and adapt to new tools, frameworks, and cloud technologies.Education:•Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Engineering, or a related field. •Certifications like Azure Developer Associate, Azure AI Fundamentals or similar are a plus. Qualification 15 years full time education

Job Summary The Computational Modeling Engineer - Discrete Manufacturing Modeling will provide deep modeling expertise and develop computational models that drive decisions to design new manufacturing systems and improve existing ones across Lilly's global manufacturing network. This role focuses on the dynamics of discrete manufacturing operations - parenteral fill/finish, device assembly, packaging, and material handling - applying modeling techniques across discrete event simulation, capacity and throughput analysis, line balancing, scheduling, and resource/operational logistics optimization. A core focus of the role is the development of Digital Twin computational models - including discrete event and optimization-based representations - that provide online modeling capabilities to manufacturing facilities, in alignment with the Engineering Digital Strategy for Manufacturing and Quality within Lilly. This is a global role, supporting functional initiatives and all Lilly Manufacturing sites globally. The primary focus of the role is to develop and deploy discrete event simulation and optimization models that increase manufacturing capacity, resilience, compliance, and inspection readiness, and that support operational excellence goals for safety, quality, and supply. The engineer will also serve as an internal advocate for simulation-based and model-based methods, fostering the use of discrete modeling tools by colleagues outside DME through instruction, consultation, and the development of internal collaborations. Key Objectives / Deliverables Develop and deploy discrete event simulation and optimization models to drive decisions that help design new and/or improve existing manufacturing and logistics processes. Develop capacity, throughput, line-balancing, and bottleneck-analysis models for parenteral fill/finish, device assembly, packaging, and material handling operations. Develop Digital Twin computational models of discrete manufacturing lines and logistics networks to provide online modeling capabilities to Lilly manufacturing facilities. Deliver sound interpretation of modeling results by maintaining in-depth knowledge of the underlying first-principles concepts (queueing theory, stochastic processes, scheduling theory) and numerical methods from which discrete event and optimization models are formulated and solved. Complement model-based solutions with empirical validation against site operating data and, when appropriate, time studies or shop-floor investigation. Prepare internal technical reports to document work and to contribute to the product or process body of knowledge, and when appropriate, publish and/or present work externally. Maintain and grow the functional value of discrete manufacturing modeling within Lilly by developing appropriate internal collaborations and sharing key learnings broadly at appropriate internal forums so colleagues can identify projects that may benefit from model-based analysis. Foster the use of discrete simulation and optimization tools by colleagues outside DME by providing instruction, consultation, and continuously advocating the use of simulation-based and model-based methods. Identify and implement modeling advances that bring value to Lilly by maintaining awareness of new developments in the external discrete event simulation and optimization landscape. Develop collaborations with appropriate external partners to help manage workload and to gain additional expertise. Partner with data leads within DME to provide data requirements that support discrete manufacturing models and Digital Twin solutions. Basic Qualifications PhD with 4-8 years of experience or MS degree with 8-15 years of experience in Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. Minimum of 4 years of related work experience (graduate research included). Experience developing models in one or more of the following: discrete event simulation, nonlinear programming, mixed-integer linear programming, or dynamic simulation of discrete systems. Demonstrated working knowledge of queueing theory, stochastic processes, and the numerical/optimization methods from which discrete event and optimization models are formulated and solved. Additional Skills / Preferences Strong technical writing and presentation skills. Capability to solve complex issues with minimal supervision. Experience with capacity analysis, line balancing, scheduling, and logistics optimization in a manufacturing environment. Experience developing simulation and optimization models leveraging commercial software tools such as ExtendSim, Frontline Solver, aspenONE, or equivalent discrete event simulation platforms. Experience with statistical analysis and data/model fitting leveraging commercial software tools such as JMP or similar. Experience developing digital twins of discrete manufacturing lines (e.g., parenteral fill/finish, device assembly, packaging). Experience working with validated systems and in a GMP/pharmaceutical industry environment. Ability to work well across different cultures and global manufacturing sites. We sit at the intersection of a two-sided marketplace, a regulated financial product, and one of the richest traveler datasets in the world which means the surface area for smart product work is enormous: embedded attach experiences, servicing delighters and AI-driven personalization of what protection even means for each traveler. jobs.title: Data Scientist III, Product Analytics
jobs.description:
Experience range: 5-10 Yrs
The Product Team creates high-quality end-to-end experiences for travelers, partners, and Expedia Group. Our focus on customer-centric innovation enables us to develop products that build loyalty and repeat business. We partner closely with teams across Expedia Group to drive growth and achieve results for our customers and the company. We are looking for a Data Scientist III, Product Analytics to partner closely with product, design, and engineering to drive decisions across our membership and loyalty experiences. This is an established IC role that independently owns analytics for one or more product areas, applying strong product thinking, experimentation, and storytelling skills with a moderate level of guidance. The role regularly interacts with stakeholders up to Senior Director level and is expected to influence strategy through clear, data backed recommendations. In this role, you will: Partner with product teams to clarify business problems, define success metrics, and translate ambiguous questions into structured analytical plans. Design, run, and analyze experiments (A/B tests, pre/post, quasi experimental reads) to measure impact, quantify trade offs, and guide iteration. Perform deep dive product analysis (funnels, cohorts, segmentation, sizing) to uncover drivers of performance and identify opportunities for growth and customer experience improvements. Build reliable datasets and dashboards using SQL and modern BI tools, enabling self serve product performance monitoring across platforms (web, app, partner). Apply solid statistical thinking (probability, sampling, inference, regression) to ensure reads are robust, distinguish signal from noise, and clearly communicate caveats. Use Python/R (or similar) to prototype models and advanced analyses when needed (e.g., regression, clustering, simple prediction) and to automate recurring analytics workflows. Tell clear, compelling stories that move stakeholders from insight to action framing context, methods, results, and recommendations for both technical and non technical audiences. Champion data quality and reproducibility by following best practices for data validation, query performance, version control, and documentation. Collaborate and upskill others by seeking peer review, sharing best practices, and providing light mentorship to more junior analysts or data scientists. Experience and qualifications: 5+ years of experience in analytics, product analytics, or data science roles. Bachelor s or Master s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Engineering) or equivalent practical experience. Proven track record of delivering data driven insights and recommendations that influenced product decisions or drove measurable performance improvements. Strong SQL : able to work confidently with large, complex datasets; write intermediate queries (joins, subqueries, CASE logic, window functions, unions); and optimize for performance and cost. Experience with at least one scripting language such as Python or R for analysis, modeling, and automating recurring tasks. Experimentation and statistics : comfortable with hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, experiment design, and interpreting regression/logistic regression outputs. Hands on experience with A/B testing platforms and understanding of when to use experiments vs. observational or exploratory analysis. Data visualization and dashboarding skills (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, or similar) with a focus on clarity, appropriate chart selection, and inclusive design basics (e.g., color use, accessibility). Ability to build and validate basic models (e.g., linear/logistic regression, simple clustering) and understand data/feature requirements and key assumptions. Demonstrated product sense : ability to connect metrics to customer journeys, refine problem statements, and propose pragmatic analytical approaches aligned with business timelines. Experience defining or refining product KPIs , building scorecards, and monitoring performance for ongoing features and launches. Strong critical thinking and problem solving skills; able to break complex problems into manageable analytical steps and iterate based on learnings. Excellent communication and influencing skills comfortable presenting to PMs, engineers, designers, and senior leaders, and adapting depth/rigor to the audience. Collaborative working style, with a proactive, ownership oriented mindset and openness to feedback, peer review, and continuous learning.

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description: Job ID 72346 Category Enterprise Technology Location Chennai, India Work Type On-site Who You Are An agent orchestrator, not a typist. You don't want to be a faster keyboard. You want to be a manager of agents — handing off the heavy lifting, reviewing the output, and keeping your hands on the architecture. The IDE is a cockpit for orchestration, not a text editor. Productively lazy. Your dream workflow: describe the requirement, let the agent build it, verify, ship, next. You automate anything a human shouldn't be doing twice. Your biggest bottleneck should be deciding what to build — while AI executes the how . Fundamentals first. Data structures, algorithms, distributed systems, networking — you understand the machine, not just the library that wraps it. When a framework breaks, you fix it. When AI gives you the wrong answer, you catch it. Orchestrating agents only works if you can tell good output from garbage. First-principles thinker with vision. You break problems to their core, question the assumptions, and rebuild. A software engineer's job is to architect solutions, not wrestle with syntax. You don't copy an architecture because "that's how it's done" — you ask why and decide if there's a better way. High agency. You don't wait for perfect specs or permission. You find a path, propose it, and move. Large organizations have walls; you figure out which ones to go through, around, or remove — and you do it constructively. Bias for action. Requirements will be messy and priorities will shift. You ship v1, learn, and iterate instead of living in design review. Why This Role Ford is a 120-year-old company moving fast on AI, and that's the real challenge: building world-class AI applications inside a large enterprise with real constraints — security, compliance, legacy systems. The engineers who thrive here treat those constraints as problems to solve, not reasons to stop. If you want a place where everything is already figured out, this isn't it. If you're a 10x thinker who wants to build something that matters — and have the grit to push through the hard parts — let's talk. What You'll Do Orchestrate agents to build. Use AI as your default way of working — agents do the heavy lifting, you direct, review, and harden. You set the bar for how the team builds with AI. Build the AI use cases. Design and ship AI-powered applications and agents — RAG pipelines, LLM integrations, agentic workflows. Understand what's happening under the hood and make it work in production, at scale. Ship cloud-native systems on GCP. Design, deploy, operate. You own the architecture, the infrastructure-as-code, and the CI/CD pipeline. No throwing code over the wall. Connect systems that don't want to be connected. Build the integration layer across enterprise SaaS platforms. Expect messy APIs, legacy constraints, and creative problem-solving. Automate what shouldn't be manual. If a human repeats it, you write the code — or point an agent at it — to stop it. Make other engineers faster. Build the tools, agent workflows, and guardrails that remove friction. Developer productivity is a multiplier. Requirements BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. MS is a plus, not a substitute for shipping software. 2+ years building and deploying full-stack applications in production. 2+ years on cloud-native platforms (GCP preferred). Demonstrable experience building AI agents or applications — show us what you've built, not what you've read. What You Bring Python — deep. You write production systems, not just scripts. JavaScript / TypeScript — React, Node.js, or equivalent. A real frontend and a real API. Front-end strength is a big plus. AI engineering — LLMs, embeddings, vector stores, RAG. Comfortable building agents and evaluation pipelines. Bonus for fine-tuning or eval work. AI-assisted development — fluent with modern AI coding tools and agent workflows, and clear-eyed about where they help and where they don't. GCP — Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, GKE, BigQuery, Cloud Storage. Deployed and operated, not just tutorials. Databases — relational and NoSQL. You know when to use what, and why. APIs & microservices — designed and built RESTful services at scale. Git, IaC & CI/CD — Terraform, Cloud Build, or equivalent. Reproducible, version-controlled infrastructure and disciplined code review.

The role works closely with development teams, OEM vendors, security teams, and operational stakeholders to ensure applications comply with organizational security requirements and industry best practices.The analyst will coordinate with OEM vendors to resolve security-related bugs, software defects, and technical issues, enforce security policies defined by the Account Security Team, and generate security and operational reports to support governance, risk management, and compliance activities.Key ResponsibilitiesApplication Security Assessment RemediationReview application security findings from SAST, DAST, SCA, API security, and penetration testing activities. Track application security vulnerabilities through the remediation lifecycle until closure. Coordinate with development, infrastructure, cloud, and application support teams to implement remediation recommendations. Validate remediation activities and perform retesting where applicable. Support secure application deployment and release processes. OEM Vendor CoordinationCoordinate with OEM vendors and third-party software providers to resolve security vulnerabilities, software bugs, patching issues, and technical defects affecting business applications. Review vendor security advisories and assess application impact. Track vendor remediation timelines and escalate critical security issues when necessary. Participate in technical discussions with OEM support teams regarding application security concerns. Ensure vendor-provided fixes are properly tested and implemented. Security Policy EnforcementEnforce application security policies, standards, and secure coding requirements as requested by the Account Security Team. Support implementation of security controls throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). Verify compliance with secure coding standards such as OWASP Top 10, CWE, and organizational security baselines. Monitor application compliance with established security requirements. Support risk exception and remediation governance processes. Security Testing ValidationSupport and coordinate: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) Software Composition Analysis (SCA) API Security Assessments Penetration Testing activities Analyze findings and prioritize remediation activities based on risk and business impact. Review security testing results and provide remediation guidance to development teams. Reporting Metrics Generate security and operational reports mutually agreed with the Account Security Team. Produce dashboards and metrics related to: Open application vulnerabilities Critical and high-risk findings Remediation SLA compliance Application security testing coverage Secure SDLC compliance Present application security posture and remediation status to stakeholders and management. Security Governance Compliance Support compliance initiatives involving: OWASP ASVS OWASP Top 10 PCI DSS NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) ISO 27001 SOC Controls Assist with internal and external audits related to application security. Maintain application security documentation, risk registers, and remediation tracking records. Continuous ImprovementIdentify opportunities to improve application security processes and controls. Recommend enhancements to security testing methodologies and tooling. Assist in integrating security requirements into DevSecOps pipelines. Support Application Security Program maturity initiatives. Contribute to development of secure coding awareness and training materials. Required QualificationsEducationBachelor's degree in Cyber Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or related field. Equivalent professional experience may be considered. ExperienceMid-Level Analyst3–5 years of experience in Application Security, Security Operations, Software Development, Vulnerability Management, or related cybersecurity functions. Senior Analyst5–8 years of experience supporting enterprise application security programs. Coordinate remediation with development teams and OEM vendors. Validate security fixes and perform retesting. Track remediation SLA compliance. Enforce application security standards and policies. Generate weekly and monthly application security reports. Participate in vulnerability review meetings. Support secure SDLC and DevSecOps initiatives. Assist with audit and compliance activities. jobs.title: Sr Software Engineer
jobs.description: Company Description It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started. Join us to put AI to work for people. Job Description Overview The AI Application Software Engineer designs, builds, ships, and operates applications whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret user intent, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the user's behalf. In Field Service Management, this means building AI-native experiences for scheduling, dispatch, and service workflows that automate routine work, escalate exceptions, and improve customer outcomes. This is a hands-on, forward deployed role for a senior engineer whose first instinct is AI — someone who can shape ambiguous customer problems into precise specifications, author the instructions and prompts that govern agent behavior, build the application and integrations around them, and prove through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly. This is not a machine learning or AI research role; you will not train foundation models. You own what ships, whether a human or an agent produced it. What You Get to Do Build AI-native applications. Design and ship applications built around agentic behavior across Field Service Management — scheduling, dispatch, and workflows that reason over context, automate routine work, and escalate exceptions. Work AI-first in delivery. Direct coding agents to build, refactor, and test; use AI to think more sharply in front of customers; and apply it as part of everyday engineering practice rather than as a side tool. Deliver forward deployed. Work embedded in customer environments, tuning instructions and evaluation sets on the ground, using AI to compress turnaround without cutting quality. Author and maintain agentic instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern agent behavior — treating them as reviewed, regression-covered engineering artifacts. Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic behavior. Design and operate golden datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring, CI gates, drift detection, adversarial testing, and grounding checks that make change safe. Design conversational experiences. Build experiences that hold context, confirm before consequential actions, and hand off cleanly to humans. Collaborate across product, UX, and documentation. Bring the AI-first instinct into cross-functional partnerships, not just your own code. Own quality and safety in production. Monitor containment, hallucination, prompt injection, and data leakage, then feed failures back into specifications and evaluation sets. Qualifications Experience A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production software, including hands-on delivery of AI-native application features that real users depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts, designing AI-driven workflows, and building evaluation and testing for non-deterministic behavior is required. Experience with chat experiences is required; voice or multi-channel experience is strongly preferred. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity is required; prior forward deployed experience is an advantage. Education Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 3 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD without experience; or equivalent work experience. Key competencies Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing. Good to have technologies like HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Java. AI-native application development. Hands-on experience with agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling latency, cost, and failure. Agentic instruction and prompt engineering. Demonstrated skill with instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, structured outputs, grounding, citation, graceful failure, and disciplined iteration against measured outcomes. Specification precision. Ability to define a problem rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements it correctly, and to judge when to solve it in code, in instructions, or by delegating. Customer-facing delivery with AI-native speed. Comfort working directly with customers under real constraints, using AI to cut turnaround, and communicating capability and risk credibly to non-engineers. AI safety and data handling. Working knowledge of prompt injection, data leakage, over-broad tool access, and unsafe autonomous action, translated into concrete guardrails and least-privilege controls. Desired experience Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment. A platform-level view. Experience with agent runtimes, context engineering, retrieval, and memory. Domain depth. Experience in Field Service Management, scheduling, or workforce management is valued but not required; the right engineer can learn the domain. Evaluation and observability tooling. jobs.title: Staff, AI Product Manager
jobs.description: About the Role: GSK’s Enterprise AI team, a highly skilled applied AI group, translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across every major group at GSK — R&D, Medical, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Legal, Finance, and beyond. Bionic pods — AI product managers, forward deployed engineers, full-stack engineers, data engineers, and AI agents and workers — embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes. We are hiring a Staff, AI Product Manager to own the Orchestration and Automation platform tower: the low and medium code platforms where GSK builds agents and automations, and the enablement model that lets thousands of non-engineers use them safely. The estate spans workflow and agent builders such as Power Platform, Copilot Studio and n8n, alongside the adjacent orchestration tooling that sits with them. You will own the roadmap and the governance model, and act as the platform consultant business teams come to when they need to turn demand into working automations. Why This Role Exists GSK runs various low and medium code platforms, and demand from business teams outpaces any central delivery team. This role exists to take consolidation decisions, and to build the self-enablement layer — guardrails, templates, training, support — that lets citizen developers build safely without engineering review on every change. In this role you will be the person who: Owns the Orchestration and Automation platform tower and its roadmap. Takes consolidation decisions across the low and medium code platform estate. Acts as the platform consultant for business teams building on the estate. Owns the governance model that defines what a citizen developer may build unsupervised. How This Differs from Traditional Product Management This is not a traditional enterprise product role managing a source system’s roadmap, releases, and backlog. As an AI Product Manager in Enterprise AI, you: Build new AI products from ambiguous, unsolved business problems. Work with probabilistic systems, defining evaluations, acceptable error, and human oversight. Help lead a bionic pod, deciding which work goes to engineers and which to AI agents and workers, and how they hand off. Prototype hands on and are measured on business outcomes. Key Responsibilities Platform Portfolio & Consolidation Map capability against actual usage across the whole low and medium code estate, and recommend what consolidates, what stays, and what retires. Quantify value rigorously. Build credible business cases that survive finance and senior business unit scrutiny — cycle time saved, manual effort removed, licence cost avoided, automations running in production. Develop deep automation pattern recognition so you can spot the workflows worth automating and the ones that should be fixed at source instead. Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping Shape the platform roadmap. Maintain a living view of in-flight, queued, and de-prioritized platform work, with the rationale for each decision, and feed it into the broader AI Platforms & Tools portfolio. Make trade-off recommendations. When two business sponsors both want platform investment, define the success metrics, run the analysis, and recommend where effort goes. Protect engineering focus. Push back — with evidence — on opportunities that won’t move scalable outcomes. Engineering Partnership & Enablement Consult on platform fit and design. Advise business teams and delivery squads on which platform fits, how to structure the build, and what it takes to reach production. Translate ambiguous requests into crisp problem statements and success metrics. Shape engagements end-to-end. Define scope, success criteria, exit conditions, and scaling pathways before kick-off, then stay close as engineers execute. Surface re-use and platform leverage when a one-off solution should become a reusable capability. Design the human and agent split. Decide which tasks the pod’s AI agents and workers own, where engineers and business users stay in the loop, and how evaluation and oversight make that safe. Stakeholder Alignment & Communication Operate fluently with VP-level business and scientific leaders. Run conversations that turn fuzzy ambitions into concrete, fundable AI engagements. Build sponsor coalitions that secure data access, change-management commitment, and air cover for your engagements. Communicate impact clearly in language that connects AI work to patients, science, and enterprise outcomes. Measurement, Learning & Iteration Apply Enterprise AI’s value-realization framework to every engagement and platform in the tower, and improve it with what you learn. Run honest post-mortems and feed lessons back into how the tower selects platforms and prioritizes demand Required Skills: 16+ years of progressive experience in enterprise platform leadership, with a meaningful part of it spent owning a platform or platform estate end to end: roadmap, architecture direction, operations, and lifecycle. Demonstrated track record of taking a platform from fragmented or underused to well run: consolidation calls made, adoption grown, and the operating model that sustained it. Experience running a platform in a regulated enterprise, with working knowledge of at least one part of the pharma value chain and the data, decisions, and constraints inside it. Solid technical fluency in modern AI/ML, covering LLMs, agentic systems, AI agents and workers, data and evaluation patterns, sufficient to set architecture direction, challenge engineers, scope realistically, and avoid hype-driven choices. Experience leading engineers directly while also leading a far larger citizen developer community through influence, frameworks, and quality of thinking. A platform product heritage: roadmap shaping, lifecycle and version management, vendor and licensing ownership, service levels, and stakeholder alignment across a large and varied user base. Preferred skills : Deep, hands-on Microsoft Power Platform experience is mandatory: Power Apps, Power Automate and Dataverse at enterprise scale, including environment strategy, ALM, licensing, and the governance model around them. Has owned a low or medium code automation platform at enterprise scale and run a citizen developer or self-service programme covering thousands of users, with guardrails that held under pressure. Fluent with the wider low and medium code agent and workflow stacks that sit alongside Power Platform, such as Copilot Studio, n8n, and the equivalents from the major cloud vendors. Skills AI Platforms, Change Management, Data Analysis, Microsoft ALM, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Power Automate, Microsoft Power Platform, Roadmap Development, Statistical Analysis, User Needs Analysis Why GSK? Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale. People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people. jobs.title: GenAI-Engineer
jobs.description: It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they are doing! We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business. 5-8 years of experience as a Data Scientist with deep expertise in GenAI, NLP/LLM technologies. The candidate should have hands-on experience ML model building as well as training and fine-tuning large language models from the ground up. This role requires a strong technical background in machine learning, deep learning, and practical experience with modern AI frameworks. Responsibilities: Design, develop, and implement advanced solutions leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs). Take full ownership of initiatives, delivering end-to-end solutions with minimal supervision. Stay current with the latest advancements in Generative AI, LLMs, RAG systems, and applied research. Build and maintain reusable code libraries, tools, and frameworks to accelerate AI development. Participate in code reviews to ensure high-quality, maintainable, and scalable solutions. Contribute across the entire software development lifecycle—design, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align AI solutions with business goals, integrate contributions into core systems, and influence roadmaps. Apply strong analytical and problem-solving skills to design efficient solutions for complex business challenges. Communicate effectively across technical and non-technical teams, ensuring transparency and alignment. Own business impact of AI solutions, including adoption, accuracy, latency, and cost efficiency Translate ambiguous business problems into structured AI solution approaches and measurable outcomes Drive solution success metrics (e.g., productivity gains, automation %, decision accuracy) Engage directly with business and technical stakeholders to understand requirements, present solutions, and influence decision-making Communicate solution architecture and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences Contribute to client discussions, PoCs, and proposal development. Design scalable, modular, and production-grade AI systems (APIs, pipelines, orchestration layers) Define architecture patterns for LLM applications (RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, hybrid systems) Make trade-offs across latency, cost, accuracy, and maintainability Build reusable accelerators, frameworks, and components that can be leveraged across multiple use cases and clients Contribute to internal IP creation (assets, templates, reference architectures) Ensure reliability and robustness of LLM systems through evaluation frameworks, guardrails, and fallback strategies Design safe and responsible AI systems (hallucination mitigation, bias handling, governance) Optimize cost-performance trade-offs in large-scale deployments Identify when NOT to use LLMs and propose alternative approaches Contribute to code reviews, design reviews, and mentorship of junior team members Drive quality standards and best practices across projects Stay ahead of advancements in GenAI and proactively evaluate their applicability to business problems Contribute to internal knowledge sharing, training, and capability building. Must-Have Skills: Generative AI & NLP: SaaS-based LLMs: LangChain, LlamaIndex, vector databases, prompt engineering (CoT, ReAct, agents), Azure OpenAI function calling, multimodal models. Open-Source and SaaS LLMs: Azure OpenAI, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4, etc. At least one agentic Generative AI framework: CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph, n8n, LangFlow, SmolAgents, Semantic Kernel. Advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems: hybrid retrieval, knowledge graph–based retrieval, multi-hop RAG, hierarchical/contextual retrieval strategies, evaluation/monitoring of RAG pipelines. Classical NLP: text classification, topic modeling, Q&A systems, conversational AI/chatbots, search, Document AI, summarization, content generation, and Named Entity Recognition (NER). Databricks ecosystem: Databricks Genie, Databricks AI/BI, AgentBricks MS Copilot Studio and knowledge on no-code/low-code app development. MCP server, tools, skills and creation and maintenance of reusable componets. If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us! Not the right fit? Let us know you're interested in a future opportunity by clicking Introduce Yourself in the top-right corner of the page or create an account to set up email alerts as new job postings become available that meet your interest!

Working knowledge of DevOps practices, including CI/CD pipelines and monitoring tools. Understanding of secure coding practices and basic enterprise security standards (e.g., IAM, encryption). Soft Skills: Strong debugging and problem-solving skills with a hands-on mindset. Clear communication to collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to juggle hands-on coding with architectural design contributions. Eagerness to learn and adapt to new tools, frameworks, and cloud technologies. Education: Bachelor s degree in computer science, Engineering, or a related field. Certifications like Azure Developer Associate, Azure AI Fundamentals or similar are a plus. 15 years full time education

jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer
jobs.description: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Title and Summary Senior AI Engineer Mastercard's Business & Market Insights (B&MI) group empowers organizations to achieve growth and innovation goals by delivering unparalleled data-driven intelligence and cutting-edge AI solutions. By harnessing proprietary data, frontier generative AI, and global expertise, B&MI helps businesses make smarter, faster, and more impactful decisions. We transform complex, multi-modal data into agentic systems and generative applications that drive measurable business outcomes and sustained competitive advantage. We're looking for a Senior AI Engineer, Generative AI & ML Engineering, for the Operational Intelligence Program within B&MI. In this hands-on role, you'll design, build, and ship production-grade agentic AI systems. These include agents that make extensive tool calls into enterprise services and APIs, handle complex multi-step workflows, and deliver secure, scalable, reliable results. You'll work across agent orchestration, tool calling, memory, retrieval, and LLMOps, help set the engineering standard for Gen AI development, and mentor other engineers on the team. Much of this work is strong backend engineering. If you bring deep experience building production services and have started building with LLMs, we'd love to Roles & Responsibilities Architect and build the tool-calling layer that powers our agents: wrap internal services, data platforms, and external APIs as well-defined tools with clear schemas, contracts, and permissions. Engineer reliable tool execution at scale, including parallel and chained tool calls, timeouts, retries, idempotency, error recovery, and graceful handling of tool failures or bad model outputs. Develop high-performance Python backend services for LLM orchestration, covering async job handling, streaming responses, caching, rate limiting, and distributed workflows supporting high-throughput Gen AI operations. Engineer state, memory, and context management subsystems so agents can maintain session continuity across long, multi-step, tool-heavy interactions. Architect multi-agent and skills-based agent systems using frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or similar, enabling autonomous reasoning, tool use, inter-agent coordination, and adaptive decision-making at enterprise scale. Build observability for agent behavior, including end-to-end tracing of tool calls, measuring tool-selection accuracy, and debugging multi-step agent runs in production. Build retrieval systems (RAG and Graph-RAG) where agents need grounded knowledge, using vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, pgvector, OpenSearch) and knowledge graphs (e.g., Neo4j, AWS Neptune). Establish LLMOps and MLOps pipelines on Databricks (AWS), covering MLflow, prompt and agent evaluation, model lineage tracking, CI/CD, and monitoring. Design multimodal generative AI pipelines that unify text, image, tabular, and graph data using modern transformer-based and foundation models. Guide fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and alignment strategies (e.g., PEFT, LoRA, instruction tuning, RLHF) to adapt foundation models for specialized enterprise use cases, working closely with ML specialists. Implement Responsible AI practices, including hallucination mitigation, bias detection, output safety guardrails, explainability, and compliance with data ethics standards. Evaluate and productionize advances in agentic AI, multimodal models, and frontier foundation models, benchmarking them against enterprise performance and safety requirements. Lead, mentor, and grow a team of engineers, and set the engineering standard for Gen AI development across the program. All About You Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, AI/ML, or Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. A strong track record of building and operating production backend systems at scale, including distributed services, APIs, async processing, data stores, and observability. Strong API design and integration experience: you know how to build services that other systems, and now LLMs, can call safely and reliably. Excellent Python engineering skills, including async programming, API development (FastAPI or similar), and microservices, plus SQL proficiency. Hands-on experience shipping at least one LLM-powered application to production that uses tool/function calling, such as agents that call APIs, query databases, or trigger workflows. This can be with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or open-source models. A working understanding of Gen AI engineering patterns, such as prompt design, embeddings, semantic search, and agent memory, or a demonstrated ability to ramp up quickly on new technical domains. Experience with at least one cloud platform (AWS preferred; Azure or GCP welcome). Experience leading or mentoring engineers, plus strong communication and stakeholder management skills. jobs.description: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. On this platform, agents make extensive tool calls into enterprise services and APIs and must run securely, reliably, and at scale. You'll set the standards teams build on across tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, self-correcting agents, memory, retrieval, and LLMOps. You'll also make the key decisions on models, platforms, and trade-offs. Working closely with engineering, product, security, and business leaders, you'll shape the long-term direction of Gen AI across B&MI and mentor architects and senior engineers. You'll also stay hands-on with prototypes that de-risk big bets. The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale. This covers schemas, contracts, versioning, access control, and resilient execution (parallel and chained calls, retries, timeouts, idempotency, circuit breakers, and fallbacks). Set the architecture for multi-agent and skills-based agent systems (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen), including when to use agents versus deterministic workflows and how agents coordinate, delegate, and share context. Architect agent memory and state for long-running, multi-step sessions, including short- and long-term memory (e.g., Mem0, Zep, LangGraph memory), session persistence, and memory scoping and retention. The ability to influence without authority, aligning engineering, product, and leadership around a technical direction and explaining trade-offs in business terms. Implement robust batch and near real time data pipelines supporting analytics, reporting, data warehousing, and downstream applications. Build reusable data flows, workflows, and transforms aligned to enterprise data architecture standards. 2) Data Modeling, Transformation & Enrichment Design complex transformation logic using BODS features such as queries, transforms, lookups, hierarchies, and reusable objects. Implement data enrichment, standardization, and harmonization logic across multiple source systems. Apply canonical data modeling practices to reduce duplication and point to point complexity. 3) Data Quality, Profiling & Governance Implement data quality rules for validation, cleansing, matching, deduplication, and standardization. Build profiling and validation pipelines to assess data completeness, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness. Support governance requirements through lineage-aware jobs, audit trails, and traceable transformations. 4) AI Native Data Engineering (Agentic ETL Layer) Build data engineering agents that can: o Analyze source metadata and recommend transformation logic. o Propose data quality rules based on observed patterns and historical issues. o Auto-generate initial ETL mappings and job scaffolding, validated against enterprise standards. Implement retrieval grounded assistance that uses metadata catalogs, mapping documents, business rules, and historical defects to produce verifiable recommendations. Enable conversational exploration of data pipelines (e.g., why did this record fail , what changed in yesterday s load ) with grounded, auditable outputs. 5) Testing, Validation & Evaluation Loops Design automated validation strategies: schema checks, row counts, reconciliation rules, referential integrity checks, and regression comparisons. Establish evaluation harnesses for AI behaviors: golden datasets for transformations, accuracy checks for generated rules, and drift detection. Gate releases of ETL logic and AI-generated artifacts through measurable quality thresholds. 6) Performance, Scalability & Reliability Optimize ETL jobs for performance and scalability (parallelism, pushdown, efficient transforms, resource tuning). Perform root cause analysis for load failures and data issues document and automate preventive actions. Use AI augmented diagnostics to cluster recurring issues and recommend remediation steps grounded in runbooks and past incidents. 8) Modernization & Platform Evolution Support modernization initiatives by integrating BODS pipelines with cloud data platforms and analytics ecosystems. Assist in transitioning legacy ETL logic toward more modular, metadata driven, and AI augmented data architectures. Collaborate with data architects, analytics teams, and platform engineers to deliver end to end data solutions. AI native capability: tool augmented workflows, retrieval grounded recommendations, evaluation loops, and safe automation boundaries. Metadata management, lineage concepts, and data governance frameworks. Experience integrating ETL platforms with cloud data ecosystems and modern analytics tools. Scripting or automation skills to support pipeline orchestration and operational tooling. What This Role Does Not Center On Training or fine tuning foundation AI models. Every facility has a trailer yard — the physical space where line-haul vehicles arrive, get loaded or unloaded, and depart. The Relay Yard Automation (RYA) team builds the software that manages these trailer yards across 6,000+ Amazon facilities on three continents. Our products handle 200K+ gate transactions per day and facilitated the arrival and departure of 55M vehicles last year. Our gate automation program has already eliminated millions of manual transactions, with a long-term goal of fully autonomous yard operations. The tech stack is diverse by necessity: Android mobile apps for yard associates and drivers, React web applications for remote gate agents and yard operators, Java/TypeScript backend services on AWS, and hardware integrations running on edge compute devices deployed in the field. Systems are loosely coupled, event-driven, and must operate reliably in environments ranging from 1M+ sq ft North American fulfillment centers to small urban European delivery stations. jobs.title: Engineer II, Full Stack Engineer
jobs.description: Job Purpose: Enterprise AI (EAI) builds AI products that combine real modelling work with user-facing applications, and ships them to production. Full Stack Engineers move across data, models, platforms, APIs and interfaces in a single workflow. In our operating model, digital workers do much of the hands-on build. They generate services, APIs, interface components and tests, run evaluations and monitor what is in production. Our engineers set the architecture and standards that work is built to, and own the quality of what ships. EAI products and agents draw on a governed context layer that makes data, meaning, permissions and history retrievable at the moment they are needed. Full Stack Engineers build the products and agents that consume it, and decide how that context reaches users. The Full Stack Engineer II independently builds and ships AI-integrated features, working closely with GSK business teams to prototype against real data and workflows at a days-to-weeks cadence. The role owns the quality of what digital workers deliver in those features, makes evidence-based calls on what to continue or stop, and contributes reusable components others adopt. Responsibilities: Own use cases from problem framing through working prototype and first production version, at a days-to-weeks cadence and without close supervision. Qualify incoming asks: challenge underspecified problems, assess feasibility and define scope before committing to work. At the end of each piece of work, form and defend an evidence-based recommendation to continue or stop, presented clearly to business and EAI leadership. Work closely with business teams, prototyping against real data and workflows and building trusted relationships with product owners and engineering leads. Required skills: 6+ years of full-stack or AI/ML engineering experience, including production deployments. Demonstrated ability to take ideas from sketch to working software at speed, independently and under time pressure. A startup, lab or innovation-team background is an advantage. Strong proficiency in Python and at least one of TypeScript, JavaScript, Go or similar, with experience designing and shipping backend services and complete UI features. Hands-on experience with GenAI patterns: agents, multi-agent orchestration, RAG, tool use, prompt engineering and evaluation, including evaluation pipelines and LLM-specific monitoring in production. Daily use of AI coding agents as the primary mode of development, with sound judgement on what to accept, change or reject. A track record of raising team standards through code review and documentation, and of contributing reusable engineering patterns that others adopted. Education : Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred skills: Prior experience as a Full Stack Engineer, Customer Engineer or Solutions Architect, ideally at an AI-native company or hyperscaler. Experience in regulated industries, such as life sciences, healthcare or financial services, and familiarity with GxP, GDPR and SOX. Working knowledge of fine-tuning fundamentals and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations.
