jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description: Senior Machine Learning Engineer Description - We are looking for a Senior MLOps Engineer to design, build, and operate the infrastructure that enables machine learning models and large language models to be deployed safely, reliably, and at scale. In this role, you will create the end-to-end capabilities required to move models from experimentation into production, expose them through secure and highly available endpoints, and enable users and applications to interact with AI-powered services. You will work across AWS and Databricks to establish robust CI/CD pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, observability, governance, rollback mechanisms, and operational standards. You will partner closely with data scientists, machine learning engineers, software engineers, security teams, and platform engineers. The ideal candidate combines strong cloud and DevOps engineering skills with a practical understanding of machine learning systems, LLM deployment patterns, and production reliability. Key Responsibilities MLOps Platform and Architecture Design and implement a scalable MLOps platform using AWS and Databricks. Define reference architectures and reusable deployment patterns for traditional machine learning models, deep learning models, and large language models. Build standardized workflows that move models from development and validation into staging and production. Develop self-service capabilities that allow data scientists and ML engineers to deploy models without manually managing infrastructure. Establish clear separation between development, testing, staging, and production environments. Design multi-region or multi-availability-zone architectures where required by business continuity and availability objectives. CI/CD and Model Deployment Build automated CI/CD pipelines for model code, inference services, infrastructure, configuration, and model artifacts. Implement automated testing across the deployment lifecycle, including: Unit testing Integration testing Model validation Data contract validation API and endpoint testing Security testing Performance and load testing Regression testing Automate model packaging, containerization, versioning, approval, promotion, and deployment. Support deployment strategies such as blue-green deployments, canary releases, shadow deployments, and controlled traffic shifting. Implement reliable rollback and roll-forward mechanisms for application code, infrastructure, model versions, prompts, and configuration. Ensure deployments are reproducible, auditable, and recoverable. Model and LLM Serving Design and operate secure, scalable, low-latency inference endpoints. Deploy models using appropriate services and patterns across AWS and Databricks, such as: Databricks Model Serving MLflow Model Registry Amazon SageMaker Amazon ECS or EKS AWS Lambda, where appropriate API Gateway Application Load Balancers Build synchronous, asynchronous, batch, and streaming inference capabilities. Design serving architectures for LLM-powered applications, including: Hosted foundation models Open-source models Fine-tuned models Retrieval-augmented generation Embedding services Vector search Prompt and response orchestration Tool-calling and agentic workflows Optimize inference performance, scalability, GPU utilization, concurrency, throughput, latency, and cost. Implement autoscaling, request throttling, queuing, caching, timeout handling, and graceful degradation. Reliability, Recovery, and Business Continuity Build recoverable model-serving endpoints with clearly defined recovery time and recovery point objectives. Implement automated health checks, failover mechanisms, retry policies, circuit breakers, and service recovery procedures. Design backup and recovery processes for: Model artifacts Model registry metadata Feature definitions Deployment configurations Infrastructure state Prompts and application configuration Vector indexes and knowledge-base assets Create disaster recovery procedures and regularly test restoration and failover capabilities. Ensure production services can recover from failed deployments, infrastructure outages, model errors, and upstream dependency failures. Develop operational runbooks and incident response procedures. Monitoring and Observability Implement end-to-end observability for infrastructure, applications, models, data, and user interactions. Monitor: Availability Request volume Latency Error rates Resource utilization Model performance Data quality Data drift Concept drift Prediction distributions LLM response quality Hallucination and safety indicators Token consumption Cost per request Establish dashboards, alerts, service-level indicators, and service-level objectives. Integrate monitoring with incident management and on-call processes. Enable traceability from user requests through model inference, retrieval, orchestration, and downstream services. Support root-cause analysis by maintaining structured logs, metrics, traces, model lineage, and deployment history. Security and Governance Implement security controls for model-serving environments, APIs, data access, and deployment pipelines. Apply least-privilege access using AWS IAM, Databricks permissions, service principals, and role-based access control. Secure secrets, credentials, API keys, certificates, and tokens using approved secrets-management solutions. Implement encryption in transit and at rest. Design private networking, endpoint controls, firewall rules, and secure connectivity patterns. Support authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and tenant isolation for AI services. Ensure models and LLM applications comply with organizational requirements for privacy, security, auditability, and responsible AI. Maintain model lineage, approval records, version history, and deployment audit trails. Implement controls for sensitive data, personally identifiable information, prompt injection, unsafe outputs, and unauthorized model access. Infrastructure as Code and Automation Build and maintain cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or AWS CloudFormation. Automate environment provisioning, policy enforcement, deployment configuration, and platform upgrades. Create reusable modules, templates, libraries, and deployment frameworks. Implement configuration management and environment-specific parameterization. Ensure infrastructure changes are peer-reviewed, tested, version-controlled, and traceable. Collaboration and Engineering Standards Partner with data scientists and ML engineers to productionize models and define deployment requirements. Work with software engineering teams to integrate model endpoints into user-facing products and internal applications. Collaborate with cybersecurity, architecture, legal, privacy, and governance teams. Define MLOps engineering standards, design principles, coding practices, and operational requirements. Conduct architecture reviews, code reviews, and production-readiness assessments. Machine Learning Experience : Significant experience in MLOps, platform engineering, DevOps, site reliability engineering, cloud engineering, or production machine learning. Proven experience deploying and operating machine learning models in production. Strong hands-on experience with AWS services and cloud architecture. Strong hands-on experience with Databricks, including MLflow, model registries, jobs, clusters, permissions, and model-serving capabilities. Experience building CI/CD pipelines using tools such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, or AWS CodePipeline, Docker and containerized application deployment. Experience with Kubernetes and managed container platforms such as Amazon EKS or ECS. Proficiency in Python and experience building production-quality APIs and inference services. Experience with REST APIs, asynchronous processing, event-driven architectures, and distributed systems. Strong knowledge of Infrastructure as Code, preferably Terraform. Experience with model versioning, artifact management, experiment tracking, and deployment promotion workflows. Experience implementing monitoring, logging, tracing, alerting, and production support processes. Strong understanding of high availability, disaster recovery, fault tolerance, and rollback strategies. Knowledge of cloud networking, IAM, secrets management, encryption, and secure software delivery. Training and inference workflows Online and batch inference Model serialization and packaging Feature engineering and feature consistency Model validation and evaluation,l drift and data drift Model explainability and reproducibility GPU-based model serving Embeddings and vector databases Retrieval-augmented generation Prompt management and versioning LLM evaluation and guardrails Token limits, context management, and inference cost optimization Responsible AI, content safety, and human-in-the-loop controls This role does not necessarily require the candidate to develop new machine learning algorithms. However, the candidate must be able to understand model behavior, deployment constraints, performance characteristics, and operational risks. Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. 12+ years of total experience Experience deploying generative AI or LLM-based applications in production. Experience with Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, Databricks Mosaic AI, or similar AI platforms. Experience with vector-search technologies such as Databricks Vector Search, OpenSearch, Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, or pgvector. Experience with LLM application frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or equivalent orchestration tools. Experience with observability platforms such as Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, CloudWatch, OpenTelemetry, or Splunk. Experience applying SRE practices to machine learning and AI systems. Experience operating platforms in regulated, enterprise, or data-sensitive environments. Relevant AWS, Databricks, Kubernetes, or cloud architecture certifications. What Success Looks Like Within the first 6 to 12 months, the successful candidate will: Establish a standardized and automated path from model development to production. Reduce the time required to deploy a new model or LLM service. Enable repeatable deployments across development, staging, and production. Provide reliable and secure endpoints through which users and applications can interact with AI. Implement automated rollback and recovery for failed deployments. Establish monitoring for service health, model performance, quality, security, and cost. Improve availability, deployment frequency, change-failure rate, and recovery time. Create reusable platform components that increase engineering productivity. Establish production-readiness standards for machine learning and generative AI services. Example Performance Indicators Model deployment lead time Deployment frequency Percentage of automated deployments Change-failure rate Mean time to detect incidents Mean time to recover Endpoint availability P95 and P99 inference latency Model rollback success rate Recovery-test success rate Infrastructure provisioning time Cost per inference request Percentage of production models with complete lineage and monitoring Number of security or compliance exceptions Internal developer and data scientist satisfaction Ideal Candidate Profile You are a pragmatic platform engineer who understands that deploying a model is only the beginning. You think about security, reliability, monitoring, recovery, cost, governance, and the end-user experience from the start. You are comfortable moving between cloud architecture, infrastructure automation, CI/CD pipelines, Python services, Databricks workflows, model registries, Kubernetes, and production incident management. You can translate experimental AI solutions into dependable services that users can trust. jobs.description: Who We Are At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses. We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI-powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive. The Role Your Role: As a Automation Tech Lead - Power platforms, you will provide technical leadership for the design, development, integration, deployment, and operational support of enterprise automation solutions. Lead troubleshooting and resolution of complex incidents, integration failures, runtime issues, performance bottlenecks, and environment-related challenges. Collaborate with business, product, platform, and engineering teams to deliver reliable, scalable, and compliant automation solutions while managing stakeholder expectations. Your Future at Kyndryl Every position at Kyndryl offers a way forward to grow your career. We have opportunities that you won’t find anywhere else, including hands-on experience, learning opportunities, and the chance to certify in all four major platforms. Whether you want to broaden your knowledge base or narrow your scope and specialize in a specific sector, you can find your opportunity here. Who You Are You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others. Required Technical and Professional Experience: 7-15 years of experience, including significant hands-on experience in automation engineering, technology development, and enterprise automation operations. Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience with Microsoft Power Platform and/or RPA technologies, including Power Automate, Power Apps, Dataverse, and UiPath. Strong expertise in Power Platform development, including Model-Driven Apps, cloud flows, Dataverse architecture, automation design, and enterprise application integration. Hands-on experience with REST APIs, Dataverse APIs, JSON, XPath, SQL, FetchXML, JavaScript/TypeScript, and enterprise integration development. Experience working with Azure Cloud, Azure SQL, Microsoft 365, GitHub, source control, environment management, and deployment processes. Strong understanding of automation architecture, production support, monitoring, troubleshooting, upgrades, security controls, operational governance, and service management practices. Mandatory Certification: PL-400 (Microsoft Power Platform Developer Associate) or PL-500 (Microsoft Power Automate RPA Developer Associate). Strong technical leadership, stakeholder management, Agile delivery, communication, analytical, problem-solving, and team mentoring capabilities. Preferred Professional and Technical Expertise: Experience with enterprise RPA platforms such as UiPath, Automation Anywhere, or Blue Prism, including orchestration, monitoring, and operational support. Strong knowledge of ITSM processes and tools such as Jira Service Management, Jira, SharePoint, Wrike, or equivalent platforms. Experience designing scalable automation frameworks, reusable components, DevOps practices, and governance models. Microsoft certifications including PL-400 (Power Platform Developer Associate), PL-500 (Power Automate RPA Developer Associate), PL-900, AZ-900, or equivalent certifications. Professional certifications in Agile Service Management, GitHub Copilot, or automation technologies such as UiPath, Automation Anywhere, or Blue Prism are preferred. Being You The “Kyn” in Kyndryl means kinship, which represents the strong bonds we have with each other, our customers and our communities. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way. What You Can Expect Your career with us isn’t just a job—it’s an adventure with purpose. We offer a dynamic, hybrid-friendly culture that supports your well-being and empowers you to grow. Our Be Well programs are thoughtfully designed to support your financial, mental, physical, and social health—because we know that when you feel your best, you do your best. From your very first day, you’ll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won’t just contribute—you’ll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth. We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You’ll develop in-demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting-edge learning opportunities—from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands-on experiences. And through it all, you’ll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success. We want you to thrive here—and we’re committed to helping you do just that. Ready to make an impact? Join us and help shape what’s next. Get Referred! If you know someone that works at Kyndryl, when asked ‘How Did You Hear About Us’ during the application process, select ‘Employee Referral’ and enter your contact's Kyndryl email address.

jobs.title: Software Engineer | Cloud Native BNG Solution Testing, Scale & Performance, Python | 8-12 year
jobs.description: Meet the Team The Cisco cnBNG Solution Testing team validates carrier-grade broadband solutions running on IOS-XR routing platforms, including Cisco 8000, ASR 9000, and NCS 5500/5700. Our focus is ensuring that cnBNG solutions meet demanding service-provider requirements for functionality, scale, performance, resiliency, interoperability, and operational readiness. We validate the cnBNG solution end-to-end across Control Plane and User Plane functions, subscriber protocols, forwarding, high availability, and platform infrastructure. We operate at the intersection of software, hardware, networking, and customer deployments, with an automation-first approach and responsible adoption of AI-assisted engineering practices. Your Impact As a Software Engineer in the cnBNG Solution Testing team, you will own end-to-end solution, scale, performance, and resiliency validation of cnBNG deployments. You will design sophisticated service-provider network topologies, develop comprehensive test strategies, automate large-scale subscriber and traffic scenarios, and validate the system under realistic customer workloads. You will work extensively with traffic-generation platforms such as Keysight IXIA and Spirent, analyze system and forwarding performance, identify bottlenecks, and collaborate with development teams to drive defects to resolution. You will play a critical role in assessing product quality and providing evidence-based recommendations for release readiness. Design and implement end-to-end cnBNG solution testing across Control Plane, User Plane,subscriber management, forwarding, platform infrastructure, and external network elements. Own scale and performance qualification, including subscriber scale, session setup/teardown rates, throughput, latency, packet loss, convergence, CPU/memory utilization, and system behavior under sustained load. Develop realistic service-provider test topologies covering PPPoE, IPoE, DHCPv4/v6, PPP, RADIUS/CoA, L2TP, subscriber policies, accounting, QoS, and subscriber lifecycle scenarios. Build and validate large-scale cnBNG deployments with multiple Control Plane and User Plane nodes. Develop strong proficiency with Keysight IXIA and Spirent traffic generators, including subscriber emulation, protocol emulation, traffic generation, traffic analysis, performance benchmarking, and large-scale test execution. Create traffic profiles that model real-world broadband deployments, including mixed IPv4/IPv6 traffic, multiple packet sizes, bidirectional traffic, QoS classes, and subscriber service profiles. Validate CUPS / CP-UP separation, including session programming, state synchronization, state replay, reconciliation, Control Plane and User Plane failures, and recovery scenarios. Perform comprehensive high-availability and resiliency testing, including SRG geo/warm standby, process restart, node failures, link failures, ISSU, NSR/NSF, control-plane failures, and subscriber session continuity. Validate IOS-XR forwarding functionality including L2/L3 forwarding, FIB/adjacency, MPLS/L3VPN, H-QoS/policing, ACLs, mirroring, OAM/BFD, slowpath, and NPU forwarding behavior. Develop and maintain scalable Python-based test automation using pyATS/Genie or equivalent frameworks, integrating tests into CI/CD pipelines and regression suites. Build reusable automation libraries for topology setup, subscriber provisioning, traffic generation, fault injection, statistics collection, verification, and automated result analysis. Analyze performance trends and identify bottlenecks across software, forwarding hardware, NPU resources, CPU, memory, and control-plane interactions. Perform soak, longevity, stress, negative, boundary, and capacity testing to uncover issues that may only appear under sustained or extreme workloads. Validate subscriber QoS, accounting, lawful intercept, policy enforcement, and other service-provider features under functional and scale conditions. Validate CLI, YANG models, model-driven telemetry, gRPC/NETCONF/gNMI, and operational data required for managing and troubleshooting large cnBNG deployments. Debug sophisticated solution-level issues using IOS-XR logs, traces, telemetry, packet captures, core dumps, IXIA/Spirent statistics, and platform/NPU diagnostics. Perform detailed root-cause isolation, determining whether failures originate in the Control Plane, User Plane, forwarding infrastructure, Silicon One NPU, automation environment, traffic generator, or external network components. Partner closely with development, platform, system architecture, and customer-facing engineering teams to reproduce defects and drive them to closure. Define measurable test exit criteria and provide data-driven release-quality and readiness recommendations based on functional, scale, performance, and resiliency results. Use Git and modern software-development practices for automation code, test reviews, defect management, and CI/CD integration. Actively use approved AI coding assistants and engineering agents for automation development, test generation, log analysis, failure clustering, defect analysis, and troubleshooting while responsibly validating AI-generated output. Mentor junior engineers and help improve solution-testing methodology, automation architecture, scale infrastructure, and overall engineering quality. Minimum Qualifications (Must-Have ) Bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, Telecommunications, or a related field. Strong experience in system, solution, scale, performance, and resiliency testing of networking products or carrier-grade networking solutions. Strong understanding of test methodologies covering functional, integration, system, regression, scale, performance, stress, longevity, failover, and high-availability testing. Hands-on expertise with Keysight IXIA and/or Spirent traffic-generation platforms, including protocol emulation, subscriber emulation, traffic generation, scale testing, and performance analysis. Strong Python programming and experience developing scalable test automation using pyATS/ Genie or equivalent frameworks. Experience integrating automated test suites into CI/CD and continuous regression pipelines. Strong IP networking fundamentals, including L2/L3 forwarding, IPv4/IPv6, routing, MPLS/L3VPN, and QoS. Knowledge of broadband/subscriber technologies and protocols including PPPoE, IPoE, DHCPv4/v6, PPP, RADIUS/CoA, and L2TP. Experience configuring, validating, and solving IOS-XR or another carrier-grade network operating system. Ability to design and implement large-scale network topologies and systematically characterize capacity, throughput, latency, convergence, resource utilization, and failure recovery. Strong understanding of high availability, duplication, subscriber-state management, and fault- recovery mechanisms. Strong Linux skills and experience with Git, debugging tools, packet collections, logs, telemetry, and defect-management systems. Technical Leadership & Mentorship Technical Mentorship: Provide strong technical leadership, architectural guidance, and mentorship to a global team of platform engineers, data architects, and reporting developers. jobs.title: Senior Privacy Engineer – Automation & Data Mapping
jobs.description: Job Description The Senior Privacy Operations Engineer bridges privacy compliance and technical implementation, architecting, building, and maintaining the tooling, automation, and data infrastructure that powers the company’s global privacy program across UK/EU, US, APAC, and other regions. This role works closely with engineering and product teams to operationalize privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default requirements, and owns the technical backbone connecting privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust), work-management systems (e.g., Azure DevOps, Jira), and the organization’s broader data and cloud infrastructure. This is a senior, hands-on engineering role requiring both strong technical depth and working knowledge of global privacy regulatory concepts. Key Responsibilities Privacy Automation Engineering Design, build, and maintain automation for privacy operations workflows, including data subject rights fulfillment, data discovery, data mapping, and privacy assessment triggering. Build and maintain API and Power Automate integrations between privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust) and internal systems (ticketing/ADO/Jira, identity, data stores), including field mapping, assignment logic, bi-directional status sync, and error handling/logging so systems do not drift apart. Implement risk-based conditional logic and trigger workflows for privacy assessments (PIAs/DPIAs/TIAs) tied to intake or procurement systems, including escalation paths for high-risk triggers and governance/audit trails over the trigger rules themselves. Design and maintain automated redaction and exception-flagging pipelines (e.g., keyword/pattern matching, ML classifiers) for DSAR fulfillment, ensuring a mandatory human-review checkpoint before release and maintaining an audit log of redaction decisions. Data Mapping & ROPA Infrastructure Build and maintain an automated, event-driven data flow inventory and data mapping pipeline, tied to system/vendor intake and procurement processes rather than periodic manual surveys. Build and maintain integrations with data discovery and classification tooling (e.g., OneTrust Data Discovery, BigID, Collibra, AWS Macie, Azure Purview, database crawlers) to automatically feed classifications and data flows into ROPA records. Implement drift-detection mechanisms that reconcile ROPA records against discovery/mapping tool outputs, and support metrics such as percentage of ROPA records reviewed within a defined window. Support technical aspects of privacy impact assessments, including data flow diagrams and system/architecture review. Privacy-by-Design Engineering & Product Collaboration Partner with engineering and product teams to implement privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default controls within products and internal systems. Assist in the technical implementation of data retention and deletion requirements across structured and unstructured data sources. Advise engineering teams on technical architecture considerations for new products and features from a privacy and data protection perspective. Program Tooling, Reporting & Observability Build and maintain KPI dashboards and reporting pipelines (e.g., ADO Analytics, Power BI) that translate raw work-item and automation data into executive-ready privacy program metrics (DSAR SLA compliance, assessment backlog, incident response times). Monitor and report on the health of privacy tooling and automated processes, troubleshooting integration or data-quality issues as they arise. Maintain governance over report definitions and automation/trigger rule changes so metrics and workflows remain consistent and trustworthy over time. DSAR & Assessment Automation at Scale Design and maintain automated routing of DSAR tasks with data-owner mapping across multiple systems, SLA tracking tied to statutory deadlines, and tiered escalation as deadlines approach. Build scalable automation and surge-capacity mechanisms (triage automation, templated responses) to support DSAR volume spikes, incorporating lessons learned into ongoing process improvements. Support automation of assessment intake quality, including conditional required fields, real-time validation, and automated reminders to reduce incomplete submissions. Required Qualifications 5-7 years of experience in a data engineering, software engineering, or technical privacy/compliance engineering role, ideally supporting privacy or compliance operations at a global or multinational organization. Strong proficiency in at least one programming/scripting language (e.g., Python, SQL) and demonstrated experience building and maintaining API integrations and automated workflows (e.g., Power Automate, custom scripts, middleware). Hands-on experience building integrations between privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust, BigID, Collibra) and internal systems (ticketing/ADO/Jira, identity, data stores), including field mapping, assignment logic, and bi-directional status sync with error handling. Experience designing and maintaining automated data discovery and data mapping pipelines across structured and unstructured data sources (e.g., AWS Macie, Azure Purview, database crawlers) that feed ROPA records. Experience implementing risk-based conditional logic and trigger workflows for privacy assessments (PIA/DPIA/TIA) tied to intake or procurement systems. Experience building reporting/analytics pipelines (e.g., ADO Analytics, Power BI) that translate raw operational data into KPI dashboards for privacy program leadership. Solid understanding of core privacy concepts (data minimization, purpose limitation, data subject rights, retention) and global privacy regulations (UK GDPR/EU GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, PIPEDA, or similar) as applied to technical system design. Experience working with structured and unstructured data across multiple systems and cloud environments. Preferred Qualifications Experience with privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust, BigID, Collibra) and their APIs/connector frameworks. CIPT certification. Experience with cloud data infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including native discovery/classification services (e.g., Macie, Purview). Experience building automated redaction/exception-flagging pipelines with tuned accuracy and governed human-review checkpoints. Experience supporting DSAR automation at scale, including SLA tracking/escalation design and volume-spike scaling strategies. Experience designing event-driven data mapping architectures integrated with CMDB/asset inventory or cloud discovery tooling. Skills & Competencies Strong systems-design thinking with the ability to balance automation against defensibility and risk Ability to work independently and collaboratively across global engineering, legal, and privacy teams Strong troubleshooting and debugging skills across integrated systems Adaptability to evolving regulatory and technical requirements Clear communication skills to translate technical architecture into terms non-technical privacy and legal stakeholders can act on #LI-KP1 What’s in it For You? jobs.title: SDE, Alexa For Shopping
jobs.description: DESCRIPTION What if you could talk to your Amazon Store? With Alexa+ on Echo Show, customers can now do exactly that. The full Amazon store is live on Echo Show 15 and 21 — a new way to shop at home that combines voice as a natural way to express needs with the product details, reviews, and videos customers rely on to make confident decisions. This product started with an ambitious question and was built from scratch — no prior version to iterate on, no existing architecture to extend, no playbook to follow. The team pioneered novel challenges including rendering the full, always-current Amazon store natively on Echo Show in real time, building visual grounding from scratch so Alexa's responses stay anchored to what the customer sees on screen, and creating a conversational commerce paradigm that lets customers skip screens entirely with natural language. We are seeking a Software Development Engineer to help build the next chapter of this experience — scaling what we've built, expanding to new surfaces and marketplaces, and pushing the boundaries of agentic, multimodal shopping. As an early-career engineer on this team, you'll design and build meaningful components alongside experienced engineers, own your work through design, implementation, testing, and livesite, and grow quickly in a high-ownership environment. This is greenfield, 01 work at the intersection of Generative AI, multimodal experiences, and conversational commerce. You will have the freedom to experiment, learn, and invent on behalf of our customers, and you'll work for a strong leadership team that optimizes for your growth and pairs you with mentors who will guide your career. Key job responsibilities As a Software Development Engineer I on this team, you will: Design, build, test, and operate features that scale and extend the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices. Write high-quality, well-tested code and participate actively in code reviews, both giving and receiving thoughtful feedback. Contribute to systems that render the Amazon store in real time, keep it in sync, and support conversational, multimodal shopping flows. Help extend the experience to new surfaces and international marketplaces, working through ambiguity where there is no existing playbook. Own your components end-to-end through livesite operations — monitoring, on-call participation, and continuous improvement of reliability and performance. Collaborate with engineering, science, product, and design partners across Alexa Shopping, including teammates in Seattle across time zones. Contribute ideas to technical designs, ask good questions, and grow your scope and autonomy over time with support from senior engineers and mentors. A day in the life Here's what a typical day might look like. You'll spend meaningful time building — designing and implementing features that scale the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices, whether that's improving how the store renders in real time, sharpening visual grounding, or extending the experience to a new marketplace. You'll write code, review your teammates', and get thoughtful feedback on yours. Days blend focused coding with a short standup, design conversations where your ideas are genuinely wanted, and pairing with a senior engineer or mentor when you're working through something ambiguous. Because this is 01 work, you'll often be making decisions without a playbook — and that's the fun part. You'll partner closely with engineering, science, product, and design colleagues across Alexa Shopping, many of them in Seattle, so some collaboration spans time zones. Your internal stakeholders are the product, design, and partner engineering teams shaping the Alexa+ shopping experience; your end customers are shoppers at home talking to their Echo Show, expecting it to just work. The problems you'll tackle range from "how do we keep the store always in sync and fast on-device?" to "how do we make a conversational shopping flow feel effortless?" — meaty, customer-facing problems where what you build lands in people's living rooms. About the team We're the team that taught the Amazon Store to talk back. We took an idea that didn't have a blueprint and shipped it to customers' living rooms — and now we're just getting to the fun part: making it bigger, faster, and available to shoppers around the world. Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make shopping on Alexa feel effortless and delightful, no matter where a customer is or which device they reach for. We sit right where voice, vision, and Generative AI meet retail at Amazon scale — which means the problems we solve genuinely haven't been solved before, and the person who cracks them is often the newest engineer with a fresh idea. Culture-wise, we're builders who like ambiguity and dislike bureaucracy. We ship, we learn, we tell stories over chai, and we celebrate the wins (and the instructive failures). We hire smart people and give them room to run — you'll own real problems from day one, with experienced engineers and mentors in your corner, not looking over your shoulder. We take the work seriously and ourselves a little less so. If you like the idea of building something customers can literally talk to, you'll fit right in. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience 2+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience Experience contributing to the architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and current systems PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent 3+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. jobs.title: Senior Principal - EUC / MDM Platform Architect
jobs.description: Business Introduction GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centred on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems. Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines. Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges. Job Purpose Be the definitive technical authority for how 50,000+ employees across [X] countries experience and interact with their devices. This role owns the architecture, reference designs, technical standards and engineering direction for the entire end user computing estate — laptops, desktops, mobiles, tablets, virtual desktops, meeting rooms, and specialised or regulated endpoints. Where the Director owns delivery, budget and people, the Principal Architect owns what good looks like technically and holds the organisation to it. This is a hands-on-capable role: the expectation is to prototype, prove and pressure-test designs personally, not solely to review other people's slides. The Principal Architect is accountable for ensuring the estate is secure by design, cloud-native, automatable, cost-efficient and — critically — genuinely pleasant to use. They are the person who says no to architecture that will not survive contact with 50,000 users, and who can explain why in terms both engineers and executives accept. Key Responsibilities Own the target-state architecture for end user computing: platform selection, device management topology, identity integration, application delivery, security control placement and telemetry. Produce and maintain reference architectures, design patterns, technical standards and architecture decision records (ADRs) — with trade-offs made explicit rather than buried. Define the technical roadmap that underpins the EUC strategy: platform migrations, deprecations, convergence of fragmented tooling, and the sequencing that makes it deliverable. Continuously evaluate the market — modern management, AI PCs and on-device inference, cloud PC/DaaS economics, zero-trust endpoint models — and separate genuine capability from vendor narrative. Act as the design authority for all endpoint change: chair or sit on the EUC architecture review board, approve significant designs, and hold veto on standards deviation. Set and police the exception process — make the right path the easy path, and make deviations visible, time-bound and owned. Review and assure supplier and MSP technical designs; ensure partners build to the organisation's architecture rather than their own delivery convenience. Set engineering standards for configuration-as-code, packaging, testing, release management and rollback across the endpoint estate. Prototype and prove new capability in a lab before it reaches production; build the reference implementation the engineering teams then industrialise. Mentor and technically develop senior engineers and platform leads; raise the ceiling of the whole team, not just your own output. Partner with Cyber Security to embed zero-trust principles at the endpoint: device trust and attestation, conditional access, least privilege, application control, EDR and DLP placement. Architect for regulated and validated environments — GxP-qualified endpoints, computer system validation (CSV/CSA), data residency and privacy obligations, and audit/SOX ITGC evidence generation as a designed-in property rather than a manual scramble. Own the technical response to endpoint-relevant threat scenarios and drive architectural remediation of systemic vulnerabilities. Architect the digital employee experience (DEX) telemetry model: what is measured, how it is collected, where it lands, and how it drives automated remediation. Design for self-healing and self-service by default; treat every recurring ticket category as an architectural defect until proven otherwise. Translate architecture into business consequence for senior stakeholders — cost, risk, productivity, time-to-value. Represent EUC architecture in enterprise architecture forums, security governance, and vendor executive briefings. Professional Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent demonstrable professional expertise. Relevant certifications desirable (e.g., Microsoft Certified: Endpoint Administrator Expert, Azure Solutions Architect Expert, Cybersecurity Architect Expert, Jamf Certified Expert, TOGAF, CISSP or SABSA). Area of Specialisation End user computing architecture at global enterprise scale — platform selection, device management topology, identity integration, application delivery and telemetry. Modern endpoint management (Intune/MECM) and macOS management (Jamf), including co-management, hybrid-to-cloud-native migration and staged ring-based rollout. Endpoint security architecture and zero-trust design — device trust, conditional access, application control, EDR/XDR, DLP and secure baselines. Regulated and validated endpoint environments — GxP-qualified endpoints, CSV/CSA, data residency and audit/SOX ITGC evidence generation designed in. Experience Required Overall 15 years and 12+ years in IT infrastructure or end user computing, including 5+ years in a principal, lead or enterprise architect capacity with recognised design authority. Architecture ownership for an endpoint estate of 20,000+ devices across multiple countries and regulatory jurisdictions. Expert-level, hands-on-derived command of modern endpoint management (Intune/MECM) and macOS management — sufficient to build the reference implementation personally, not only to specify it. Demonstrable advanced scripting and automation portfolio; evidence of configuration-as-code applied to a production endpoint estate. Working fluency in enterprise endpoint security and zero-trust architecture, with a track record of co-designing controls alongside a Cyber Security function. Led the architecture of at least one large-scale endpoint platform migration or transformation through to production, including the failures and what was learned from them. Able to produce architecture documentation of a standard that withstands external audit and supplier scrutiny. Proven credibility with both senior engineers and executive stakeholders, in English, in a global matrixed organisation. Willingness to travel internationally, approximately [5–15]% of the time. Desirable: Experience in a regulated industry — pharmaceutical, life sciences, biotech, financial services or healthcare — with practical GxP/CSV/CSA and Annex 11 / 21 CFR Part 11 exposure. Architecture for specialised endpoints: laboratory instrument workstations, manufacturing and shop-floor devices, clinical and field devices, kiosks, shared and multi-user workstations. Leading a major platform transformation: SCCM-to-Intune migration, Windows 10 11 at scale, MSP transition, or M&A integration/divestment of an endpoint estate. Sustainability-aware design — device longevity, power management, refurbishment and Scope 3 implications of architectural choices. Accessibility and assistive technology designed into the standard build rather than bolted on. Network fundamentals relevant to endpoints — SASE/ZTNA, split tunnelling, Wi-Fi 6/7, certificate-based network access. Contribution to the wider community — open-source tooling, conference speaking, published technical writing, vendor customer advisory boards. Skills/Background Deep technical breadth across Windows and macOS internals, modern endpoint management, identity, endpoint security, application delivery, virtual desktop / cloud PC, and mobile — with the judgement to know where tenant-wide standardisation matters and where a business exception is defensible. Advanced PowerShell and at least one general-purpose language (Python, C#, Go) applied to real automation, not toy scripts. Configuration-as-code and GitOps discipline — version-controlled endpoint configuration, CI/CD for policy and package deployment, automated testing and staged ring-based rollout as the default way endpoint change is delivered. API-first integration — Microsoft Graph, ServiceNow, MDM and security tool APIs; designing integrations that survive vendor change. Telemetry and data craft — designing measurement into the estate, with competence in the query languages and platforms the data lands in (KQL, Log Analytics, Power BI or equivalent). Architectural discipline — reference designs, ADRs, HLD/LLD, and the ability to write clearly enough that others can build from it and external auditors can accept it. Trade-off reasoning — cost, risk, experience, security and operability weighed explicitly; comfortable being the person who quantifies the uncomfortable option. Scale intuition — designing for 50,000 devices, unreliable networks, disconnected users, and the long tail of exceptions that always exists. Technical leadership without authority — landing decisions across engineering, security, service delivery and vendors by credibility and evidence. Executive communication — making architecture legible and decision-ready for non-technical leadership. Constructive challenge — able to disagree with a Director, a vendor or a security architect and keep the relationship intact. Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. The job holder works with product teams, R&D partners and manufacturing technology teams to define practical strategies for connecting data and systems (including the use of ontologies, knowledge graphs, integrations and AI (Artificial Intelligence) where appropriate), enabling more seamless reuse of product and process knowledge across platforms. They also help define and operate the technical foundations (data pipelines, integrations, environments and deployments) needed to run these digital and AI-enabled capabilities safely and at scale, and to demonstrate that product and process data is being reused across R&D, CMC and commercial systems with improved data quality and time-to-access. Key Responsibilities: Set up and maintain CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment) pipelines and integration flows to move digital product profile data between PDLM (Product Data & Lifecycle Management) and other systems, using agreed branching strategies and automated checks. Ensure pipeline, integration and mapping code is kept under version control, automatically tested and peer-reviewed before release, so changes remain traceable, repeatable and supportable. Use approved AI tools and collaborate with AI and analytics teams to provision data pipelines, integrations, environments and access patterns that enable safe AI proofs of concept and AI-assisted mapping of data models and ontologies, improving productivity and ways of working while validating outputs and following GSK’s Responsible AI, privacy and security requirements. Own the design of data and integration services within enterprise architecture guardrails, documenting decisions, trade-offs and rationale in decision records and technical documentation. Define environment promotion flows (e.g. DEV, TEST, VAL, PROD (Development / Test / Validation / Production) for data and integration services supporting R&D, CMC and commercial use of product and process data. Support releases and integrations end-to-end: maintain pipelines, automate deployments, manage repositories and environments and ensure changes follow validation and change-control requirements. Work with R&D and central ontology / knowledge-graph teams to implement and operate data and metadata structures (for example applying agreed ontologies, reference data and mappings) so digital product profile data can be linked and reused across platforms, without owning the ontology roadmap itself. Design and support integration patterns between PDLM and key downstream systems (such as MES (Manufacturing Execution System), LES (Laboratory Execution System)/LIMS (Laboratory Information Management System), ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning), control and regulatory/CMC platforms) so product and process data can flow reliably from source to execution and submissions. Make practical use of AI-assisted development, agent-based workflows and prompt templates for engineering, testing, documentation and support, validating every AI output for accuracy, security, (Good Practice) GxP/data integrity and maintainability before it is committed or released, and applying Responsible AI, data privacy and cyber security controls. Monitor and troubleshoot data pipelines, integrations, environments and related services, including performance and data quality, and drive sustainable remediation for recurring issues. Document data flows, integration contracts, deployment patterns and runbooks and keep this documentation aligned with evolving product and system changes, including decision records and standards. Coach engineers and analysts working on digital product profile, data and integration work, and define and maintain data and integration engineering standards by reviewing engineering practices and establishing reusable models, patterns, templates and knowledge. Drive continuous improvement in reliability, observability, performance and security for data and integration services supporting the digital product profile and transformation use cases, using measures such as data reuse, data quality and time-to-access. Minimum 7 years’ experience in data engineering, integration engineering, DevOps or similar roles in complex enterprise or manufacturing environments. Experience in designing and delivering data and integration solutions spanning R&D, CMC and/or manufacturing domains, including PDLM or equivalent digital product profile platforms. Experience in working with ontologies, controlled vocabularies or knowledge-graph technologies to link data across systems, in collaboration with central ontology and data standards teams. Experience in enabling AI/ML or advanced analytics through well-designed datasets, features and integration points. Experience in using AI-assisted development, agent-based workflows and prompt templates for engineering, testing, documentation and support, with application of Responsible AI, data privacy, cyber security and GxP controls. Experience in integrating with or working on manufacturing, laboratory or quality systems (for example MES, LES/LIMS, ERP, control or regulatory/CMC platforms). Experience in partnering with DevOps or platform teams to deploy and operate data and integration services, including pipelines, environments, monitoring and incident response. Preferred Qualifications: Apply analytical and troubleshooting skills applied to complex data and integration issues. jobs.title: Applied Scientist II, Amazon Business - External Integrations
jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Amazon Business System Integrations connects Amazon Business with millions of business users and thousands of partner procurement, ERP, and finance systems. We build the APIs, protocols, and agentic experiences that let customers buy on Amazon Business directly from the systems they already use. As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will own and advance the ML and GenAI capabilities that make these integrations smarter, faster, and more reliable. You will drive model accuracy, scientific innovation, and global scale across external systems integrations. Our work includes API-based and protocol-based shopping, such as punchout and emerging agent protocols, along with agentic interactions where buyers and AI agents search, compare, and purchase through natural language. It also covers partner onboarding and integration automation, mapping and normalizing catalog, product, and order data across many partner formats, and evaluation frameworks that measure the quality, accuracy, and latency of our agents. Key job responsibilities As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will work across three dimensions: Invent, Implement, and Influence. Invent: You bring deep domain knowledge and fluency with state-of-the-art scientific approaches and emerging research. You practice customer-obsessed science, working backwards from the needs of business buyers, procurement teams, and integration partners to extend or invent new ML approaches, even when no textbook solution exists. You design novel ML and LLM-based methods for agentic shopping, product search and matching, schema and data mapping across partner systems, and automated evaluation of agent quality. You help define the research agenda for our agentic and protocol-based capabilities, and you lead the scientific strategy for accurate, low-latency responses in conversational and API-driven procurement. You author or co-author articles for internal or external peer-reviewed venues when appropriate and not precluded by business considerations. Implement: The ML components you develop are integrated directly into production systems serving Amazon Business customers and partners worldwide. You make sound tradeoffs between accuracy and latency, innovation and stability, and short-term and long-term solutions, favoring reuse and established frameworks where appropriate. You make progress semi-autonomously with only occasional guidance, implement at the right level of complexity the first time, and evaluate emerging technologies, including LLMs and GenAI frameworks, largely on your own. You ensure your models and pipelines integrate robustly with catalog, offer, cart, order, and partner data sources and with the services that power external integrations. Influence: You contribute to planning for the team, including goals, priorities, and roadmaps for ML and GenAI capabilities. You lead the scientific strategy for expanding agentic and integration capabilities across new partners, protocols, and countries. You collaborate with engineering, product, and program teams across Amazon Business so that data integration and ML pipelines are robust and scale with adoption. You mentor scientists and engineers, champion best practices for the AI-Driven Development Life Cycle (AIDLC), and provide peer feedback on research methods and results. You help recruit bar-raising talent through interview drives, and you are visible in the broader scientific community as a subject matter expert, including serving as a Program Committee member or reviewer for peer-reviewed venues. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of building models for business application experience Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing Master's degree, or PhD PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience using Unix/Linux Experience in professional software development Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner. null

You also decide whether a problem needs an agent, a simpler automation, or nothing at all, and you have explicit authority to stop or re-scope work that won’t deliver impact. You thrive in ambiguous environments with a low-ego mindset, leveraging AI coding tools as core collaborative partners in your engineering workflow. Leverage full-stack engineering across backend services, APIs, data models, interactive screens, approval UIs, and chat interfaces as the complete medium to deliver high-ownership, user-facing agent systems. Apply solid software engineering practices to AI systems, treating prompts, skills, configs, and specs as versioned artifacts, with code review, tests, CI or CD, and staged rollouts. Implement evaluation, guardrails, and quality control: derive evals from workflow data, establish quality gates and guardrails, integrate human-in-the-loop approvals where needed, and monitor production runs to refine agents over time. Use measured results to decide how to evolve or retire agents, and turn successful systems into patterns and libraries that can be reused. Experience you’ll need (must haves) Around 7 or more years of professional software engineering experience in production systems, and around 2 or more years of professional, hands-on experience building AI agents and agent powered production applications with measurable outcomes. Strong full stack engineering background, with a track record of designing, building, and owning services end to end, including backend APIs and integrations, data models, and user facing interfaces such as approval UIs, dashboards, or chat surfaces. A builder mindset: comfortable defining baselines and metrics, reporting results in business terms, working in a fast moving environment, and closing the loop by building, demoing, learning, and building again. If you like seeing improvements in hours saved, errors avoided, and teams unblocked, you will have plenty of chances to measure that here. Software engineering skills and best practices System design: break down complex problems, design APIs and data models, reason about latency, throughput, and failure modes, and choose simple, robust architectures. Algorithms, data structures, access control permissions, and data provenance. Spec driven development: turn vague requirements into clear problem statements, write or refine design docs, and use a Spec Plan Task Code Converge flow so work is traceable from design to code, including when you use AI coding agents. Execution discipline: use version control, code review, automated tests, CI or CD, staged rollouts and rollbacks, logging, metrics, and tracing, and improve systems based on issues and signals from production. Design robust agent harnesses and multi agent orchestrations: model tools and resources, manage context and state, and keep runs reliable under real world data and load. Establish continuous evaluation and safety mechanisms: turn production failures into test cases, gate changes on eval suite results, and enforce guardrails across agent workflows. Exercise clear judgment on AI fit: decide when a problem needs an agent versus a simpler automation or no build, and make tradeoffs around model choice, latency and cost, context strategy, and autonomy using data rather than intuition. jobs.title: Senior / Lead Platform Forward Deployed Engineer - Cogentiq I2C
jobs.description: It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they are doing! We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business. About Cogentiq I2C Cogentiq I2C is Fractal's agentic AI platform for invoice-to-cash operations, spanning Collections, Cash Application, Deductions, Credit Risk, and Invoice Management. The platform runs on a four-tier architecture: a Next.js application layer, FastAPI services, the Cogentiq APA agentic orchestration layer, and a data estate built on Azure Databricks and PostgreSQL. Deployments land in client Azure tenancies against live ERP data (Dynamics 365, SAP), which means deployment engineering is a first-class discipline, not an afterthought to development. Why this role, now The platform has crossed from being built to being deployed. Collections is entering pilot with enterprise clients, and the deployment machinery is real: Databricks Asset Bundles with one-click, script-based deployment; auto-loader ingestion running historical and incremental loads into a common data model; versioned bundles and wheel-file packages delivered through Git and Azure Artifactory; and a quick-start standard under which a newcomer must be able to stand up the full data platform by running one setup script. This role carries that machinery into client environments and makes it hold under client governance, client data, and client timelines. It owns everything between our release artefacts and a running, observable, correctly governed installation; candidates who want to work on agent behaviour and LLM integration should apply to the AI FDE track instead. What you will do Own the deployment architecture of client installations from environment readiness through hypercare: bundle strategy, environment topology (Dev, QA, production; per-client catalogs), release sequencing, and sign-off that the installation meets the validation standard. Navigate Unity Catalog and platform governance Client and internal IT control catalog and metastore provisioning, storage decisions, and access models. You will assess what their governance model means for our setup scripts, negotiate provisioning paths, and know when a shared-infrastructure convenience creates an SOW, NDA, or data-isolation problem that must be escalated rather than worked around. Set and enforce the platform engineering standards: idempotent, rerunnable deployments; fail-fast error handling with no silent except-and-continue paths; environment-variable-driven parameterisation with a single point of change per client value; and configuration conventions that hold across Databricks today and Fabric tomorrow. Own the shared utilities architecture: interface-function contracts and factory-pattern abstractions across Databricks, Fabric, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and storage back ends, packaged as versioned wheel files through Azure Artifactory, so swapping a client's platform is a configuration change, not a rewrite. Make the hard ingestion calls: auto-loader versus custom conflict-driven ingestion when the client will not provision Databricks, checkpoint and reprocessing strategy, retry and alerting design per pipeline, and writeback reliability to the application database. Run incident command during deployment and hypercare. When a deployment breaks in a client environment, you run the incident: triage across the data estate, the application database, and upstream ERP feeds; communicate honestly with the client; and land the fix and the post-incident correction to the playbook. Own the deployment playbook as a product. The quick-start guides, validation suites, and synthetic data configurations you leave behind must make the next deployment cheaper. The bar is that a newcomer deploys the platform from your playbook with one setup script. Coach junior Platform FDEs, reviewing their work against the standards you set and growing them toward deployment ownership. What You need 6 or more years in data platform or deployment engineering, with at least two years deploying into environments you did not control (client tenancies, regulated environments, or equivalent). Deep Azure Databricks: Asset Bundles, workflows, Unity Catalog and metastore governance, cluster and library management, service-principal automation, and the CLI. Strong Python and SQL, with the judgement to review pipeline code for idempotency, failure behaviour, and configuration hygiene, not just correctness. PostgreSQL in production: schema evolution, write reliability, connection behaviour under load. CI/CD for data platforms: Git-based release flows, semantic versioning, artefact repositories, and backward compatibility across component versions. Domain literacy in order-to-cash and accounts receivable data: invoices, receipts, remittances, customer masters, and ERP AR structures in Dynamics 365 or SAP. You cannot validate a deployment whose data you do not understand. Client-facing composure: you will be the technical face of the deployment to client IT and finance stakeholders. Nice to have: Microsoft Fabric, observability design (OpenTelemetry, Application Insights), and experience taking a data product through pilots at multiple clients in parallel. Success in the first year Two client deployments taken from environment readiness through hypercare, each validated against the standard suite and signed off on schedule. A deployment playbook that demonstrably reduced the cost of the deployment that followed it, measured in elapsed time from access granted to validated installation. Platform standards (idempotency, fail-fast, parameterisation) adopted across the data engineering codebase, evidenced in review practice, not just documentation. At least one governance or infrastructure negotiation with client IT resolved without escalation to leadership. If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us! Not the right fit? jobs.title: Research Engineer – Generative AI and Computer Vision
jobs.description: Company Description Bosch Global Software Technologies Private Limited is a 100% owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH, one of the world's leading global supplier of technology and services, offering end-to-end Engineering, IT and Business Solutions. With over 27,000+ associates, it’s the largest software development center of Bosch, outside Germany, indicating that it is the Technology Powerhouse of Bosch in India with a global footprint and presence in the US, Europe and the Asia Pacific region. Job Description Role Overview The Research Engineer – Generative AI and Computer Vision focuses on advancing state-of-the-art Generative AI and deep learning methods for real-world computer vision applications. The role combines applied research, experimentation, and engineering to develop robust AI solutions for image understanding, synthetic data generation, visual inspection, and continuous model monitoring. The role will contribute to applied research and development of scalable AI capabilities spanning the full computer vision lifecycle—from data preparation and model development to deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement. The work will address practical challenges such as limited or imbalanced training data, rare events, changing image conditions, data drift, and model-performance degradation in operation. This role offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced AI research and real-world deployment, translating novel Generative AI and computer vision methods into reliable and scalable solutions across a range of industrial and business applications. Roles & Responsibilities : Generative AI and Synthetic Data: Research, design, and implement Generative AI approaches for creating realistic and diverse synthetic image datasets. Explore diffusion models, generative adversarial networks, image-to-image generation, controllable generation, and related techniques to address limited data, rare defects, class imbalance, and long-tail inspection scenarios. Computer Vision Model Development: Develop and evaluate deep learning models for industrial image inspection tasks such as image classification, defect detection, anomaly detection, object detection, segmentation, and representation learning. Work with CNN-based, transformer-based, and multimodal architectures. Data-Efficient Learning: Investigate methods including transfer learning, self-supervised learning, few-shot learning, domain adaptation, active learning, and synthetic data augmentation to reduce annotation effort and improve model performance under limited-data conditions. Model Monitoring and Robustness: Develop methods for continuously monitoring deployed inspection models and image-data pipelines. This includes detecting data drift, changes in image conditions, model-performance degradation, confidence shifts, unusual defect patterns, and out-of-distribution inputs. Research and Experimentation: Formulate research hypotheses, design controlled experiments and ablation studies, establish appropriate evaluation benchmarks, and analyze results with scientific rigor. Compare state-of-the-art methods and identify approaches suitable for industrial deployment. Prototype and Product Integration: Build proof-of-concept solutions and research prototypes using Python and modern deep learning frameworks. Collaborate with software, cloud, MLOps, manufacturing, and domain teams to integrate validated methods into scalable AI platforms and applications. Scalable AI Lifecycle: Contribute to capabilities covering data preparation, model training, validation, deployment, monitoring, retraining, and continuous improvement across the complete computer vision model lifecycle. Technology Transfer and Scientific Impact: Translate research outcomes into scalable and production-ready AI components. Document technical findings, communicate results to technical and business stakeholders, and contribute to publications, invention disclosures, patents, reusable frameworks, and Bosch’s intellectual-property portfolio. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with global research, engineering, manufacturing, and product teams to understand inspection requirements and convert real-world challenges into well-defined AI research and development problems. Qualifications Educational qualification: Ph.D. or M.S. or M. Tech from top Indian or foreign institutes (IITs, IIITs, IISc etc.) in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, Electronics and Communication Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. Experience : At least 3 years of relevant professional or applied research experience in computer vision, deep learning, Generative AI, machine learning, or related areas. Mandatory/requires Skills : Strong understanding of machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision fundamentals. Hands-on experience developing computer vision solutions using techniques such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and other sequence models where applicable, transformers, autoencoders, and other modern neural-network architectures. Strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch. Experience with supporting libraries such as NumPy, pandas, OpenCV, scikit-learn, and common image-processing libraries. Practical experience with transformer-based vision models, such as Vision Transformers, hierarchical vision transformers, detection transformers, or related architectures. Hands-on knowledge of Generative AI methods for image data, particularly diffusion models, generative adversarial networks, variational autoencoders, or image-to-image generation methods. Experience designing synthetic data-generation or advanced data-augmentation pipelines for training and evaluating computer vision models. Experience with one or more computer vision tasks such as image classification, object detection, semantic or instance segmentation, anomaly detection, defect detection, or visual similarity learning. Experience with the Hugging Face ecosystem (models, libraries, and SDKs) for rapid prototyping and evaluation of state-of-the-art AI models. Hands-on experience with model evaluation methodologies and metrics (such as Precision, Recall, F1-score, AUC, and ROC), including the rigorous interpretation of results to optimize model decision thresholds. Ability to formulate research questions, design rigorous experiments and ablation studies, establish evaluation metrics, benchmark alternative approaches, and interpret empirical results. Understanding of model generalization, domain shift, data drift, out-of-distribution detection, uncertainty estimation, and model-performance monitoring. Good software-engineering practices, including version control, modular implementation, code reviews, testing, technical documentation, and reproducible experimentation. Strong analytical, problem-solving, presentation, and communication skills. Ability to collaborate effectively with interdisciplinary and geographically distributed teams. Preferred Skills - Any of the following will be an added advantage : Experience applying computer vision to industrial quality inspection, automated optical inspection, manufacturing, robotics, medical imaging, autonomous systems, or other safety- or quality-critical applications. Experience with synthetic defect generation, rare-event simulation, controllable image generation, domain randomization, or simulation-to-real transfer. Familiarity with vision-language models, multimodal foundation models, zero-shot or open-vocabulary vision methods, and parameter-efficient model adaptation (PEFT techniques such as LoRA, QLoRA etc.). Knowledge of self-supervised learning, contrastive learning, active learning, weakly supervised learning, few-shot learning, and continual learning. Experience with monitoring metrics and techniques such as input-data drift, feature drift, prediction drift, confidence calibration, outlier detection, defect-rate analysis, and alert generation. Familiarity with MLOps practices and tools for experiment tracking, model registries, automated training pipelines, containerization, deployment, observability, and model lifecycle management. Experience deploying machine learning models using cloud platforms and container technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes. Knowledge of model optimization methods—including quantization, pruning, knowledge distillation, efficient inference, and deployment on edge or resource-constrained systems—with exposure to tools like TensorRT and ONNX Runtime, and industrial vision standards/software like NeuroCheck and MVTec HALCON. Publications in recognized AI, machine learning, or computer vision venues, or demonstrated experience contributing to patents and invention disclosures. Experience working with large-scale real-world image datasets and developing AI solutions beyond academic benchmark datasets. Familiarity with GenAI-assisted software-development and research tools to improve experimentation and development productivity.

Deliver AI products at scale Own end-to-end delivery for your teams’ commitments: multi-quarter roadmap, dependency management, realistic sequencing, and predictable shipping without heroics. Partner with Product Management, Design, Data, Security, and SRE to turn ambiguous problem statements into shipped, measurable AI capabilities. Move AI work from promising prototype to durable production system — reliability targets, monitoring, graceful degradation, rollback, and on-call ownership. Make disciplined trade-offs between customer-visible quality, delivery speed, and long-term platform investment, and explain those trade-offs credibly to executives. Partner globally with US teams Operate as a peer to AI Engineering, product, and architecture leaders in the US — jointly owning strategy rather than receiving it. Represent India AI Engineering in global planning, architecture councils, and executive reviews, and bring back context that helps your teams make better local decisions. Ensure AI systems handling sensitive workforce and HR data meet privacy, residency, and security obligations (GDPR, India’s DPDP Act, customer contractual commitments, SOC 2 / ISO controls). Partner with Legal, Security, and Privacy on AI governance, vendor and model risk review, and customer-facing AI transparency commitments.
