jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer III
jobs.description:
Experience range: 8-13 Yrs
Job Description About the role Swiggy s Data Platform enables teams to move, process, and use data reliably at scale. As an SDE III, you will design and build foundational platform capabilities across data ingestion, distributed compute, storage, and serving. You will own problems end to end-from architecture and implementation through rollout, observability, and operations-and help raise the engineering bar for the team. This role is for an engineer who enjoys solving difficult systems problems: keeping data pipelines dependable as volumes and workloads grow, making platform behavior predictable for users, and improving performance and cost without compromising correctness or governance. What you ll do Design, build, and operate scalable data-platform services and distributed systems used by product, analytics, and machine-learning teams. Develop reliable batch and streaming data processing and ingestion capabilities, with clear guarantees around correctness, recovery, and data freshness. Improve the performance, availability, and cost efficiency of data workloads through sound architecture, measurement, and iterative optimization. Build platform abstractions and self-service workflows that make common data tasks easier and safer for engineering and data users. Establish strong operational practices: observability, alerting, capacity planning, incident response, and durable root-cause fixes. Apply access control, data governance, and safe change-management practices to production systems and datasets. Lead technical design reviews, break down ambiguous problems, and make pragmatic decisions that balance speed, reliability, and maintainability. Partner with infrastructure, product, analytics, and machine-learning teams to understand needs and deliver platform capabilities with measurable outcomes. Mentor engineers through design and code reviews, and contribute to a culture of ownership and continuous improvement. What you ll bring 8+ years of software engineering experience building and operating production systems, including meaningful experience with distributed systems or data infrastructure. Strong programming skills in one or more languages such as Java, Scala, Python, or Go, and the ability to write maintainable, well-tested code. A solid understanding of distributed computing concepts, data structures, concurrency, fault tolerance, and system design. Hands-on experience with large-scale data processing or streaming technologies-for example, Apache Spark, Kafka, Flink, or comparable systems. Experience designing reliable data pipelines and working with data storage formats, lakehouse systems, or analytical warehouses. Good SQL skills and an understanding of data modeling, partitioning, performance tuning, and data-quality concerns. Experience operating cloud-based production systems, including monitoring, troubleshooting, and managing service reliability. A strong sense of ownership: you can take a problem from an unclear requirement to a production solution and its ongoing health. Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively across engineering and data-focused teams. It s a plus if you have Experience with platforms such as Databricks, Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Snowflake, or similar technologies. Experience building multi-tenant platforms, developer tooling, or self-service infrastructure. Experience with data governance, lineage, access control, or privacy-aware data systems. A track record of improving reliability, performance, or infrastructure cost at significant scale. Experience leading technical initiatives and helping other engineers grow. How success looks Data workloads become more reliable and easier to operate as platform usage and complexity grow. Platform users can onboard and run workloads with less manual intervention and clearer operational feedback. Improvements to performance, cost, freshness, or reliability are measurable and sustained. Technical decisions and production changes are well documented, observable, and safe to evolve. Qualifications 8+ years of software engineering experience building and operating production systems, including meaningful experience with distributed systems or data infrastructure. jobs.title: Assistant Manager - Supply
jobs.description:
Experience range: 4-6 Yrs
Job Summary About the Role: Member-only hotel rates are the first promise CREW makes. This role is the person who makes that promise true. We are looking for a commercially sharp Assistant Manager - Hotel Supply Partnerships to build CREWs directly contracted hotel portfolio. You will sit down with hotels, resorts and regional chains across our priority markets and negotiate the rate, the inclusions and the terms that let a CREW member book a stay that is visibly better than what theyd get on any public OTA. Half this job is deal-making. The other half is a daily discipline: knowing every morning where CREWs rate stands against the market on the properties that matter, spotting the parity break or the undercut the day it appears, and doing something about it before a member sees a cheaper price elsewhere. This is a build role, not a maintenance one. The portfolio is early: youll be working from where our members actually travel and where were currently losing bookings on price, and closing those gaps property by property, city by city. Youll also own what happens after the signature - getting the rate loaded, mapped and live, holding the hotel to the terms when a member is standing at the front desk, and renewing on better commercials next season. Were looking for someone with genuine hotel supply-side experience - OTA, bedbank or wholesaler, TMC, hotel chain sales or revenue management, or a DMC - who has signed contracts themselves and knows the commercial vocabulary cold. The ideal candidate is street-smart in a negotiation, comfortable arguing a rate with data in hand, and has the ownership to chase a contract from first meeting to first booking without waiting for perfect clarity. jobs.description:
Experience range: 0-5 Yrs
Job Summary The developer-led GTM playbook for DevTools and API products in B2B 2026: bottom-up adoption, technical content, dev-relations, sales-led motion. Key Takeaways 1. Developer-led GTM is bottom-up by default. Developers discover DevTools through technical content, peer recommendation, GitHub browsing, Stack Overflow answers, and trial-based exploration. The classic B2B SaaS sales-led motion (cold outbound, demo request, sales-led trial) actively repels developers. Bottom-up adoption is the default GTM motion for DevTools. 2. Technical content is the primary marketing asset. Documentation, API references, code samples, GitHub repositories, technical blogs, and tutorials drive 70 85% of DevTools acquisition. Conventional content marketing (blog posts, case studies, gated whitepapers) plays a secondary role. The marketing team that writes documentation as if it were marketing wins; the team that writes blogs without documentation depth loses. 3. Freemium and free trial economics differ from horizontal SaaS. Free-to-paid conversion rates for DevTools run 1 3% on freemium and 8 18% on free trial lower than horizontal SaaS because developers evaluate technically before committing. The acquisition economics work because LTV/CAC ratios run 4 8x at scale when product-led adoption replaces sales-led acquisition cost. 4. DevRel and marketing are not the same function. Developer Relations (DevRel) handles community engagement, technical content, conference speaking, GitHub presence, and developer feedback. Marketing handles paid acquisition, demand generation, brand positioning, and enterprise sales support. Confusing the two produces underperformance DevRel run as marketing kills technical credibility; marketing run as DevRel produces inefficient demand generation. 5. Enterprise expansion requires sales-led motion at scale. Pure bottom-up DevTools companies hit enterprise expansion ceilings around $100M ARR because procurement, security review, compliance review, and contract negotiation require sales-led motion that pure PLG can't provide. The right model: PLG for SMB and mid-market, sales-led overlay for enterprise triggered by usage thresholds, multi-team expansion signals, and seat-count growth. 6. Paid acquisition for DevTools is technical-content-first. Google Ads CPCs for DevTools run -25 moderate. The right configuration: paid acquisition drives traffic to documentation, code samples, and signup pages not book a demo landing pages. LinkedIn works for enterprise expansion (CTO, VP Eng, Director of Platform targeting), not initial developer adoption. 7. Community channels are non-negotiable. GitHub presence (stars, contributions, public repos), Stack Overflow tag activity, Reddit (r/programming, r/devops, vertical subreddits), Hacker News, Discord/Slack communities, and Dev.to drive 25-40% of DevTools acquisition. Vendors absent from these channels are invisible to developer audiences. 8. The GrowthSpree MCP unifies DevTools pipeline. Six platforms Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, GA4, GSC, HubSpot or Salesforce, and product usage analytics into one natural-language interface. A senior operator asks Claude: For our enterprise prospects, which accounts have 5+ developers using the free tier and have engaged with enterprise content in the last 30 days These are PLG-to-sales-led expansion triggers. Answer in 2 minutes. Disclaimer: This job posting has been aggregated from external source. Role details, content, and availability are subject to change. Ability to recognize AML and sanctions red flags and suspicious transaction patterns. Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills. Strong attention to detail and ability to document investigation rationale clearly. Ability to manage case volumes while meeting productivity, quality and SLA targets. Good written and verbal communication skills. Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word and other MS Office applications . Preferred Experience / Tools Exposure to one or more screening, KYC or transaction-monitoring platforms would be advantageous, for example: World-Check LexisNexis Fenergo NICE Actimize FircoSoft Dow Jones Risk & Compliance Client-specific or proprietary AML monitoring platforms Education Bachelor's degree

This role combines strategic technical leadership with practical software engineering. You will work across a complex landscape of services, APIs, infrastructure and engineering teams, helping to simplify the platform, reduce operational complexity and improve engineering effectiveness. Success depends on working collaboratively with engineers, architects, product teams and stakeholders to develop solutions that teams understand, support and ultimately own. You will provide technical leadership, challenge thinking, facilitate decision-making and help teams align around a shared technical direction. You will remain hands-on, contributing code, solving complex technical problems, building prototypes and helping teams deliver high-quality software at scale. Lead the simplification and modernisation of a complex technology estate, reducing technical debt, operational burden and unnecessary complexity. Work collaboratively with teams to design scalable, resilient and maintainable solutions that can be confidently built, operated and supported. Remain actively involved in software engineering through coding, design reviews, prototyping and technical problem solving. Improve engineering effectiveness through better tooling, automation, developer experience, platform capabilities and engineering practices. Champion modern software engineering practices, including AI-assisted development, intelligent automation and agentic tooling, helping teams improve productivity, quality and delivery outcomes. Improve platform reliability, observability, operational excellence and long-term maintainability. Coach, mentor and influence engineers across multiple teams, raising technical standards and strengthening engineering capability Requirements Significant experience designing, building and evolving large-scale distributed systems and platforms. Strong software engineering background with the ability to contribute high-quality production code. Proven experience simplifying complex technology estates and driving architectural evolution. Experience influencing technical direction across multiple teams and organisations without direct authority. Strong understanding of architecture, platform engineering, DevOps, reliability and operational excellence. Excellent communication, collaboration and stakeholder management skills. A pragmatic approach to technology decisions, balancing innovation with reliability, maintainability and business outcomes. Passion for engineering excellence, continuous improvement and modern software engineering practices. Success in This Role The Store Operations platform is simpler, more scalable and easier to maintain. Engineering teams are more productive and able to deliver value faster. Operational complexity and support overhead have been significantly reduced. Reliability, resilience and observability have improved. Teams have adopted effective modern engineering practices, including appropriate use of intelligent automation and AI-assisted development. Technical decisions are made collaboratively and are actively supported by the teams that own and operate the technology. Role Summary A hands-on Principal Engineer who works with engineering teams to simplify a complex Store Operations platform, improve engineering effectiveness, and introduce modern software engineering practices through technical leadership, collaboration and software delivery. The role will identify strategic CGT opportunities, understand customers scientific, process-development and manufacturing workflows, and bring together capabilities from across Thermo Fisher Scientific to create differentiated, end-to-end solutions. A critical aspect of this role is the ability to influence without direct authority . The incumbent will work across multiple businesses, commercial teams, product specialists, application scientists, marketing, service and other functions to create alignment around customer opportunities and mobilize the right capabilities to win. The role will act as a CGT workflow orchestrator , moving customer engagement beyond individual products toward integrated solutions spanning research, process development, clinical translation and commercial manufacturing. Key Responsibilities CGT Workflow Selling & Business Growth Develop and execute the commercial strategy for growing Thermo Fisher Scientific s Cell & Gene Therapy business across assigned markets and strategic customers. Identify and develop high-value opportunities where multiple Thermo Fisher businesses can participate in the customer workflow. Build a strong pipeline of integrated CGT workflow opportunities rather than relying primarily on individual product opportunities. Understand customer programs from early research and process development through clinical translation, scale-up and commercial manufacturing to identify opportunities across the workflow. Connect relevant capabilities across cell biology, cell culture, cell processing, gene editing, viral vector and plasmid workflows, bioprocessing, analytical technologies, instruments, consumables, reagents and services . Translate customer scientific and manufacturing challenges into integrated Thermo Fisher value propositions. Drive penetration and share of wallet within strategic CGT customers through broader workflow adoption. Maintain strong commercial discipline around pipeline development, opportunity progression, forecasting and execution. One Thermo Fisher - Cross-Business Leadership Serve as the commercial integrator for CGT opportunities across Thermo Fisher Scientific businesses . Bring together Business Units, commercial teams, Technical Sales Specialists, Application Scientists, Product Management, Marketing, Service and other relevant stakeholders around priority CGT opportunities. Establish a clear opportunity strategy and define how different businesses can collectively address the customer s workflow. Create alignment across businesses on customer priorities, value propositions, engagement strategy and execution. Identify gaps or overlaps between businesses and facilitate decisions that enable a coordinated One Thermo Fisher approach. Act as the internal voice of the CGT customer, ensuring customer workflow requirements and emerging needs are understood across relevant businesses. Influence Without Authority Success in this role will depend heavily on the ability to lead through influence rather than organizational authority . The incumbent will: Build credibility and trusted relationships with commercial and business leaders across Thermo Fisher Scientific. Influence Business Units and sales teams to collaborate on opportunities that span organizational boundaries. Create alignment among stakeholders who may have different priorities, objectives and reporting structures. Mobilize resources across businesses without necessarily having direct control over those resources. Establish shared objectives and mutual accountability around strategic CGT opportunities. Navigate a complex matrix organization and resolve competing priorities through collaboration, data, customer insight and business rationale. Build internal advocacy for CGT opportunities and secure commitment from relevant stakeholders. Facilitate decisions and maintain momentum across complex opportunities involving multiple internal and customer stakeholders. Lead complex, high-value opportunities involving multiple Thermo Fisher businesses and multiple customer stakeholders. Conduct strategic business reviews and workflow discussions with key customers. Support scientific forums, workshops, seminars, roundtables and customer innovation discussions that strengthen Thermo Fisher Scientific s position within the CGT ecosystem. Proven record of building alignment and driving execution across multiple businesses and functions. Workflow & Solution Selling Ability to understand complex customer workflows and connect multiple Thermo Fisher capabilities into differentiated customer solutions. jobs.description:
Experience range: 10-15 Yrs
Work Schedule Standard (Mon-Fri) Environmental Conditions Office Job Description JOB DESCRIPTION: Sr Business Analyst - Product Owner At Thermo Fisher Scientific, we develop innovative software solutions that enable our customers to advance science and improve human health. It is a close-knit, collaborative, cross-functional environment where Product Management, Software Engineering, Software Verification & Validation, Quality, and other functions work together to deliver high-quality products. The software team is tasked with applying industry best practices to the definition, design, development, verification, validation, and delivery of world-class software products for clinical and research settings. We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Sr Business Analyst - Product Owner who will serve as the primary liaison between the Product Management team and the Software Engineering and Software V&V teams. This individual will translate product and customer needs into clear, complete, testable, and implementation-ready requirements and user stories so that Development and V&V teams have a common understanding of intended product behavior. The Product Owner will act as the single point of contact for functional understanding of the product and will own the quality and completeness of requirements throughout the software development lifecycle. You are excited and passionate about participating in an Agile/SCRUM setting to meet customer expectations and continuously drive quality and delivery improvements. You are comfortable working with technical and business stakeholders, facilitating decisions, identifying gaps, and constructively challenging assumptions. You do not stop at identifying problems; you develop practical proposals, build cross-functional alignment, drive actions to closure, and use meaningful metrics to demonstrate measurable improvement in requirement quality, defect prevention, and product delivery. Essential Functions: Serve as the primary liaison between Product Management, Software Engineering, and Software V&V, ensuring a common understanding of product requirements, workflows, priorities, and expected system behavior. Translate product requirements, customer needs, business objectives, scientific workflows, and regulatory considerations into clear Epics, Features, User Stories, and Acceptance Criteria that can be independently understood and executed by Software Development and V&V teams. Own the functional quality and completeness of software requirements throughout the product development lifecycle and ensure requirements are clear, consistent, testable, traceable, and sufficiently detailed before implementation begins. Ensure user stories capture the business and user objective, functional behavior, user workflows and use cases, business rules, acceptance criteria, positive and negative scenarios, boundary and exception conditions, dependencies, assumptions, data and integration considerations, and expected behavior required for verification and validation. Establish and drive effective requirements review and backlog refinement mechanisms so that Product Management, Engineering, V&V, and other relevant stakeholders have a shared understanding of scope and expected behavior before development begins. Drive adoption and continuous improvement of Definition of Ready, requirement quality standards, story templates, review checklists, traceability practices, and other mechanisms that improve requirement completeness and reduce downstream ambiguity and rework. Act as the single point of contact for functional interpretation and clarification of product requirements for Software Engineering and V&V teams. Maintain an end-to-end understanding of product workflows and proactively identify gaps, inconsistencies, dependencies, and unintended interactions across features. Ensure key product decisions, requirement clarifications, assumptions, changes, and impact assessments are documented and communicated to affected stakeholders, including impacts to existing functionality, development, V&V, documentation, timelines, and related product components. Drive processes and preventive actions that reduce defects whose root cause is attributed to Requirement Miss, incomplete or ambiguous requirements, inadequate acceptance criteria, or inconsistent functional interpretation. Play a leadership role in software defect triage, partnering with Product Management, Engineering, and V&V to establish expected system behavior and distinguish among software implementation defects, requirement misses or ambiguities, test coverage gaps, change requests or enhancements, and expected product behavior. Ensure defect triage results in clear decisions, owners, actions, and closure criteria, and drive timely resolution of product and functional questions that could otherwise block Software Development or V&V execution. Analyze requirement-related defects and defect trends to identify systemic patterns and recurring gaps. Partner with Engineering, V&V, and Product Management leaders to define corrective and preventive actions and drive those actions through completion. Establish and monitor meaningful quality and delivery metrics, including Requirement Miss defects, requirement-related defect escape rate, user-story rework after development begins, story readiness, acceptance-criteria completeness, requirement churn, defect recurrence, triage aging, corrective-action completion, and reduction in Development and V&V rework. Use metrics not only for reporting but to identify systemic issues, prioritize improvement opportunities, demonstrate the effectiveness of corrective actions, and show measurable improvement across releases or program increments. Work effectively with senior leadership and cross-functional teams, influence without direct authority, facilitate difficult discussions, create alignment among stakeholders with different priorities, and drive decisions and actions to closure. Demonstrate a strong ownership mindset, team spirit, and proactive approach to process and delivery improvement. Raise gaps early and pair identified issues with practical recommendations, proposals, or solution options rather than limiting the role to escalation or issue identification. Mentor and guide team members in effective requirements development, user-story creation, functional analysis, defect triage, and product-development practices, promoting shared accountability for product quality and delivery across Product Management, Engineering, and V&V. jobs.description: You will drive an automation-first operating model , turning recurring operational tasks into reliable, reusable software and workflows. This role combines independent technical ownership, production reliability, and collaboration across development, infrastructure, security, and cloud service teams. Develop self-service capabilities for environment provisioning, service onboarding, deployment, configuration, health validation, and troubleshooting. Automate NonProduction environment lifecycle activities, including provisioning, upgrades, configuration synchronization, drift detection, and cleanup. Support designated NonProduction platforms, investigate recurring issues, and turn support findings into durable tooling and framework improvements. Partner with developers, QA, release engineering, SRE, and security teams to identify friction and prioritize improvements. Evaluate echnical tradeoffs across reliability, performance, scalability, security, cost, and operational complexity; document design decisions and recommend solutions aligned with service objectives and delivery needs. Participate in the scheduled oncall rotation and support Production environments, including after-hours coverage; triage alerts, respond to incidents, coordinate escalations, restore service, and ensure clear handovers and follow-up actions. Experience implementing observability using metrics, logs, dashboards, or distributed tracing. Strong troubleshooting skills across application dependencies, Kubernetes, infrastructure, and networking fundamentals. Demonstrated ability to identify developer friction or repetitive support work and address it through automation or self-service capabilities. Practical experience using AI-assisted development tools, including reviewing generated code and validating results. Ability to independently deliver well-scoped projects and collaborate effectively with users of the platform. Experience building internal developer platforms, portals, command-line tools, or workflow frameworks. Familiarity with Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, centralized logging, and telemetry correlation. Experience with environment metadata, configuration drift analysis, feature-flag tooling, artifact/BOM management, or deployment comparison. Experience building AI-assisted diagnostic tools, retrieval-based knowledge systems, or agents integrated with operational APIs. Familiarity with agent evaluation, permission boundaries, human approval workflows, and safe tool execution. Experience with event-driven automation, asynchronous workflows, idempotency, retries, and partial-failure recovery. Experience supporting shared development and test environments with multiple teams or tenants. Experience measuring developer productivity and using adoption, reliability, and support data to guide improvements. Familiarity with NonProduction cloud cost optimization and resource lifecycle management.

Key Responsibilities Own end-to-end verification strategy, planning, and closure for one or more complex IPs/subsystems. Architect and review UVM-based verification environments, ensuring reusability and scalability across projects. Drive functional and code coverage closure; define coverage models and identify verification gaps early in the cycle. Lead protocol-level verification efforts (e.g., I3C, MIPI, AMBA), including VIP evaluation, integration, and debug. Mentor and technically guide junior verification engineers; support their ramp-up on tools, methodology, and protocols. Required Skills Bachelor's/Master's degree in Electronics, Electrical, or Computer Engineering (VLSI specialization preferred). 5-7 years of experience in digital design/IP verification, with demonstrated ownership of verification closure for at least one complex IP or subsystem. Strong expertise in System Verilog and UVM methodology — testbench architecture, sequences, scoreboards, and reference models. Proven experience with functional coverage, code coverage, and assertion-based verification (SVA); ability to define coverage models from specification. Hands-on experience with industry-standard simulation tools (VCS, Xcelium, or Questa) and debug tools. Experience with formal verification tools and methodology (e.g., JasperGold) for FSM, connectivity, or control-logic verification. Solid understanding of one or more protocols such as I3C, I2C, SPI, AMBA,MIPI-CSI, or similar interconnect/interface standards, including VIP-based verification. Strong scripting skills (Python, Perl, or TCL) for automation, flow development, and regression management. Ability to read and interpret design specifications, RTL, and identify verification risk areas independently. Preferred / Good to Have Experience mentoring or technically leading a small team of verification engineers. Exposure to mutation testing or other coverage-quality assessment techniques. Familiarity with low-power verification (UPF/CPF) and Gate Level simulations. Experience working with EDA vendors (e.g., Cadence, Synopsys) for tool/methodology support and issue resolution. Prior contribution to internal verification methodology documents, guidelines, or reusable verification IP (VIP) development. Experience working in a globally distributed team environment. Soft Skills Strong technical leadership and mentoring ability. Excellent problem-solving and debugging skills, with the ability to work through ambiguous or under-specified requirements. Strong written and verbal communication skills — able to present technical status and risk clearly to management. Ownership mindset with the ability to work independently and drive closure under deadlines. Collaborative approach to working with design, architecture, and cross-functional teams. Exposure to AI/ML assisted verification techniques to improve verification productivity and efficiency. What We Offer A technical leadership track with visibility into IP-level and subsystem-level verification strategy. Opportunity to shape verification methodology, including formal and protocol verification practices. Mentorship and people-development opportunities within a growing team. Exposure to advanced verification domains including formal verification and next-generation Security IP and systems. Collaborative, cross-functional work environment with global teams. way that helps the engineer see it too You manage multiple projects without losing track of details, and your team knows you will catch issues before they escalate to the customer or senior management jobs.title: Vulnerability Management Analyst — Semiconductor IP
jobs.description: Date posted 10/11/2026 Category Engineering Hire Type Employee Job ID 19196 Remote Eligible No Date Posted 10/11/2026 Vulnerability Management Analyst - Semiconductor IP We Are: At Synopsys, we drive the innovations that shape the way we live and connect. Our technology is central to the Era of Pervasive Intelligence, from self-driving cars to learning machines. We lead in chip design, verification, and IP integration, empowering the creation of high-performance silicon chips and software content. Join us to transform the future through continuous technological innovation. You Are: You are someone who builds trust with product and engineering teams when the topic is risk. You listen first, explain complex findings in clear language, and own your conclusions. You help people understand what a vulnerability means for their work and what they should do next. You are practical when information is incomplete. You stay focused on timely action, challenge unclear choices in a respectful way, and keep looking for better ways to reduce risk. You care about teamwork, follow-through, and leaving guidance that others can use. This is a full-time role. What You’ll Be Doing: Analyze vulnerabilities affecting semiconductor IP products, firmware, and related interfaces, and determine residual risk with clear assumptions. Prioritize findings so product teams can act in a timely way: severity, exploitability, affected assets, and recommended mitigations. Work with design, verification, firmware, and product teams to explain vulnerabilities, walk through impact, and agree how the team will mitigate. Advise those teams on practical mitigations, compensating controls, and verification or test evidence that shows the risk is reduced. Work in semiconductor IP development and associated test flows, using the tools those teams use to design, verify, and test IP, so analysis matches how the product is actually built. Build and maintain your own analysis, intake, scoring, and reporting tools, including in Python, when existing tools are not enough. Scripts and tools should be readable and usable by other analysts. Track open risk through the cybersecurity lifecycle, from intake through analysis, treatment, verification, and internal release decisions, and keep status current. Facilitate working sessions so similar IP classes get consistent analysis, risk language, and mitigation guidance. Look for new and practical ways to detect, assess, and mitigate risk, including improved methods, automation, and lessons from prior findings. Use agentic workflows (AI agents, structured prompts, and human-in-the-loop review) to speed research and first drafts without handing off ownership of risk conclusions. Run the job in Jira, Confluence, Git, and GitLab: track vulnerability and risk work, keep documentation current, and version work products through review. The Impact You Will Have: Give product teams vulnerability analysis and risk determinations they can trust and act on without re-deriving the work. Reduce time-to-mitigation by explaining findings clearly and agreeing practical next steps with the teams that own the product. Leave mitigation and test guidance that design, verification, and firmware teams can execute. Keep residual risk visible and current so internal release and treatment decisions are based on evidence, not stale status. Improve consistency of vulnerability handling and risk language across similar IP classes. Raise the quality of risk reduction over time by bringing new methods, better mitigations, and fit-for-purpose tools into the workflow. What You’ll Need: Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. An advanced degree is welcome, not required. Typically 3 or more years in vulnerability management, product cybersecurity, embedded security, or a closely related engineering role. Stronger evidence on vulnerability analysis and risk determination can offset fewer years. Title (Analyst or Senior Analyst) will match demonstrated depth. Strong practical experience in vulnerability analysis on real products, not only scanning or training exercises. Ability to determine risk: severity, exploitability, affected assets, likelihood, impact, and residual risk after proposed mitigations. Ability to explain vulnerabilities and recommended mitigations to engineering teams so they can act in a timelyway. Working familiarity with semiconductor IP development and associated testing, including the tools used to design, verify, and test IP. Specific commercial tool names are not required. Ability to write and maintain your own tools, including in Python, for analysis, intake, scoring, and reporting when existing tools are not enough. This is not a software-engineering role. Tools should be readable and usable by other analysts. Experience working with incomplete information and stating assumptions when the end-system is not fully known. Experience ing a cybersecurity lifecycle across planning, design, implementation, verification, and internal release, including tracking open risk to closure. Hands-on understanding of embedded systems enough to reason about hardware-rooted and firmware vulnerabilities: SoC or MCU integration, firmware, interfaces, registers, boot and debug, and interconnects. Experience delivering analysis inside product-team cadence, including re-prioritizing when new findings or design changes arrive. Practical experience using AI agents and agentic workflows to speed research, drafting, and repetitive analysis, while keeping the human as owner of technical conclusions. Hands-on use of Jira, Confluence, Git, and GitLab (or an equivalent Git forge) for tickets, documentation, and review. jobs.title: Director, Product Management — Core Database Engine & AI
jobs.description: Our Company At Teradata, we believe that people thrive when empowered with better information. Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform activates enterprise intelligence by unifying data, knowledge and business context to achieve tangible outcomes. With Teradata, organizations can provide agents with full context for impact when it matters. Our solution lets businesses connect and scale on premises, in the cloud, or through a hybrid approach. Teradata delivers real business value with AI. What You'll Do In this role, you will lead product strategy and execution for Teradata's core database engine: the massively parallel query engine behind every workload on the platform. You will shape the roadmap across the optimizer, execution runtime, workload management, and Global Planner, and own how the engine performs on native storage, cloud object storage, and open table formats such as Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake. This role sits at the intersection of the database engine and AI. AI agents are becoming the dominant consumers of enterprise data, issuing high volumes of exploratory, speculative queries, while GenAI and machine learning can improve the engine from the inside. Every core component needs to be rethought in this light, and you will lead that rethink and turn it into a roadmap engineering can build. Two things anchor the role. Performance: you will spend significant time inside real workloads, query plans, and benchmarks, working with engineering to deliver measurable gains release after release. SQL: you will be the steward of Teradata SQL, the surface customers live in, making its syntax, semantics, and ergonomics simpler, more expressive, and safer for developers, analysts, and AI agents. Strategy: Own the engine vision and multi-year roadmap, co-owning architecture direction with senior engineering leaders and making principled trade-offs across performance, cost, and complexity. AI and agents: Lead the rethink of every core engine component for AI agents as the new dominant workload, and apply GenAI and ML inside the engine to make it faster and more autonomous. Optimizer, execution, and workload management: Agents send many redundant queries. Explore optimizing across queries, sharing intermediate results, and returning early or approximate answers. Apply learned cardinality and cost models and LLM-assisted rewrite, with guardrails that protect plan stability. Define how workload management absorbs bursty machine traffic through agent identity, priorities, and budgets. Performance: Work hands-on with engineering on query plans, regressions, and bottlenecks. Own the benchmark suite and KPIs (latency, concurrency, plan stability, price-performance), including agentic workloads, and build regression gates into releases. Open Table formats: Own the engine side of Iceberg and Delta Lake (scan planning, pruning, pushdown, write paths) so customers never trade performance for openness. Automate statistics, clustering, and compaction with AI. SQL language and query interface: Design features that turn complex problems into simple, readable queries, reduce footguns while keeping power and backward compatibility, and stay aligned with ANSI SQL. Make the dialect something agents can safely generate and execute, and let agents steer with cost estimates, plan explanations, and hints. Who You'll Work With You will work with senior database engineering leaders, performance engineering, AI platform teams, the open table format product team, sales engineering, and executive leadership across the US, Europe, and India. This role starts as an individual contributor, leading through technical depth and influence and mentoring Staff-level PMs. It may grow into managing a team of product managers. What Makes You a Qualified Candidate 15+ years in databases, query engines, or distributed data systems, including senior product management or equivalent principal or staff engineering experience Expert understanding of database internals: query planning, cost-based optimization, execution models, and MPP trade-offs Deep SQL expertise: a heavy SQL user (data engineer, analyst, or DBA) with strong opinions on language design, ergonomics, and compatibility A hands-on performance mindset: reading query plans, designing benchmarks, and finding root causes with senior engineers A strong working understanding of LLMs and AI agents, and an informed view on how they change database design and how ML can improve database internals Architecture-level knowledge of Snowflake, Databricks, and ClickHouse, and fluency in lakehouse architecture and open table formats Degree in Computer Science or a related field; an MS or PhD in databases, distributed systems, or ML for systems is a plus What You'll Bring First-principles thinking and good taste: willingness to question long-standing database assumptions, a preference for elegance over verbosity, customer obsession, daily use of GenAI tools, and the credibility to earn the trust of senior engineers The ability to read research critically, separate promise from hype, and design experiments to prove value, with a track record of setting multi-year platform strategy A plus: experience designing SQL features or language extensions, hands-on work with optimizers or learned database components, open-source contributions, or publications at SIGMOD, VLDB, or CIDR Why We Think You'll Love Teradata We prioritize a people-first culture because we know our people are at the very heart of our success. We embrace a flexible work model because we trust our people to make decisions about how, when, and where they work. We focus on well-being because we care about our people and their ability to thrive both personally and professionally. We are an anti-racist company because our dedication to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion is more than a statement. It is a deep commitment to doing the work to foster an equitable environment that celebrates people for all of who they are. #LI-NM1

jobs.description: Our Company: At Teradata, we believe that people thrive when empowered with better information. Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform activates enterprise intelligence by unifying data, knowledge and business context to achieve tangible outcomes. With Teradata, organizations can provide agents with full context for impact when it matters. Our solution lets businesses connect and scale on premises, in the cloud, or through a hybrid approach. Teradata delivers real business value with AI. What You’ll Do We are looking for an exceptional Staff Cloud & AI Platform Engineer to own and independently build a next‑generation enterprise‑scale deployment and orchestration platform. This role goes far beyond traditional CI/CD or infrastructure automation—it sits at the intersection of distributed systems, control‑plane architecture, SRE principles, and applied AI/agentic workflows. Contribute to the design and implementation of a stateful deployment control plane that treats deployments as a continuous convergence problem. Enable safe, resumable, deterministic, and SLO‑governed rollouts across multi‑cloud, on‑prem, and customer environments. Implement the practical application of AI agents in DevOps by embedding intelligent decision‑making into deployment workflows. Apply AI agents for anomaly detection, failure diagnosis, rollout control, and automated mitigation. Ensure all AI‑assisted workflows preserve correctness, determinism, and full auditability. This is a high‑impact individual contributor role requiring deep technical judgment, delivery ownership, and the ability to turn abstract design into production‑grade systems. Key Responsibilities Design and implement a stateful deployment control plane with deterministic, resumable execution and rollback support. Build deployment workflows that reconcile desired vs. actual state using durable control loops. Support multi‑cloud, on‑prem, and customer environments with a single orchestration framework. Implement SLO‑governed promotion gates, error‑budget checks, and bounded retry policies. Enable deployment models including self‑service, wave‑based rollouts, blue‑green, managed updates, and maintenance windows. Define declarative, extensible workflow schemas with explicit dependencies, retries, and rollback semantics. Integrate deployment orchestration with CI/CD systems, artifact manifests, entitlement services, and downstream execution systems. Embed AI‑assisted decision logic into deployment workflows for anomaly detection, failure diagnosis, and rollout control. Ensure AI‑driven actions remain deterministic, auditable, reversible, and policy‑constrained. Develop infrastructure and automation frameworks using Terraform, Python, and cloud‑native services. Embed observability and telemetry into workflows to drive automated validation, retries, and rollback decisions. Provide hands‑on technical leadership, mentoring engineers and driving platform architecture across DevOps, SRE, and CloudOps teams. Who You’ll Work With This is an individual contributor role. You will collaborate with project team members and architects, and report to the Senior Engineering Manager. What Makes You a Qualified Candidate Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science or related field 8+ years of hands‑on experience in DevOps, platform engineering, cloud infrastructure, or distributed systems. Proven experience developing and implementation of stateful systems such as control planes, workflow engines, or orchestration platforms. Experience building or operating enterprise‑scale deployment systems across multi‑cloud, hybrid, or on‑prem environments. Deep expertise in CI/CD, release engineering, and deployment strategies including wave‑based, blue‑green, and managed rollouts. Practical experience applying SRE principles such as SLOs, error budgets, promotion gates, and automated rollback. Strong programming skills in Python, with the ability to build long‑running services and automation frameworks. Hands‑on experience with Infrastructure as Code, preferably Terraform, and cloud‑native services (AWS, Azure, and/or GCP). Experience integrating observability and telemetry (metrics, logs, traces) into automated systems for decision‑making. Demonstrated experience building or integrating AI‑assisted or agentic workflows into DevOps or operational systems. Ability to design safe, auditable, policy‑constrained automation, especially when applying AI or autonomous decision logic. Strong technical judgment and communication skills, with experience leading architecture across teams as an individual contributor. #LI-MP1 Why We Think You’ll Love Teradata We prioritize a people-first culture because we know our people are at the very heart of our success. We embrace a flexible work model because we trust our people to make decisions about how, when, and where they work. We focus on well-being because we care about our people and their ability to thrive both personally and professionally. jobs.title: Senior Mixed Signal DV Engineer
jobs.description: Change the world. Love your job. Texas Instruments is seeking Design Verification Engineer. In this role you will confirm the accuracy of designs for analog and mixed signal electronic parts, components, or integrated circuitry for analog and mixed signal electronic equipment and other hardware systems before pattern generation/mask development. The role will require working independently from the product development team who designed the devices to confirm adherence to known design rules, procedures, and best practices. Additional job functions include analyzing equipment to establish operating data and conducting experimental tests and evaluating results to confirm the device meets all requirements in the specifications. You may also run software simulations, selecting components and equipment based on analysis of specifications and reliability. As a Design Verification Engineer you may also review vendor capability to support product development. Requires a BS degree or equivalent experience in the design of equipment, components or circuitry. Who are we and what do we do? The Advanced Circuits and Power Solutions business is known for delivering industry-leading custom IC system solutions, including display and touch power products, charger power products, camera PMICs, power path devices, sensing devices, and high-performance communication interface products. Our products integrate precision signal chains and highly efficient power components into ultra-small form factors, enabling TI’s best-in-class customers to translate their ideas into high-value products that revolutionize the personal electronics market. In this team, you will work with and learn from incredibly talented technical leaders who have influenced TI’s technology, productivity, and way of working in creative and impactful ways. You will directly interact with one of TI’s most valued, high-volume customers through intense technical reviews and architecture discussions! By enabling designs that are highly impactful to TI revenue and working with a critical customer on a versatile set of products, you will find yourself on an accelerated career path. About the job If you are looking to join an ingenious, vigorous & ambitious team that consistently delivers groundbreaking technologies into the custom mobile electronics world, here is an opportunity for you! What will you be doing in this role? Strategic & Technical Leadership Strategic Leadership: Drive TI's technology roadmap by collaborating with Process, Packaging, EDA, and other key stakeholders both within and outside the company. Industry Influence: Define and implement industry-leading best practices within TI and represent the company's technical leadership in front of key customers. Design Governance: Participate in the critical review and sign-off of designs developed within the team as well as cross-product designs across TI. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Architecture, Design, and Firmware teams to ensure successful product execution. Verification Strategy & Architecture Verification Strategy: Drive the verification strategy by creating detailed test plans, defining test cases, checkers, and coverage metrics. Develop comprehensive, coverage-driven verification plans in close collaboration with System, Application, and Design teams. UVM Architecture: Lead the ground-up development of UVM-based verification environments, including the implementation of agents, drivers, monitors, and scoreboards. Mixed-Signal Methodology: Build and enhance mixed-signal testbenches using a combination of schematics, behavioral models, and RTL. Mixed-Signal & Modeling Expertise Modeling & Simulation: Create high-fidelity analog behavioral models using Verilog-A, Verilog-AMS, Wreal (RNM), or EENet to enable efficient top-level simulation. Analog Checkers & Assertions: Implement real-time analog checkers and post-processing checker strategies to ensure functional correctness across domains. Protocol Expertise: Verify standard communication protocols such as I2C, ASI, SPI, and UART. Execution, Debug, & Support Full-Cycle Execution: Execute RTL and Gate-Level Simulations (GLS), manage regressions, and track functional and code coverage (Block, Expression, Toggle, FSM) to ensure 100% closure through tape-out. Technical Debugging: Utilize advanced debugging and problem-solving skills to resolve complex design and testbench issues. Post-Silicon Support: Collaborate with Product and Application Engineering teams to support ATE functional pattern generation and silicon characterization. Strong command of Cadence Virtuoso, AMS Designer, or equivalent industry-standard mixed-signal simulation and debug environments. Formal Verification (FV): Hands-on experience with Formal Property Verification (FPV), connectivity checks, and Unreachability (UNR) analysis for top-level sign-off. Design and build security controls across layers such as operating systems, container orchestration, CI/CD pipelines, cloud configuration, and network boundaries, to defend against sophisticated adversaries and insider threats. Design new security processes and ways of working, revamping patching cycles and golden-image and base-image refreshes across cloud and on-prem, so the team can move fast without sacrificing safety. Come to the table with ideas: identify where security and remediation processes can be improved, propose better approaches, and turn them into standards the team adopts. Set the technical approach across the full security scope: application and open-source dependency fixes, infrastructure patching, cloud configuration and guardrails, WAF, network isolation, and secrets and machine-identity management. Prioritize by risk in line with industry best practice such as CISA guidance (CISA KEV, CVSS/EPSS, and SLA-driven burndown), and champion adoption of AI-augmented security tooling, including SAST and SCA. Raise the technical bar by reviewing fixes and mentoring engineers, and coordinate with the wider security team across regions to keep standards and priorities aligned across time zones. Own clear reporting and metrics, and build the runbooks, standards, and escalation paths that make security a repeatable, auditable capability. A deep understanding of security principles, common vulnerabilities, and best practice across application, cloud, and infrastructure layers. A working command of vulnerability management at scale: prioritization frameworks, CVSS/EPSS, CISA KEV, and SLA-driven burndown. Breadth across the security stack: application and dependency vulnerabilities, infrastructure patching, guardrails, WAF, network isolation, and identity and access controls, with multi-cloud experience across two or more of AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI (all four an advantage) alongside on-premises infrastructure. Strong judgment on balancing risk reduction against operational and customer impact. jobs.title: Principal Architect - Databricks
jobs.description: What success looks like in this role: Databricks Platform Architecture Architect enterprise Databricks Lakehouse platforms on Azure, AWS, or GCP — including Unity Catalog, Delta Live Tables (DLT), and Databricks SQL. Design multi-workspace, multi-region Databricks deployments with workspace federation, network isolation (Private Link / V Net injection), and identity federation via Azure AD / Okta / SCIM. Define medallion architecture (Bronze / Silver / Gold) standards, enforcing schema evolution, data contracts, and SLA-tiered pipeline SLOs. Lead migration of legacy data warehouses (Teradata, Netezza, Snowflake, Synapse) to the Databricks Lakehouse — including SQL translation, workload profiling, and TCO modeling. Own cluster architecture decisions: autoscaling policies, instance fleet configurations, job vs. interactive cluster strategies, Photon engine enablement, and cost-per-query optimization. Design and implement Databricks Workflows and Delta Live Tables for mission-critical streaming and batch pipelines, including CDC (Change Data Capture) patterns using Autoloader and Structured Streaming. Data Governance & Security Implement Unity Catalog as the enterprise meta store: fine-grained access control (row/column-level security), lineage tracking, and cross-workspace catalog federation. Define data classification frameworks, PII masking strategies, and dynamic views for regulatory compliance (GDPR, HIPAA, SOX) within the Databricks platform. Architect Delta Sharing for secure, governed cross-organizational data sharing without data movement. Lead data mesh and data product design patterns on Databricks — aligning ownership, SLAs, and discoverability across domains. AI & ML Platform (Databricks ML) Design end-to-end ML platforms using Databricks ML Runtime, ML flow (Tracking, Registry, Projects), and Feature Store for model lifecycle management. Architect LLM / Generative AI workloads on Databricks: RAG pipelines, fine-tuning with Mosaic AI, vector search (Databricks Vector Search), and Model Serving endpoints. Define MLOps frameworks covering CI/CD for models, drift detection, A/B testing, and shadow deployments using ML flow and Databricks Workflows. Integrate Databricks AI/BI (Genie, Dashboards) for self-service analytics and natural language data querying. Stakeholder & Delivery Leadership Lead architecture reviews, technical workshops, and proof-of-concept engagements with C-suite and VP-level client stakeholders. Author solution architecture documents, reference architectures, and RFP/RFI responses for Databricks-led pursuits. Define center-of-excellence (CoE) standards, reusable accelerators, and Databricks best-practice playbooks for the Unisys Data & AI practice. Mentor and upskill a team of data architects and engineers; drive Databricks certification paths across the practice. Partner with Databricks field engineering on joint go-to-market opportunities and co-delivery engagements. #LI-SS1 You will be successful in this role if you have: 12+ years of experience in data architecture, data engineering, or enterprise analytics — with at least 5 years focused on Databricks platform delivery. Databricks Certified Data Engineer Professional or Databricks Certified Associate Developer for Apache Spark — required. Additional Databricks certifications strongly preferred. Expert-level proficiency in Apache Spark (PySpark, Scala Spark) — performance tuning, DAG optimization, shuffle management, and broadcast strategies. Deep hands-on expertise with Delta Lake: ACID transactions, Z-ordering, OPTIMIZE, VACUUM, time travel, and schema enforcement/evolution. Proven production experience with Delta Live Tables (DLT): expectations, quarantine patterns, SCD Type 1/2 in DLT, and pipeline monitoring. Strong Unity Catalog implementation experience: catalog/schema/table hierarchy design, privilege inheritance, service principals, and attribute-based access control. Experience architecting Databricks on at least one major cloud: Azure Databricks (ADLS Gen2, Azure AD), AWS (S3, IAM Instance Profiles, Glue Catalog), or GCP (GCS, Dataproc comparison). Proficiency in infrastructure-as-code for Databricks: Terraform (databricks provider), Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs), and CI/CD integration (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Jenkins). Hands-on MLflow experience: experiment tracking, model registry, model serving, and custom pyfunc models. Strong SQL expertise for Databricks SQL / Photon query optimization, materialized views, and lakehouse serving patterns. Experience with real-time streaming architectures: Kafka + Databricks Structured Streaming, Autoloader, and watermarking strategies. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer(Growth & ML), Hyderabad
jobs.description: Storytelling is, and will always be, the heart of what we do at Skydance. Our vision is to build a thriving entertainment ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced. We create for every age and audience, anchored by the strength of our content and experiences and the depth of our connection with fans. We are creator-first, audience-focused, tech-forward, globally scaled. Here, you’ll work with talented teams that move fast, think boldly and collaborate with purpose to deliver results. We aim high, champion the best ideas and win together, earning the trust of our employees, creators, partners and audiences every day. If you’re energized by the opportunity to help build the next-generation global media and entertainment company powered by creativity and technology, we’d be thrilled to welcome you aboard. LET’S GO! ㅤ Senior Machine Learning Engineer (Growth & ML), Hyderabad Meet our Team Our Data & Audience Platform organization builds advanced AI/ML solutions that power identity, audience intelligence, advertising, and personalization at scale. Our Machine Learning Engineering team in Hyderabad develops foundational AI/ML capabilities that transform first-party data signals into production-ready machine learning systems. These solutions help expand addressable audiences, improve targeting and measurement, forecast demand, and personalize content discovery — driving advertising yield, marketing efficiency, user engagement, and retention. Our Machine Learning Engineers combine strong data science expertise with hands-on engineering capabilities to take models from development to production. This includes building production-grade ML data pipelines, model training and optimization, and scalable ML infrastructure such as feature stores, training and serving pipelines, and MLOps frameworks. We primarily leverage Databricks, along with Snowflake and AWS, and actively embrace emerging technologies, including agentic AI development workflows, to build reliable, scalable, and intelligent machine learning solutions. About the Role As a Senior MLE, you will own the design and delivery of production ML systems that directly impact audience targeting, advertising revenue, subscriber engagement, and retention across our global portfolio. You will lead technical execution on key workstreams — including probabilistic identity resolution, lookalike modeling, single-title affinity, and forecasting — while mentoring MLE 2s and collaborating closely with Staff MLEs and product stakeholders. This is a high-ownership role for engineers with roughly 5–8 years of experience who can independently drive a project from problem framing through production deployment and monitoring. Roles & Responsibilities: ML System Design & Ownership Lead end-to-end development of production ML systems: data sourcing, feature engineering, model training, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring. Own key ML products such as probabilistic identity resolution (matching unauthenticated device IDs and 1P cookies to households/persons with calibrated confidence), single-title affinity (e.g., STAT two-tower retrieval), and audience/propensity models. Design scalable feature pipelines on Databricks (PySpark, Delta, Workflows/DLT, Unity Catalog) and the feature store, with documented feature contracts, backfill paths, and freshness SLAs. Architect batch and near-real-time inference pipelines integrated with Snowflake and activation systems (Mosaic, FreeWheel, GAM). Modeling & Experimentation Develop and optimize models across the ML spectrum: gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM), embedding/two-tower retrieval, neural ranking, probability calibration (e.g., isotonic regression), and probabilistic/graph-based matching. Design rigorous offline and online experiments; define evaluation frameworks (precision/recall, AUC-ROC, NDCG, decile lift, calibration curves) appropriate to each use case. Apply causal-inference techniques (propensity scoring, uplift/incrementality modeling) to measure true lift of audience targeting on engagement and retention KPIs. Contribute to lookalike modeling (LAL 2.0+) using 1,000+ first- and third-party features, including privacy-safe builds inside Data Clean Rooms (Snowflake DCR). MLOps & Infrastructure Champion MLOps best practices: model versioning, champion/challenger promotion, automated retraining triggers, drift detection, and production monitoring with MLflow on Databricks. Build and maintain robust, reproducible, auditable ML pipelines on Databricks (and AWS SageMaker where appropriate, e.g., the identity-resolution track); enforce leakage prevention and training/serving consistency. Contribute to the team’s feature-store strategy — feature contracts, backfills, and freshness SLAs — and implement data-quality checks, model-health dashboards, and alerting thresholds. Embed FinOps cost discipline (compute caps, auto-termination, job tagging) into pipeline design. Mentorship & Cross-functional Collaboration Mentor MLE 2s through code reviews, design discussions, and pairing; contribute to team technical standards. Partner with Product, Marketing, and Ad Sales to translate business requirements into ML problem formulations, and with Data Engineering on data contracts and pipeline SLAs. Communicate model performance, trade-offs, and business impact clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Flagship Projects You’ll Work On Identity Intelligence — foundational, privacy-safe identity across all brands: probabilistic ID resolution that resolves unauthenticated signals to households/persons with calibrated confidence (entity resolution with gradient boosting and embeddings, representation learning, isotonic calibration, candidate blocking, champion/challenger pipelines), expanding addressable audiences beyond deterministic matching. Audience Intelligence — advertising and marketing use cases: lookalike and predictive audiences (LAL across 1,000+ features), ML-driven smart audiences, layered retrieval + propensity, and incrementality/closed-loop optimization, with privacy-safe activation including data clean rooms. ML-based Forecasting — audience growth, demand, and advertising yield/pricing forecasting that powers ad sales and marketing decisions. Content Preferences & Affinity — genre-preference, content-preference, and single-title affinity modeling (two-tower retrieval with semantic content embeddings) that ranks audiences for upcoming titles and powers cross-channel promotion. What You’ll Bring Required 5–8 years of industry experience in ML engineering or applied data science (3+ years with a Ph.D.). Deep Python expertise and production-quality software engineering practices; production experience building and deploying ML at scale (millions+ of users/records). Strong proficiency in Databricks (PySpark, Delta Lake, Workflows/DLT, MLflow, Unity Catalog) and solid SQL/Snowflake experience for feature sourcing and model-output delivery. Experience with AWS ML services (SageMaker, S3, Lambda). Strong understanding of ML model evaluation, A/B testing, and statistical inference; knowledge in one or more of recommendations & ranking, identity resolution, embeddings/retrieval, causal/interpretable ML, forecasting, bandits, or optimization. Demonstrated ability to lead technical decisions and mentor engineers. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering, or a related quantitative field (or equivalent experience). Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to advocate technical solutions to engineers, scientists, and product stakeholders. Preferred: Recommendation systems, personalization, identity resolution, or audience modeling in a media / streaming / ad-tech context. Familiarity with Data Clean Room environments (Snowflake DCR, AWS Clean Rooms) and consent-aware activation. Experience with two-tower / retrieval architectures, probabilistic identity resolution (graph-based matching, entity resolution), and probability calibration. Hands-on experience with agentic AI frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, MCP), Databricks Genie Space configuration, and Snowflake Cortex. Experience with feature stores (Databricks Feature Store, Tecton, Feast) and contributions to open source or ML publications. What We Offer: A Great Place to work Equal opportunity employer Fast track growth opportunities About Skydance Skydance is a next-generation global media and entertainment company, comprised of three business segments: Studios, Direct-to-Consumer, and TV Media. Skydance's portfolio unites legendary brands, including Paramount, Warner Bros., HBO and HBO Max, Paramount+, Pluto TV, CBS, CNN, CBS Sports, TNT Sports, Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, MTV, Food Network, BET, HGTV, and Comedy Central.
